Suppose Θ : H^{Np} → Z̄_p satisfies Θ(Q_ℓ(X)) = det(1 − X r(Frob_ℓ)) for all ℓ ∉ S, and Θ reduces to Θ_m. Then (r̄)^{ss} ≅ ρ̄, by the Chebotarev density theorem and the Brauer–Nesbitt theorem. In particular, if r is reducible then ρ̄ is not absolutely irreducible. If only the traces Θ(T_{ℓ,2}) = tr r(Frob_ℓ) are known to agree, the same conclusion holds when p > 4.
items.note: This follows the CG20 precedent (ext-brauer-nesbitt: planned R01.1, R01.5). AUDIT-31 on R01.5 says 'Tau Ceti has the Frobenius prime sets ... but not the density theorem ... Brauer-Nesbitt is absent'. Only infrastructure is in the library, e.g. tauceti:NumberField.Chebotarev.frobeniusPrimeSet. The trace-only variant for p > 4 is the small-characteristic caveat R01.5 names. Applying the item to Θ through Q_ℓ(X) needs the missing GSp4 Hecke polynomial. External input: Chebotarev density theorem; Brauer–Nesbitt theorem (standard, invoked without citation)

items.name: Arthur's classification of the discrete spectrum of GSp4 (as used)
items.statement: As used: every discrete automorphic representation of GSp4(A) lies in a global Arthur packet Π_ψ of one of six types ([1], classification theorem on p. 78): (a) general ('generic') type, where ψ is a cuspidal automorphic representation of GL4 of symplectic type; (b) Yoshida type; (c) Soudry type; (d) Saito–Kurokawa type; (e) Howe–Piatetski-Shapiro type; (f) one-dimensional type. If Π is of general type, ψ is stable (trivial global component group), the archimedean packet Π_∞ is the L-packet of the archimedean parameter, and every element of Π = ⊗_v Π_v occurs in the discrete spectrum with multiplicity one. If Π is of Yoshida or Saito–Kurokawa type, its Hecke eigenvalues at unramified primes are those of a reducible 4-dimensional Galois representation: a sum of those attached to GL2 forms, resp. GL2 and GL1 forms.
items.note: This follows CG20's conservative reading (ext-arthur-gsp4-classification: missing, source ML.4). ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions:ML.4 ('Give Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs explicit proof-source owners: ... packets, multiplicities') names the sources 'NEWTON-THORNE, ARTHUR-MOK, EXISTING'. Arthur's GSp(4) announcement [1] and its proof by Gee–Taïbi (J. Éc. polytech. Math. 6, 2019) are not among them. The author version does not cite Gee–Taïbi; searching the reference list for 'Taïbi' finds nothing. The introduction (§1, p. 6) also announces this use: Part IV proves that the Euler characteristic of a non-Eisenstein localisation of M vanishes 'by using results of Arthur on the theory of automorphic forms'. External input: J. Arthur [1], Automorphic representations of GSp(4), in Contributions to Automorphic Forms, Geometry, and Number Theory, Johns Hopkins Univ. Press (2004), classification theorem on p. 78 (an announcement); proved by T. Gee and O. Taïbi, Arthur's multiplicity formula for GSp4 and restriction to Sp4, J. Éc. polytech. Math. 6 (2019)

items.name: The archimedean L-packet {π(λ)^g, π(λ)^h}
items.statement: For λ = (λ1, 0; c) with λ1 < 0, the archimedean L-packet of GSp4(R) containing π(λ)^h is {π(λ)^g, π(λ)^h}.
items.note: Archimedean L-packets of GSp4(R) with a limit-of-discrete-series member are planned nowhere. CG20 marked the same packet {π(λ,C0), π(λ,C1)} missing (ext-mok-archimedean-packet) and routed it to ML.4, and archimedean local Langlands for GSp4(R) is also missing there (ext-sorensen-transfer-infinitesimal-character). External input: D. Blasius, M. Harris, D. Ramakrishnan [4], Duke Math. J. 73 (1994), Prop. 5.3.7

items.name: Packets with archimedean component π(λ)^h are of general, Yoshida or Saito–Kurokawa type
items.statement: Let Π be the global Arthur packet of a discrete automorphic representation π of GSp4(A) with π∞ ≅ π(λ)^h (λ = (λ1, 0; c), λ1 < 0, a non-degenerate limit of discrete series). Then Π is of general, Yoshida or Saito–Kurokawa type.
items.note: This is a case analysis of Arthur's six GSp4 packet types against the archimedean parameter of π(λ)^h. Its input, Arthur's GSp4 classification, is missing, and no stage plans the result. CG20's analogous exclusion of types (b)–(f) (arthur-classes-b-f-excluded) is also missing. External input: R. Schmidt [68], Packet structure and paramodular forms, Trans. AMS 370 (2018), §§1.1–1.2, compared with the archimedean parameters of π(λ)^h in R. Schmidt [67], Archimedean aspects of Siegel modular forms of degree 2, Rocky Mountain J. Math. 47 (2017), p. 11

items.name: Proposition 15.2.4.1: h/g symmetry and multiplicity one for non-Eisenstein πf
items.statement: Let ρ̄ be absolutely irreducible and m as above. Let πf be an admissible irreducible representation of GSp4(A_f) that is unramified at every prime ℓ ∤ Np, and let Θ_{πf} : H^{Np} → Q̄_p be its Hecke character. Assume Θ_{πf} is congruent to Θ_m. Let λ = (λ1, 0; c) ∈ X^*(T) + (2,1;0) with λ1 < 0 (printed: λ1 > 0). Then πf ⊗ π(λ)^h is cuspidal automorphic (equivalently, occurs in the discrete spectrum) if and only if πf ⊗ π(λ)^g is, and in that case the cuspidal multiplicities satisfy m^h(πf) = m^g(πf) = 1.
items.note: This needs Arthur's GSp4 classification, the BHR archimedean packet and Schmidt's packet types (all missing, source ML.4). It also needs reducibility of the Galois representations for Yoshida and Saito–Kurokawa packets, from GL2 forms and characters: R19.1 planned, the packet-level statement missing. It is the same mathematics as CG20's arthur-classes-b-f-excluded, case-a-cuspidal-limit-of-discrete-series and the multiplicity-one part of h1-h0-dimension-equality, which CG20 routed to GSp4NonregularModularityLifting. p. 109 prints 'λ1 > 0' where λ1 < 0 is meant (image checked; the item already records this).

items.name: Specialisation of M_m at weight k is classical Klingen-level ordinary cohomology
items.statement: For every k ≥ 0, in particular for k very large, there are H^{Np}-equivariant quasi-isomorphisms M_{K,m} ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Q_p ≃ fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D))_m ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p ≃ fRΓ(X_{Kli}(p)_K, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D))_m ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p. Their cohomology is concentrated in degrees 0 and 1.
items.note: This combines Theorem 11.3.1(3) with classicality at Klingen level and the H^{Np}-equivariance of both. All of these are the paper's own §§11–13 results (missing, other clusters). Derived base change of perfect complexes is planned (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra:P7), and localisation commutes with it (IHG.2).

items.name: Automorphic description of localised ordinary Klingen-level cohomology in large weight: dim fH⁰ = dim fH¹
items.statement: Let ρ̄ be absolutely irreducible and m as above, k ≥ R − 1 and λ = (−k−1, 0; k+4). After extending scalars along Q̄_p ≃ C, f H⁰(X_{Kli}(p)_K, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D))_m ⊗ Q̄_p ≅ ⊕_{πf} f(πf^{K^p Kli(p)}) ≅ f H¹(X_{Kli}(p)_K, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D))_m ⊗ Q̄_p. The sum runs over the irreducible admissible πf of GSp4(A_f) such that πf ⊗ π(λ)^h is cuspidal automorphic and Θ_{πf} : H^{Np} → C is congruent to Θ_m. The projector f acts on πf^{K^p Kli(p)} through πp^{Kli(p)}. In particular the two cohomology groups have the same dimension.
items.note: This applies Corollary 15.2.3.1 and Proposition 15.2.4.1 (missing) at level K^p Kli(p). f acts on π_p^{Kli(p)} through the Klingen U-operators of §5.1.4–5.1.5 (missing, other clusters), and the equality of dimensions follows from m^h = m^g = 1. Klingen-parahoric fixed vectors are local representation theory, SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups (CG20 routed remark-gsp4-parahoric-oldforms there as a source). The ordinary projector formalism is PadicFamilies:L0a.

items.name: Euler characteristic of a perfect complex is invariant under derived base change
items.statement: Let C be a perfect complex over a noetherian ring Λ and φ : Λ → F a ring homomorphism to a field. Then Σ_i (−1)^i dim_F H^i(C ⊗^L_{Λ,φ} F) equals χ(C) evaluated at the point ker φ ∈ Spec Λ. Hence one specialisation determines χ(C) on the connected component of Spec Λ containing ker φ, and χ(C) = 0 as soon as each connected component contains a specialisation whose alternating sum of dimensions is 0.
items.note: Represent C by a bounded complex P of finite projectives. Then C ⊗^L F = P ⊗ F. Tau Ceti's Euler–Poincaré gives Σ(−1)^i dim H^i(P ⊗ F) = Σ(−1)^i dim(P^i ⊗ F), and rankAtStalk_eq and rankAtStalk_baseChange identify this with χ(C) at ker φ. Constancy on components follows from local constancy. The only piece missing from the libraries is perfect complexes (P7; AUDIT-17: absent). The paper uses this step implicitly (§15.2.5, p. 109). External input: Standard commutative algebra (not cited)

items.name: Short exact sequence of complexes relating the Hasse–Witt maps of G and G^D (proof of Lemma 6.3.3.1)
items.statement: Let G be a BT_1 over an F_p-scheme S and 𝓔 = Ext^1_cris(G, O_{S/F_p})_S, with Hodge filtration 0 → ω_G → 𝓔 → ω^∨_{G^D} → 0. As in Fargues [21], p. 915, there is a short exact sequence of complexes, the complexes being the rows: [ω_G →V⋆ ω_G^{(p)}] → [(ω^∨_{G^D})^{(p)} →F⋆ 𝓔 →V⋆ ω_G^{(p)}] → [(ω^∨_{G^D})^{(p)} →F⋆ ω^∨_{G^D}]. Here F⋆: (ω^∨_{G^D})^{(p)} → ω^∨_{G^D} is the dual of the Hasse–Witt map V⋆: ω_{G^D} → ω^{(p)}_{G^D}. The paper takes the long exact cohomology sequence, which implicitly uses that the middle row is exact. This relates the kernel and cokernel of V⋆_G to those of V⋆_{G^D}, so V⋆_{G^D} has rank one when V⋆_G does.
items.note:
Keep, but state it in general form as an external input from Dieudonné theory. Let G be a BT_1 over an F_p-scheme S. Then 𝓔 = Ext^1_cris(G, O_{S/F_p})_S is locally free, with Hodge filtration 0 → ω_G → 𝓔 → ω^∨_{G^D} → 0. The maps F⋆: 𝓔^(p) → 𝓔 and V⋆: 𝓔 → 𝓔^(p) satisfy Ker F⋆ = ω_G^(p) = Im V⋆ and Ker V⋆ = Im F⋆. Hence the three rows of the p. 31 diagram form a short exact sequence of complexes, and its middle row (ω^∨_{G^D})^(p) → 𝓔 → ω_G^(p) is exact. The paper cites only 'As in [21], p. 915'; hasse-witt-rank-one-for-dual lists that source as external. The proof then says 'Taking the long exact sequence in cohomology' (p. 32, image checked), which silently needs the middle row to be exact. With that exactness, Ker F⋆ ≅ Ker V⋆_G and Coker F⋆ ≅ Coker V⋆_G, which gives the rank-one conclusion. I checked on p. 32 (diagram 6.3.A) that F⋆ kills ω_G^(p) and that V⋆ lands in ω_G^(p). No existing item defines 𝓔, although hasse-invariant-Ha-prime-of-Goo, hasse-witt-rank-one-for-dual and maps-VH-W-Z all use it. The same exactness makes Z (Lemma 6.3.3.4 ff.) an isomorphism, as the proof of section-A-regular-vanishing-locus needs.
Library: none. library-coverage says 'p-divisible (Barsotti–Tate) groups do not exist in either library, and neither does Dieudonné theory of finite flat or p-divisible groups'.
Not planned. FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.2 plans 'Dieudonné modules over perfect residue fields ... Include Frobenius/Verschiebung'. CrystallineCohomology:CR.7 exports crystals 'to R07's Dieudonne crystal and Grothendieck–Messing construction'. Neither states the Dieudonné crystal of a BT_1 over an arbitrary F_p-scheme with its Hodge filtration and the exactness of F⋆ and V⋆.

items.name: Fibres of p_1 : X_Kli(p)_1 → X_1 over the p-rank 0 locus (footnote 11)
items.statement: The p-rank 0 locus X_1^{=0} has dimension 1. The map p_1 is bijective over the dense open subscheme of X_1^{=0} of abelian surfaces not isomorphic to a product of supersingular elliptic curves. Over the finite set SS of superspecial points of X_1^{=0} (abelian surfaces isomorphic to a product of supersingular elliptic curves), p_1 is a P^1-fibration. Stated without proof.
items.note:
Footnote 11 (p. 48, image checked) reads: 'The p-rank 0 locus X_1^{=0} is of dimension 1 and the map p_1 is bijective over the dense open subscheme of X_1^{=0} parametrizing abelian surfaces which are not isomorphic to a product of supersingular elliptic curves. On the other hand, the map p_1 is a P^1-fibration over the finite set of superspecial points SS of X_1^{=0}.' It is the only justification the paper gives for 'the p-rank 0 locus has codimension 1' in the proof of Lemma 7.4.2.5. Lemma 7.4.2.5 feeds the Ha′ exact sequences, Proposition 7.4.2.2 and §8. The footnote is stated without proof, but it is correct:
- A p-rank-0 abelian surface A over an algebraically closed field is supersingular.
- Its subgroups of order p are copies of α_p, parametrized by P(Hom(α_p, A)), which has dimension a(A) − 1.
- a(A) = 1 off SS (one subgroup) and a(A) = 2 on SS (a P^1).
The dimension 1 agrees with p-rank-strata-density-dimension (corrected to r + 1). Existing items do not cover this fibre description:
- lemma-7-4-2-5-second-Hasse-nonzerodivisor lists footnote 11 in its locator but does not state it.
- setup-klingen-paramodular-correspondence says only that p_1 is not quasi-finite over X_1^{=0}.
Neither library has the Klingen-level model, p-divisible groups or a-numbers (library-coverage: 'p-divisible (Barsotti–Tate) groups do not exist in either library'). No stage plans the Klingen model; klingen-level-siegel-threefold is missing.

items.name: p_1 is finite flat away from the p-rank 0 locus and the boundary; Ĉ → B̂ is finite flat
items.statement: The map p_1 : X_Kli(p) → X is finite flat away from the p-rank 0 locus and the boundary, so the cohomological correspondence can be base changed to an arbitrary (formal) scheme by §4.2.5. In particular, if Ĉ is the completion of X_Kli(p) along the étale-type component (X_Kli(p)|_{Y_{par,1}^{=1}})^{et} and B̂ the completion along Y_1^{=1}, then p_1 : Ĉ → B̂ is finite flat: B̂ is regular, p_1 is finite (the p-rank 0 locus has been removed) and dominant, and Ĉ is Cohen–Macaulay.
items.locator: §7.4.2, proof of Proposition 7.4.2.1 and footnote 10, p. 46
items.note:
Footnote 10 (p. 46, image checked) reads: 'Since the map p_1 is finite flat away from the p-rank 0 locus and the boundary, it makes sense to base change the cohomological correspondence to an arbitrary (formal) scheme by section 4.2.5.' The proof of Proposition 7.4.2.1 adds: 'the map p_1 is finite flat because B̂ is regular, p_1 is finite (because we removed the p-rank 0 locus) and dominant, and Ĉ is Cohen-Macaulay.' This is the structural input for the local computations in Propositions 7.4.2.1 and 7.4.2.2 and for base-changing the fundamental class (fundamental-class-base-change). setup-klingen-paramodular-correspondence records only the negative half, that p_1 is not finite flat over X_1^{=0} or over the boundary. The positive statement is the Klingen-level analogue of t1-finite-flat-on-abelian-locus (Lemma 10.3.1), which is an item. Proof sketch:
- p_1 is proper, and quasi-finite off X_1^{=0}, because an abelian surface of p-rank ≥ 1 has finitely many subgroups of order p; hence it is finite there.
- Y_K is smooth over Z_p, and Y_Kli(p)K is regular and lci (Proposition 6.1.4.1). Miracle flatness (ext-miracle-flatness) then gives flatness.
Neither library has miracle flatness (library-coverage: 'Neither library has the local criterion for flatness or miracle flatness') or the Klingen model.

items.name: Serre–Tate deformation theorem (lifting with prescribed p-divisible group)
items.statement: For a scheme S on which p is locally nilpotent and a nilpotent thickening S_0 ↪ S, deformations of an abelian scheme A_0/S_0 to S are equivalent to deformations of its p-divisible group A_0[p^∞] (compatibly with polarizations). Passing to the limit, a (principally polarized) abelian surface A over l lifts to Ã over W(l) with any prescribed lift of A[p^∞], here μ_{p^∞} ⊕ E[p^∞] ⊕ Q_p/Z_p.
items.note: This is a distinct external input and is not in the extraction. The existing Serre–Tate items (ext-serre-tate-local-moduli, serre-tate-local-moduli, external-serre-tate-local-computations) are Katz's canonical coordinates at ordinary points. The fixreason of ext-serre-tate-local-moduli already flags this theorem as a different statement, used on p. 47. Checked against the p. 47 image: 'Consider the lift Ã → Spec W(l) with associated Barsotti-Tate group μ_{p^∞} ⊕ E[p^∞] ⊕ Q_p/Z_p'. The paper names no theorem there. The equivalence is planned at AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli:A4: 'Prove the Serre–Tate equivalence for deformations of abelian schemes with endomorphism and polarization structures; identify its tangent map with the Hodge filtration'. Passing to the limit over W(l) needs algebraization of the formal polarized lift, planned at SchemeAndStackFoundations:SF.4: 'formal schemes, algebraization ... An algebraized object comes with a comparison to its completion'. Formal GAGA with ample-line-bundle hypotheses is also at AdicSpacesPartII:F0. This matches the routing in PAPER-MAULIK-SHANKAR-TANG-22/8 and PAPER-SHANKAR-SHANKAR-TANG-ETAL-22/27 (A4). Neither library has it: declarations.tsv has no SerreTate declaration, and library-coverage.json says '`SerreTate` has zero occurrences and there is no deformation category of abelian schemes'. The paper also uses, without comment: the splitting A[p^∞] ≅ μ_{p^∞} ⊕ G^{oo} ⊕ Q_p/Z_p over l (ext-oort-zink-splitting, missing); G^{oo} ≅ E_0[p^∞] (Dieudonné classification, FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory:R07.2); and a lift of the quasi-polarization.

items.name: Local constancy of dim (M_x)^{=h} for a compact operator (Coleman)
items.statement: Let M be a projective Banach A-module with a compact endomorphism Ũ, and h ∈ Q. Then x ↦ dim (M ⊗̂_A K_x)^{=h} is locally constant on rank one points x of Spa(A,A^+) ([14] Part A). Combined with Σ_i(−1)^i dim H^i(M^•_x)^{=h} = Σ_i(−1)^i dim(M^i_x)^{=h}, this gives Proposition 13.1.3.1.
items.note:
Keep this as an external-input item, with only its first sentence as the statement. The Euler-characteristic step belongs to the proof of Prop. 13.1.3.1.

Source. The paper cites it without a result number. p. 85 reads: 'This follows from the equality Σ_i(−1)^i dim H^i(M^•_x)^{=h} = Σ_i(−1)^i dim(M^i_x)^{=h} and the local constancy of dim(M^i_x)^{=h} (see [14], Part A).' Here [14] is R. Coleman, 'p-adic Banach spaces and families of modular forms', Invent. Math. 127 (1997). prop-13-1-3-1-euler-characteristic-locally-constant mentions it only in its xnote and note. Serre's input already has its own item (serre-slope-decomposition-of-fibres), so this should too.

Why missing:
- Neither library has p-adic Fredholm theory. The TauCeti/Analysis/Fredholm/* declarations are Banach/Hilbert Fredholm-index theory (e.g. ContinuousLinearMap.IsFredholm.adjoint), which is unrelated.
- LocallyAnalyticDistributions:L4 plans 'nuclear/Fredholm determinants in the precise compact-operator setting, slope decompositions, and compatibility with specialization on slope-adapted affinoids'. Its decomposition node L4/finite-slope-summands (from Coleman §A4 and Buzzard Thm 3.3) gives a finite projective summand of rank n from P_φ = QS.
- PadicFamilies:L2a plans 'finite-projective slope summands on adapted affinoids' (nodes strict-slope-neighborhoods and slope-polynomials).
- Together these give local constancy of dim^{≤h} at classical points of a slope-adapted affinoid. No stage or node states local constancy of dim(M ⊗̂_A K_x)^{=h} near a rank-one point of Spa(A,A^+), with neighbourhoods as in footnote 20. That statement also needs the Newton polygon of the slope factor to be locally constant near x. The note of item 454 makes the same point.

routes.title: Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology
routes.brief:
Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory; parent PadicFamilies). This is PAPER-PILLONI-20's own proposal, not a join.

Where it starts. PadicFamilies plans abstract ordinary projectors (L0a), abstract eigenvariety gluing (L2a), and Hida and Coleman families for modular curves and totally real fields, always in one cohomological degree (L0, L2, L5). It stops there: it has no Siegel layer and no family spread over several degrees. This Part II starts at that point. For the Siegel threefold with K_p = GSp4(Z_p) it builds, in order:
- degree-0 ordinary Siegel families;
- higher Hida theory: a perfect Λ-complex in degrees [0,1] interpolating H^0 and H^1 of Ω^(k,2)(−D);
- higher Coleman theory: overconvergent Klingen-level cohomology in degrees [0,1], with compact U and small-slope classicality.

Source: V. Pilloni, Duke Math. J. 169 (2020) 1647–1807, doi:10.1215/00127094-2019-0075. "p. N" is a page of the author's version of 17 June 2019; the paywalled final revision was not compared.

Final results as printed. Setting (p. 2):
- X_K → Spec Z_p is a toroidal compactification of the Siegel threefold of level K = ∏_ℓ K_ℓ ⊂ GSp4(A_f), with K_p = GSp4(Z_p).
- X_{Kli}(p)_K → X_K is the Klingen cover, and D is the boundary.
- U is attached to Kli(p)diag(p²,p,p,1)Kli(p); T is "associated to the double coset K_p diag(p²,p,p,1)K_p".
- Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]], and k: Λ → Z_p extends z ↦ z^k.

The results:
- Theorem 1.1 (pp. 2–3). There is a perfect complex M of Λ-modules of amplitude [0,1] such that:
  1. for all k ∈ Z≥0 there is a canonical quasi-isomorphism M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Q_p = RΓ(X_{Kli}(p)_K, Ω^(k,2)(−D) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p)^{U−ord};
  2. for all k ∈ Z with k > p+1 there is a canonical isomorphism H^0(M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Q_p/Z_p) = H^0(X_K, Ω^(k,2)(−D) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p)^{T−ord};
  3. the perfect complex M carries an action of the Hecke algebra of level prime-to-p, and the isomorphisms above are equivariant for this action.
- Remark 1.1. For k > p+1, the p-stabilization map H^0(X_K, Ω^(k,2)(−D)⊗Q_p)^{T−ord} → H^0(X_{Kli}(p)_K, Ω^(k,2)(−D)⊗Q_p)^{U−ord} is an isomorphism.
- Theorem 1.2 = Theorem 15.2.1 (pp. 3, 107). Let m be a non-Eisenstein maximal ideal of the prime-to-pN Hecke algebra, where N is the product of the ℓ with K_ℓ ≠ GSp4(Z_ℓ). Then M_m has trivial Euler characteristic.
  - In §15.2: ρ̄: G_Q → GSp4(F̄_p) is unramified away from pN and absolutely irreducible; m ⊂ H^{Np} is its maximal ideal, Θ_m(Q_ℓ(X)) = det(1 − Xρ̄(Frob_ℓ)); the Euler characteristic of fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D))_m is 0.
- Remarks 1.4 and 15.2.1 are conjectures: record them as Prop-valued statements and never assume them.
  - Remark 1.4: if ρ̄ stays absolutely irreducible on the Galois groups of real quadratic fields, the H^i(M_m) are Λ-torsion.
  - Remark 15.2.1: if ρ̄ is not induced from a real quadratic field, the support has Krull dimension ≤ 1.
- State these exactly as well: Theorems 11.2.1 and 11.3.1, Corollary 13.3.3.1, Proposition 13.4.1, Theorem 14.7.1 and Theorem 14.8.1.

Corrections (sourceIssues).
- Theorem 1.1:
  - K is neat (E2).
  - T is the normalised composite T_1∘T_2, which acts as p^{3−r}(T_{p,1} + (1+p+p²+p³)T_{p,0}) (E1).
  - The headline claim, that M is perfect of amplitude [0,1], is Theorem 11.3.1(2). It needs a written proof (E91). That proof applies the §2 projectors of L0a factor by factor over Λ = ∏_i Λ_i (E5) and needs Igusa-sheaf acyclicity (E90).
  - Point 1 is Theorem 11.3.1(3) tensored with Q_p, followed by Theorem 14.8.1. The proof of Theorem 14.8.1 compares the overconvergent complex M† with M ⊗ Q_p (Lemmas 14.8.2–14.8.4). E164's corrected display writes out this chain.
  - Point 3 is proved for H^{Np}. Proposition 15.1.1 must also prove five things (E147):
    - the T_{ℓ,i} commute in D(Λ);
    - T_{ℓ,0} is invertible;
    - operators at different ℓ commute;
    - they commute with U;
    - the action is compatible with specialisation (Theorems 11.3.1, 14.8.1) and with the classical action used in Corollary 15.2.3.1.
- Theorem 1.2:
  - State it for m = m_ρ̄, meaning any maximal ideal satisfying the Q_ℓ rule. Add ℓ³Θ_m(T_{ℓ,0}) = ν(ρ̄(Frob_ℓ)) to single out one (E149, E150).
  - The Euler characteristic is a locally constant function on Spec Λ. Specialise at one large k in each residue class mod p−1 (E165), via Theorems 11.3.1(3) and 14.8.1 (E164).
  - The equivalence with "non-Eisenstein" belongs to GSp4NonregularModularityLifting and is not imported.
- p. 6: specialise at k = 0 (E3), and read "obstructed" (E4).

Layers (they cover every item of the route).
1. Degree-0 Siegel Hida theory (p. 5).
   - A finite free Λ2-module M′ with M′ ⊗_{Λ2,(k,r)} Z_p = H^0(𝔛^{≥2}_{Kli}(p)_K, Ω^(k,r)(−D))^{ord′} for (k,r) ∈ Z≥0 × Z (Hida, JIMJ 2002, with Pilloni, Duke 2011).
   - Classicality for r ≥ 4.
   - This instantiates L0a; OverconvergentAutomorphicForms O7 does not claim it.
2. The spherical T-operator and its ordinary part (§§7–8, pp. 37–54).
   - From §7's introduction (pp. 37–38):
     - T as the composite of the paramodular double cosets;
     - T = T_{p,1} + (1+p+p²+p³)T_{p,0}, with footnote 8;
     - the Hecke parameters, ordinarity and Θ_{π_p}(T).
   - From §1 (p. 4): the integral factorisation into U_1, U_2, T_1, T_2, and the supersingular-isogeny heuristic.
   - §7: T_1′, T_2′ and Lemmas 7.1.1–7.1.2; the normalised T_1, T_2, T; Proposition 7.2.1 and Lemma 7.3.1.
   - §7.4: Proposition 7.4.1.1 and Lemma 7.4.1.1 (commutation with Ha mod p). Then Ha′: Lemmas 7.4.2.2–7.4.2.5, Proposition 7.4.2.1 and Corollary 7.4.2.1; Proposition 7.4.2.2 with Lemma 7.4.2.6 (factorisation through Frobenius at p-rank 0); footnotes 10–11.
   - §8: Lemmas 8.1.1, 8.1.2, 8.2.1 and Propositions 8.1.1, 8.2.1.
   - Corrections: the boundary case of Lemma 7.4.2.3 (E58); read X^{≤0} (E61), Ω for ω (E63), and (p−1)n (E67). Misprints: E51–E57, E59, E60, E62, E64–E66.
3. Deep Klingen and Igusa towers and the Λ-adic sheaves (§9, pp. 54–57).
   - 𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p)_K; X^{≥1}_{Kli}(p^m)_n with Remarks 9.1.1.1–9.1.1.2 and Lemma 9.1.1.1; IG(p^m)_n.
   - The formal towers, H_∞ and 𝔍𝔊(p^∞).
   - 𝔉^κ, Remark 9.3.1, 𝔉^χ, the F^κ_{m,n} and their limits, F^k_{n,n} ≅ ω_{H_n}^{⊗k} and KΩ^(k,r).
   - The paramodular variants and Lemma 9.5.1.
   - Corrections: E68–E71 (E70 supplies the n = 1 affineness step).
4. The Klingen U-operator (§10, pp. 57–66).
   - ℭ_𝔜(p^m) and Lemma 10.1.1; 𝔛^{m−et}_par; ℭ¹ and ℭ² with Lemmas 10.2.1–10.2.2 and footnote 15; ℭ(p^m) and Proposition 10.2.1.
   - The traces (Lemmas 10.3.1–10.3.4, Remark 10.3.1), (10.4.A), and U_1, U_2, U.
   - The mod-p compatibilities with Ha and Ha′ (Lemmas 10.5.2.1–10.5.3.1); U on X_1^{=1} and on 𝔉^κ; Lemma 10.7.1; U ↔ p^{3−r}U_{Kli(p),1}.
   - Corrections: L has order p⁴ (E72), and ℭ(p^m) is lci (E75). Misprints: E73, E74, E76–E80.
5. Higher Hida theory (§11, pp. 66–73).
   - T^{et}, T^m, T′, T″, T‴; Lemmas 11.1.1.1–11.1.1.4 and 11.1.2.1; Corollaries 11.1.1.1–11.1.1.2 and 11.1.3.1.
   - Theorem 11.2.1 with M^• and N^•. Corollary 11.2.1: for k > p+1 the map eH^0(X, Ω^(k,2)(−D) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p) → fH^0(𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), Ω^(k,2)(−D) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p) is an isomorphism (the paper prints "quasi-isomorphism" for this map of modules; terminology only, with no sourceIssues entry).
   - Theorem 11.3.1 with its resolutions and the C_m factorisation.
   - Corrections: Lemma 11.1.1.4 holds for n ≥ 1 (E85), via L ⊇ G[p]^m and r ≥ 2 (E84); the step f∘i∘(1−e) = 0 (E86); weight (k,2) in 11.2.1(6) (E87); 11.2.1(7) from Proposition 2.2.1 (E88); E5, E90, E91. Misprints: E81–E83, E89, E92–E95.
6. Higher Coleman theory I: overconvergent sheaves (§12, pp. 73–83).
   - 𝔛(p^n,ε), Fil^can, Gr^can; the flag varieties, the Klingen quotient and 𝔗_{w′}.
   - 𝔏^{κ_A}, 𝔊^{κ_A,w}, 𝔉^{κ_A,w} (𝔏^{κ_A} by O1's invariant-sheaf construction on Pilloni's torsor 𝔉𝔏^+ → 𝔉𝔏; Lemma 12.6.2.2 from AIP's Siegel results, O8), and the analytic spaces and sheaves (Lemmas 12.6.2.1–12.6.2.2, 12.7.2.1–12.7.2.2).
   - C(n,ε,w,κ_A,r), H^i(†,κ_A,r), Propositions 12.8.2.1 and 12.9.1, and §§12.9.1–12.9.2.
   - Corrections: the intersection step of Lemma 12.9.2.1 (E106); w′ > 0 (E97). Misprints: E96, E98–E105.
7. Higher Coleman theory II (§§13.2–13.4, pp. 85–91; Remark 1.2).
   - C, the flag map, the normalised U, and compactness (§§13.2.1–13.2.4).
   - ℱ^{κ,w,++} and Proposition 13.3.1.1; the BGG sequence (Lemma 13.3.2.1, Proposition 13.3.2.1, Corollary 13.3.2.1); Proposition 13.3.3.1 and Corollary 13.3.3.1.
   - C_cusp(A_l); 𝒵 → 𝒲 as an instance of L2a's spectral variety for complexes (§13.1 goes there by source route); Proposition 13.4.1 from Proposition 13.1.3.1.
   - Corrections: d_1∘U = p^{k+1}U∘d_1 (E119). Proposition 14.4.1.1(2) is needed at level p^n (E115), together with a bounded-torsion comparison (E116). Localise at α^{−1} rather than take the fibre of C_cusp(A_l) (E123). ℂ means ℂ_p throughout §§13.3–14.9 (E117). Urban's slope condition (E107; slope decompositions are LocallyAnalyticDistributions L4's). Misprints: E108–E114, E118, E120, E121.
8. Klingen-level classicality and M† versus M (§14, pp. 91–106; pp. 3–5).
   - §§14.1–14.4: 𝒳_{Kli}(p)_ε, Lemmas 14.1.1–14.1.2, C_n, deg L_n, Lemma 14.3.1, Corollaries 14.3.1–14.3.2, Proposition 14.4.1.1, and §14.4.2's F^+, F^{++} and normalised U^n (Remark 14.4.2.1).
   - §§14.5–14.7: analytic continuation, integral projective systems, Theorem 14.7.1 and Corollary 14.7.1.
   - §14.8: f, the Klingen two-affine covering with its overconvergent Čech subcomplex, Lemmas 14.8.1–14.8.4 and Theorem 14.8.1.
   - §14.9: Proposition and Corollary 14.9.1, I, Lemma 14.9.1(b), Lemma 14.9.2, (𝔈_{p,2})^{≥1}, Lemma 14.9.2.1 and Remark 14.9.3.
   - M†: its comparison with M ⊗ Q_p (injective on H^0, surjective on H^1), ordinary classicality, and the quasi-isomorphism in all weights.
   - Corrections:
     - r ≥ 0 (E128); 0 < ε < 1 (E130, E132); Corollary 14.6.2's estimate (E134, E137); Lemma 14.7.1 (E135, E138); d_i^{†,′} is the slope-0 part (E140).
     - Lemma 14.8.3 via Lemma 5.1.5.2 weakened to need only αβ ∉ {αγ, βδ, γδ}, with (π^{Kli})_{αβ} the generalised ℓ^{−1}αβ-eigenspace of U_{Kli(ℓ),1}; the valuations (0, k+1, k+1, 2k+2) make αβ simple (E142).
     - Valuation ≥ 0 and i ∈ {0,1} in Proposition 14.9.1 and Corollary 14.9.1 (E139, E141); L_n ⊂ G[p^{2n}] (E124); deg L_n ≥ n (E127).
     - Misprints: E122, E125, E126, E129, E131, E133, E136, E143–E145.
9. Main theorems and the Hecke action (§1; §§15.1–15.2, 15.2.5).
   - The §15 setting and M_K; the prime-to-p correspondences on 𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p) and Proposition 15.1.1 (E146); T_K and M_{K,m}.
   - Theorem 1.1 and Remark 1.1.
   - The injection H^0(M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Z_p) → M′ ⊗_{Λ2,(k,2)} Z_p. Its expectations on p. 5 stay expectations.
   - Classicality of the p-divisible classes in weight (0,2).
   - The specialisation of M_{K,m} to Klingen level, and dim fH^0 = dim fH^1 at level K^pKli(p). This is planned here: apply f, which acts through π_p^{Kli(p)}, to IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes' automorphic description and h/g symmetry at level K^pKli(p) (E164).
   - Theorem 15.2.1 and Remark 15.2.1.

Operators at p. This roadmap owns T = T_1∘T_2 on all of RΓ(X) and its comparison with SiegelModularFormsModPn's T_{p,1}. It also owns every integral or overconvergent Klingen-level operator: U_1, U_2, U, the integral U_{Kli(p),2} on Ω^(k,2)(−D) ⊗ I^{−3} (Lemma 14.9.1(b)), and the analytic U^n (§14.4.2). Elsewhere:
- SiegelModularFormsModPn owns the spherical correspondences over the p-rank ≥ 1 locus (Lemma 14.9.1(a)) and Hartogs in general form. Lemma 14.9.2 imports Hartogs and proves only the Klingen I^{−3} part.
- IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes owns the characteristic-0 actions, including the characteristic-0 T_{p,2} and U_{Kli(p),2} of §14.9.
- Do not merge the Klingen covering of §14.8 with SiegelModularFormsModPn's spherical covering by lifts of Ha and Ha′.

Imports, atlas roadmaps:
- Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions (PadicFamilies) L0a, L2a (the paper's §2 and §13.1 go there by source route).
- Locally analytic distributions, growth, and character spaces (LocallyAnalyticDistributions) L3, L4.

- Shimura towers and perfectoid representability (PerfectoidShimuraVarieties) S1, S3.
- Adic Spaces PartII (AdicSpacesPartII) F0, R0, R1, R2, R3, with E14, E16, E17 applied there.
- Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra) P7, P9, R03.3.
- Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory) R07.1–R07.2.
- Abelian Schemes And Arithmetic Moduli (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli) A3–A4.
- Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations) SF.2, SF.4.
- Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry) A0-extension, R09.1.
- Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry (ShimuraCompactifications) C2, C3, C4, C5.
- Siegel and PEL moduli problems (PELModuli) M2, M4, M5.
- Shimura data, Hermitian domains, and adelic level structures (ShimuraData) D5.
- Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms (AutomorphicBundles) B3.
- Integral Hecke actions, determinants and interpolation (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants) IHG.2, IHG.3.
- Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) SR.1, SR.2, SR.3, SR.4, requesting there the weakened Lemma 5.1.5.2 of E142.
- Reductive groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models (ReductiveGroupsPartII) RG2.4.
- Explicit K₀: projectives, rank and determinant (KTheoryLowDegrees) Z.2, Z.6.
- Profinite and pro-p groups (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/ProfiniteProPGroups), stage "Layer 9 prerequisites: two owned inputs": the completed group algebra, for Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]] (§9.3).

Imports, proposals (all upstream):
- Algebraic modular forms, reduction and Serre weights, Part II: Siegel modular forms of genus two modulo p^n (SiegelModularFormsModPn): Ha, Ha′ (E43), the p-rank strata, the lifts, Hartogs, the spherical operators, and p-adic Siegel modular forms ([60] Def. 4.3) with their q-expansions and the integrality of U on q-expansions (layer 1; Proposition 13.3.1.1).
- Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes (IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes): the §4.3 correspondences (request their composition rule there, E147), the prime-to-p T_{ℓ,i}, Lan's vanishing, Eisenstein boundary, the h/g symmetry, Harris's automorphic description of interior cohomology (Theorem 15.2.3.1, Corollary 15.2.3.1), and the characteristic-0 T_{p,2} and U_{Kli(p),2} of §14.9.
- Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: integral models and reduction (ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII): Y_Kli, Y_par, the local models, the Klingen cover, and the §7.1 correspondence X ← X_{Kli}(p) → X_par with G → G′ → G (p_1 and p_2 are not quasi-finite over the p-rank-0 loci, p. 38, nor finite flat over the boundary, footnote 9).
- Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry, Part II: integral boundary charts of Hodge type (ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary): X, X_{Kli}(p), X_par and X^⋆ over Z_p (E40), the Faltings–Chai toroidal Hecke correspondences (C_{ℓ,i} for Proposition 15.1.1; the integral C_{p,2} of §14.9.2), and Stroh's extension of H over the boundary (footnote 27).

Never import Minimal modularity lifting for GSp₄ in non-regular weight (GSp4NonregularModularityLifting).

Consumers:
- GSp4NonregularModularityLifting, for layer 1 (Pilloni 2012) and M.
- AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity (DESIGN-BCGP18, pending, not in the atlas), whose brief asks for higher Coleman theory as its own roadmap: this one.

Future source: Boxer–Pilloni, "Higher Hida theory for Siegel modular forms" (Invent. Math. 2026), which extends the families to the whole weight space.

Acceptance tests:
- deg T_{p,1} = p(1+p+p²+p³).
- On a spherical π_p, Θ(T) = p^{2−r}(αβ+αγ+αδ+βδ+γδ) + p^{1−r}(1+p+p²)αδ.
- Tr∘i = (p+1)Id at n = 0.
- Deep Klingen maps have degree p+1 (m = 1) or p (m ≥ 2) over the ordinary locus, and are isomorphisms over p-rank 1.
- L[p] of order p³ excludes Lagrangians of type (Z/p²)².
- For p odd, Spec Λ has p−1 components, and Theorem 15.2.1 holds on each; for p = 2, Λ is local.
- A Jordan block for U separates the eigenspace from the generalised eigenspace in §13.4 (E123).
- Hecke parameters of π_p contributing to eH^i (k ≥ 1) or fH^i (k ≥ 0), i ∈ {0,1}, have valuations (0,0,k+1,k+1) (Corollary 14.9.1; E141).

routes.title: Algebraic modular forms, reduction and Serre weights, Part II: Siegel modular forms of genus two modulo p^n
routes.brief:
This route joins SiegelModularFormsModPn, proposed by PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 (CG20). It has the same id, the same parent, Algebraic modular forms, reduction and Serre weights (AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights), and the same title. The design job merges the two briefs. The roadmap still starts where the parent stops: after R15.6, which has no genus-two layer. It builds the genus-two analogue of R15.1–R15.3, and Pilloni's Hasse-invariant material extends the genus-one Hasse invariant of R15.3.

Below is what V. Pilloni, "Higher coherent cohomology and p-adic modular forms of singular weights", Duke Math. J. 169 (2020) 1647–1807, doi:10.1215/00127094-2019-0075, adds. "p. N" is a page of the author's version of 17 June 2019. That version is post-referee; the journal's final revision of 15 October 2019 is paywalled and was not compared. sourceIssues numbers are PAPER-PILLONI-20's.

Setting.
- Add the paramodular Y_par (§6.1.3) and its toroidal compactification X_par (§6.1.5.4, imported from ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary), with semi-abelian scheme G′.
- X_n and X_par,n are the reductions mod p^n. ω = det ω_G on X, and det ω_G′ on X_par. The results hold for all primes p.
- Pilloni's Ω^(k,r) = Sym^k ω_G ⊗ det^r ω_G is CG20's ω(k+r, r).
- Pilloni's T_{p,2} (diag(p,p,1,1), p. 21) is CG20's T = T_{p,1} (β_{p,1} = diag(1,1,p,p)). Pilloni's T_{p,1} (diag(p²,p,p,1)) is CG20's T₂ = T_{p,2} (β_{p,2} = diag(1,p,p,p²)). The subscripts are swapped between the two sources; fix one naming.

Amendment to CG20's layer 2.
- HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0 owns Ha = det V⋆ for a BT₁ over any F_p-scheme, LF (Prop. 6.3.1.1), Lemma 6.3.1.1 and Lemma 6.3.4.1 (E47).
- Delete "T0 should take h from here" and drop T0 from the consumers. This roadmap imports Ha.
- CG20's H2 comparison (the Hasse ideal of HilbertModularVarietiesAndShimuraCurves H2 is locally generated by lifts of h) stays here, stated for the Ha imported from T0.

Final results as printed, then corrections:
- Proposition 6.3.3.1 (p. 33).
  - Hypotheses (§6.3, p. 30, and §6.3.3, p. 31): S is a normal reduced F_p-scheme. G is a BT₁ over S of height 4 and dimension 2, whose generic étale and multiplicative ranks are 1. Its Hasse–Witt map V⋆: ω_G → ω_G^(p) has rank 1, that is, Ker V⋆ is an invertible sheaf and locally a direct factor of ω_G. S′ ⊂ S is the dense open subscheme where both ranks are 1.
  - Statement: "The Hasse invariant Ha′(G) ∈ H⁰(S′, ω_G^{p²−1}) extends to S. Moreover, it vanishes precisely on S∖S′."
  - Corrections: read (det ω_G)^{p²−1} (E44). Lemmas 6.3.3.3 and 6.3.3.5 are false as stated. Either replace S∖S′ in them by the locus of multiplicative rank 0, or assume that the étale and multiplicative ranks are equal at every point, as they are for abelian surfaces (E43).
- Lemma 6.3.4.2 (p. 34). Let S be an F_p-scheme and G, G′ Barsotti–Tate groups over S (E46) of constant multiplicative rank. Let λ: G → G′ be an isogeny with kernel L ⊂ G[p]. Suppose each geometric point x → S has a multiplicative H_x ⊂ G_x[p] with H_x ⊕ L_x = G_x[p]. Then there is a canonical isomorphism λ̃⋆: det ω_G′ → det ω_G with λ̃⋆Ha(G′) = Ha(G), and λ̃⋆Ha′(G′) = Ha′(G) when the second Hasse invariant is defined.
- §6.4 (pp. 34–35). X_n^{=r} is dense open in X_n^{≤r}, and likewise at paramodular level. The strata have dimension r+1, not 3−r (E48). "≤r" means at most r and "≥r" at least r (E45).
- Lemma 6.4.1 (p. 35): "The schemes X_1^{≤1} and X_{par,1}^{≤1} carry the reduced schematic structure", where X_1^{≤1} = V(Ha(G)) and X_{par,1}^{≤1} = V(Ha(G′)). In the proof, Fe₂ = −pe₃ (E49).
- Lemma 6.4.2 (p. 36). Ha′(G) ∈ H⁰(X_1^{=1}, ω^{p²−1}) and Ha′(G′) ∈ H⁰(X_{par,1}^{=1}, ω^{p²−1}) extend to X_1^{≤1} and X_{par,1}^{≤1}, and vanish on X_1^{≤0} and X_{par,1}^{≤0}. In the proof, λ^t: (G′)^t → G′ (E50). Then X_1^{≤0} := V(Ha′(G)) ⊂ X_1^{≤1} and X_{par,1}^{≤0} := V(Ha′(G′)) as schemes (p. 37).
- Remark 6.4.1 (p. 37; proof only sketched). Ha′(G) vanishes to order 2 along the rank-0 locus. For p ≥ 3 it has a square root of weight (p²−1)/2 that vanishes to order 1; for p = 2 it has none.
- Lemma 14.9.1, spherical half (p. 103; k ≥ 0): T_{p,2} acts on RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}, Ω^(k,2)(−D)).
- Lemma 14.9.2, spherical half (p. 103). For n ∈ Z≥0 ∪ {∞} (with p^∞ = 0), the map H^i(X, Ω^(k,2)(−D)/p^n) → H^i(𝔛^{≥1}, Ω^(k,2)(−D)/p^n), where X is the toroidal compactification over Z_p, is bijective for i = 0 and injective for i = 1. It is the complement of 𝔛^{≥1} that has codimension 2 (E143).

Additions by layer:
- 2a. Ha′ over F_p-schemes (§§6.3.2–6.3.4):
  - the filtration G^m ⊂ G^o ⊂ G, G^oo = G^o/G^m, Ha′(G^oo) and Ha′(G) = Ha(G^m)^{p+1} ⊗ Ha′(G^oo);
  - Lemma 6.3.2.1, LF^{⊗(p+1)}(Ha′(G)) = Ha′(G^D); the composite in its proof ends in (det ω_{G^D})^{p²−1} (E42);
  - Lemmas 6.3.3.1–6.3.3.5, with H ⊂ G[F], the maps V⋆_H, W and Z, and the section A (E43);
  - invariance under étale isogenies, and Lemma 6.3.4.2.
  The Dieudonné crystal Ext¹_cris(−, O_{S/F_p})_S over reduced F_p-schemes (used for G^oo in §6.3.2, and for G in §6.3.3), its Hodge filtration, and the sequence of perfect complexes in the proof of Lemma 6.3.3.1 are routed to FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory R07.2 (source route dieudonne-crystal-exact-sequence-of-complexes-HW-duality). This layer proves them only if that route is rejected.
- 2b. Strata (§6.4):
  - Ha on X_1 and X_par,1, including the boundary: instantiate T0's Ha, which T0 extends to semi-abelian degeneration charts, for G and G′. Prove here only the Siegel-specific facts: V(Ha(G)) and V(Ha(G′)) have as underlying sets the loci of multiplicative rank ≤ 1, which gives the scheme structures X_1^{≤1} and X_{par,1}^{≤1}; and Ha has q-expansion 1;
  - the Grothendieck–Messing computation for Lemma 6.4.1 (E49);
  - Ha′ on X_1^{=1} and X_{par,1}^{=1}, extended to the boundary through G[p]^o and G′[p]^o (truncated BT₁ of height 3, dimension 2 and multiplicative rank 1);
  - finiteness of the superspecial set SS (Narasimhan–Nori; the reference is corrected in E174), and rank 1 of the Hasse–Witt map on the ≤1 loci off SS;
  - X_1^{≤1}∖SS is smooth, and X_{par,1}^{≤1}∖SS is locally F_p[a,b,c]/(ab). ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII supplies, on its Iwahori-level moduli, the local-model chart F_p[x,y,a,b,c]/(xy, ax+by+abc) and the special-fibre strata X_0^{m,e}, X_0^{sg,F}, X_0^{o,m} and X_0^{et,o} of Pilloni, Duke Math. J. 157 (2011), pp. 186–189 (its Layer 2 recovers them). This roadmap proves only the identifications in the proof of Lemma 6.4.2 (pp. 36–37). X_1^{≤1}∖SS is the union of X_0^{m,e} and X_0^{sg,F}, and the closure of X_0^{m,e} is locally F_p[x,y,a,b,c]/(xy, ax+by+abc, a, y, x+bc) ≅ F_p[b,c]. X_{par,1}^{≤1}∖SS is open in the union of the closures of X_0^{o,m} and X_0^{et,o}, which are the quotients by a = 0 and b = 0 of F_p[x,y,a,b,c]/(xy, ax+by+abc, y+ac, x) ≅ F_p[a,b,c];
  - Lemma 6.4.2 and Remark 6.4.1.
  Merge with CG20:
  - Ha′ plays the role of CG20's h̃: both are sections of det^{p²−1} on CG20's S (= X_1^{≤1} as schemes). Plan one section.
  - CG20's Z ⊂ CG20's S (= X_1^{≤1} as schemes) is X_1^{≤0} as sets.
  - For p ≥ 3, V(Ha′) should be twice Koblitz's divisor (Remark 6.4.1). Prove this.
  - HigherHidaAndColemanTheory needs the scheme V(p, Ha, Ha′) (E61).
- 2c. Lifts:
  - Ha^{p^{n−1}} lifts canonically to H⁰(X_n, ω^{p^{n−1}(p−1)}), and hence to every X_n-scheme by pullback, e.g. X^{≥1}_{Kli(p),n}, since (a+px)^{p^{n−1}} ≡ a^{p^{n−1}} mod p^n (p. 70). CG20's A^{p^{m−1}} statement follows, since the same congruence holds with ϖ in place of p.
  - The spherical two-affine covering (§14.8, proof of Lemma 14.8.2, p. 101). Descend Ha and Ha′ to V(p) and V(p, Ha) in 𝔛^⋆; plan this step, which the paper leaves implicit. For large n, lift Ha^{n(p+1)} and Ha′^n non-canonically to sections s₁ and s₂ of the ample sheaf (det ω_G)^{n(p²−1)} over 𝔛^⋆. Then 𝔛^{⋆,≥1} = D(s₁) ∪ D(s₂). The second bullet of HigherHidaAndColemanTheory's item two-affine-covering-of-p-rank-one-locus-and-overconvergent-subcomplex imports this from here; that roadmap keeps the Klingen covering.
- 1 and 3. p-adic Siegel modular forms of weight (κ, r) (Pilloni, Bull. SMF 140 (2012), Def. 4.3):
  - the ordinary Igusa tower of the Siegel threefold, built here;
  - the forms on it, their q-expansion map and the q-expansion principle;
  - the formal q-expansion operator that the Klingen U induces on them. It preserves integral q-expansions (Hida, JIMJ 1 (2002)). Identify it on q-expansions with one of CG20's formal operators; CG20's layer 3 identifies its Klingen U_{p,2} with Z₂.
  HigherHidaAndColemanTheory owns the analytic Klingen U (p^{3−r}U_{Kli(p),1}, §10, p. 57), the embedding of H⁰(†, κ, r) into p-adic forms (p. 89) and degree-0 Siegel Hida theory (ordinary projector, M′, control). It imports the space of p-adic forms and their q-expansions from here. On p. 89, read ℂ_p for ℂ (E117).
- 4. Operators at p. Build each spherical correspondence once over the p-rank ≥ 1 locus. The T_{p,2}-correspondence is ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary's C_{p,2}; CG20's Hilbert-scheme construction of the β_{p,1} correspondence is its restriction to Y, not a second construction.
  - T_{p,2} (CG20's T). (C_{p,2})^{≥1} → 𝔛^{≥1} is finite and generically étale, and 𝔛^{≥1} is smooth, hence normal, which gives a trace. T′_{p,2} lands in p³Ω^(k,2)(−D). By normality this is checked at ordinary points by Serre–Tate, where the (differential, trace) factors are (p^{k+4}, 1), (p², p) and (1, p³). So the normalized sheaf map p⁻³T′_{p,2} is integral, and T_{p,2} acts on RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}, Ω^(k,2)(−D)) (Lemma 14.9.1) and, with Hartogs, on H⁰. On H⁰ in every weight ω(j,k) with j ≥ k ≥ 2, CG20's Lemma 8.8 gets T from the same correspondence, normalized by q-expansions.
  - CG20's T₂ and Q₂ (Pilloni's T_{p,1}-type). Plan only the H⁰ action, normalized by q-expansions (CG20 Lemmas 8.8 and 8.12). Neither source proves an action on RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}). Pilloni (p. 37) does not define T_{p,1} integrally, because its cocharacter is not minuscule.
  - Hartogs, stated once. X is smooth over O (O = Z_p in Pilloni), so each X_n = X ⊗ O/ϖ^n is Cohen–Macaulay. Let E = Ω^(k,r) or Ω^(k,r)(−D) (k ≥ 0, r ∈ Z) and n ∈ Z≥1 ∪ {∞}. Then H⁰(X, E/ϖ^n) → H⁰(𝔛^{≥1}, E/ϖ^n) is bijective and H¹(X, E/ϖ^n) → H¹(𝔛^{≥1}, E/ϖ^n) is injective. The reason is that the complement, the p-rank-0 locus, has codimension 2 in X_n (E143), so SF.2's depth extension applies; n = ∞ follows by passing to the limit. K/O coefficients follow by colimits. Koecher is not needed, because X_1^{=0} misses D: the torus part gives multiplicative rank ≥ 1 at the boundary.
  - Instances of Hartogs: H⁰(X_1^{≥1}, Ω^(k,r)(−D)) = H⁰(X_1, Ω^(k,r)(−D)) (p. 53); the spherical half of Lemma 14.9.2, which the first map of HigherHidaAndColemanTheory's item lemma-14-9-2-extension-over-codimension-two imports from here; and CG20's Lemma 8.8. HigherHidaAndColemanTheory proves only the Klingen I^{−3} half of Lemma 14.9.2.
  - The depth extension is routed to SF.2 (source route external-sga2-depth-extension). If that route is rejected, CG20's fallback applies and this layer proves it.

Imports added:
- Hodge–Tate theory, canonical subgroups, and automorphic period maps (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups) T0: Ha, LF, Lemmas 6.3.1.1 and 6.3.4.1. CG20 had T0 as a consumer; it is now upstream.
- Abelian Schemes And Arithmetic Moduli (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli) A4: Serre–Tate with polarizations and its tangent map, for Lemma 6.4.1 and the ordinary-point factors of layer 4.
- Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: integral models and reduction (ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII): Y_par; Proposition 6.1.4.1 (for Lemma 6.4.1); the moduli of Lagrangian subgroups of G[p] (CG20's β_{p,1}) with the finiteness of its fibres at points of p-rank ≥ 1, which layer 4 uses for the finiteness of (C_{p,2})^{≥1} → 𝔛^{≥1}; the dual polarization λ^t: (G′)^t → G′ of the paramodular chain (E50); and the moduli of abelian surfaces with a polarization of degree prime to p and Iwahori level at p, with its local model and special-fibre strata. The latter is the Iwahori instance of the parahoric Siegel lattice-chain construction that that roadmap's joined briefs plan. ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII's brief from this extraction must name this instance, and its local model comes through that roadmap's local-model import.
- Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry, Part II: integral boundary charts of Hodge type (ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary): X_par, X^⋆_par and the compactified C_{p,2}.
- Scheme, stack, cohomology and intersection foundations (SchemeAndStackFoundations) SF.2 becomes an import, in place of CG20's request.
CG20's existing import of Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory) R07.1–R07.2 now also supplies G^m ⊂ G (Lemma 6.3.4.2) and the Dieudonné crystal of layer 2a. CG20's imports of ShimuraCompactifications C3–C5 and DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3 already cover Koecher, X^⋆ and depth. Neither of the two Part II roadmaps above imports this roadmap. IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes stays upstream.

Consumers added:
- Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory).
- AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity (DESIGN-BCGP18, pending) is already a consumer, and now also uses this roadmap through HigherHidaAndColemanTheory.

Acceptance tests:
- For every p, the form J (⟨e₁,e₄⟩ = ⟨e₂,e₃⟩ = 1) is not compatible with the printed F: ⟨Fe₂,Fe₃⟩ = −p, where compatibility needs p·σ⟨e₂,e₃⟩ = p. It is compatible with Fe₂ = −pe₃ (E49). This keeps Ker F = ⟨ē₁,ē₂⟩, the matrix (−Y 0; −Z 1) and the tangent conditions X = Z, Z = 0 and X = 0, and the Hasse invariant of the universal deformation is −Y. The item hasse-invariant-simple-zero-at-p-rank-one-points uses the equally valid Fe₃ = −e₂, which gives Y, and states the incompatibility only for odd p. Use E49's normalization, for every p.
- F_p[x,y,a,b,c]/(xy, ax+by+abc, a, y, x+bc) ≅ F_p[b,c].
- Lifts of Ha are not canonical mod p², but their p-th powers are.
- With p inverted, T_{p,2} equals the operator of IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes.
- Normalization of T_{p,2} against CG20's T on q-expansions. The paper computes the ordinary-point factors only for r = 2. The general form below is derived for this brief and must be checked. In weight Ω^(k,r) with r ≥ 2, the (differential, trace) factors should be (p^{k+2r}, 1) for multiplicative kernel, (p^r, p) for mixed kernel and (1, p³) for étale kernel. Then p⁻³T′_{p,2} = U + p^{r−2}Z + p^{k+2r−3}V on q-expansions. This is CG20's T = U + p^{k′−2}Z + p^{j′+k′−3}V (Lemma 8.3) at (j′,k′) = (k+r, r). At r = 2 the factors are those of p. 104.

routes.title: Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes
routes.brief:
This entry joins the Part II that PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 proposes and PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 joins, under the same id, parent (Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, AutomorphicBundles) and title. The design job merges the three briefs. It starts where AutomorphicBundles B3–B5 stop. Its layers are CG18's 1–4 and CG20's 5–8. Source: V. Pilloni, "Higher coherent cohomology and p-adic modular forms of singular weights", Duke Math. J. 169 (2020) 1647–1807, doi:10.1215/00127094-2019-0075. Pages refer to the author version of 17 June 2019 (printed page = PDF page); the Duke text could not be compared. sourceIssues are PAPER-PILLONI-20's.

Notation.
- S^tor_{K,Σ} is a toroidal compactification of the complex Siegel threefold S_K of neat level K.
- D = S^tor_{K,Σ} ∖ S_K is its boundary (printed S^tor_{K,Σ} ∖ S_{K,Σ}, E29).
- Ω^{(k,r)} = Sym^k ω_G ⊗ det^r ω_G for (k,r) ∈ Z≥0 × Z (CG20's ω(k+r,r)).
- Over Z_p, X, X_Kli(p) and X_par are the toroidal compactifications at spherical, Klingen and paramodular level at p, and X^⋆, X^⋆_Kli(p), X^⋆_par are the minimal ones.
- N is the product of the primes ℓ with K_ℓ ≠ GSp4(Z_ℓ), and H^N = ⊗'_{ℓ∤N} H_ℓ. H^{Np} is the same algebra away from Np.
- m ⊂ H^{Np} is any maximal ideal with Θ_m(Q_ℓ(X)) = det(1 − Xρ̄(Frob_ℓ)) for all ℓ ∤ Np, for a continuous absolutely irreducible ρ̄: G_Q → GSp4(F̄_p) unramified outside Np (IHG.3; E150).

Final results, as printed, with corrections.
- Theorem 6.2.2.1 ([50], thm. 8.6; p. 30). "For all (k,r) ∈ Z≥0 × Z and i > 0, R^iπ_*Ω^{(k,r)}(−D_X) = 0 and R^i(π_par)_*Ω^{(k,r)}(−D_{X_par}) = 0", for π: X → X^⋆ and π_par: X_par → X^⋆_par over Z_p.
  - State Lan's theorem once, in the form of [50] Def. 8.5 and Thm. 8.6: for a quasi-coherent sheaf on a toroidal compactification at any neat level that is formally subcanonical over a Z_(p)-algebra R. It then also holds modulo p^n, which §8.2 uses on X_1.
  - Also state it locally on the minimal compactification, for sheaves given only over π^{−1}(U) with U open. HigherHidaAndColemanTheory can then apply it over X^{⋆,≥1}_Kli(p) modulo p^n (§11.3). It must still check Def. 8.5 for its Igusa sheaves (E90).
  - The spherical, paramodular and Klingen (X_Kli(p) → X^⋆_Kli(p)) cases over Z_p are instances.
  - The proof of Lemma 14.8.2 (p. 101) uses the Klingen case for the analytic adic spaces 𝒳_Kli(p) → 𝒳^⋆_Kli(p) over Spa(ℂ_p, O) (ℂ there is ℂ_p, E117) and cites "[50], thm. 8.9". In [50], 8.9 is the remark that the proof of Thm. 8.6 works for non-smooth cone decompositions (E90), so both citations mean Thm. 8.6.
  - HigherHidaAndColemanTheory deduces that analytic case from the algebraic one by flat base change to O_{ℂ_p}, p-adic completion and passage to the adic generic fibre. It uses the proper comparison of Adic Spaces PartII (AdicSpacesPartII) R1–R2, which it imports.
- Theorem 15.2.3.1 ([30], coro. 5.3.2; p. 108). Let λ = (λ1,0;c) ∈ X^*(T) + (2,1;0) with λ1 < 0, k = −λ1 − 1 and c = −λ1 + 3. Then for every integer k ≥ R − 1:
  - H̄^0(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)}) = ⊕_{π_f}(π_f^K)^{m^h(π_f)}, over the irreducible admissible π_f of GSp4(A_f) with π_f ⊗ π(λ)^h cuspidal automorphic, where m^h(π_f) is its multiplicity;
  - similarly for H̄^1, with π(λ)^g and m^g.
  R comes from Theorem 15.2.2.1(2), whose hypothesis reads −λ1 ≥ R (printed λ1 ≥ R, E159).
- Corollary 15.2.3.1 (p. 108). For k ≥ R − 1:
  - H^0(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D))_m = ⊕(π_f^K)^{m^h(π_f)}, over the irreducible admissible π_f with π_f ⊗ π(λ)^h cuspidal automorphic and Θ_{π_f}: H^{Np} → ℂ congruent to Θ_m;
  - similarly H^1(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D))_m = ⊕(π_f^K)^{m^g(π_f)}, over the π_f with π_f ⊗ π(λ)^g cuspidal automorphic and Θ_{π_f} congruent to Θ_m.
  The H^1 display lacks the subscript m, and without it the statement is false (E156). In the proof the sequence is exact, not short exact, and continues to H^1(Ω^{(k,2)}) (E157). The boundary case is k = 0, not k = 2 (E162).
- Proposition 15.2.4.1 (p. 109). "Let π_f be an admissible irreducible representation of G(A_f) which is unramified at primes ℓ not dividing Np. Let Θ_{π_f}: H^{Np} → Q̄_p be the associated character of the Hecke algebra. Assume that Θ_{π_f} is congruent to Θ_m. Let λ = (λ1,0;c) ∈ X^*(T) + (2,1;0) with λ1 > 0. Then π_f ⊗ π(λ)^h is automorphic if and only if π_f ⊗ π(λ)^g is automorphic and moreover, m^h(π_f) = m^g(π_f) = 1."
  - Read λ1 < 0 (E163).
  - Read "automorphic" as "occurs in the discrete spectrum", and m^h, m^g as discrete multiplicities. π(λ)^h and π(λ)^g are tempered, so such π are cuspidal (Wallach; CG20's case-a-cuspidal-limit-of-discrete-series). These are therefore the multiplicities of Corollary 15.2.3.1.
  - In the proof, ψ is of general type, so S_ψ = 1 and Π_∞ = {π(λ)^g, π(λ)^h}. Do not claim that the global packet is tempered (E161).
  - The proposition rests on Arthur's classification, which is conditional in ML.4.
State Theorem 15.2.3.1 and Corollary 15.2.3.1 at any neat K, including K_p = Kli(p). §15.2.5 applies them at level K^pKli(p) (E164).

Additions, by layer.

Layer 3.
- Correspondences:
  - cohomological correspondences T: R(p1)_*p2^*F → G and their map on RΓ (Definition 4.3.1(2), p. 19);
  - the adjoint form p2^*F → p1^!G (Remark 4.3.2);
  - construction from p2^*F → p1^*G and a fundamental class (§4.3.1);
  - renormalisation ϖ^{−k}T (Remark 4.3.3).
  State these for quasi-coherent sheaves. Definition 4.3.1 says "coherent", but §15.1 applies it to 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D) on the formal scheme 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p).
- What §4.3 lacks (E147):
  - the composite of two cohomological correspondences, via fibre product and base change of f^! and of fundamental classes (Proposition 4.2.5.1, from A0-extension);
  - restriction to opens and to locally closed strata;
  - base change to formal completions (footnote 10, p. 46, cites §4.2.5 for this);
  - reduction modulo p^n.
  §§7.4, 10.5 and 15.1 use each of these.
- The H^N-action on H^i(Ω^{(k,r)}) and H^i(Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) (p. 24; [30] prop. 2.6):
  - T_{ℓ,i} comes from the Faltings–Chai correspondences and the fundamental class of p1;
  - T_{ℓ,2} = ℓ^{−3}T'_{ℓ,2} and T_{ℓ,i} = ℓ^{−6}T'_{ℓ,i} for i ∈ {0,1} (p. 25), with target p1^!Ω^{(k,r)} (E32);
  - Remark 5.3.1 makes the smallest Hodge–Tate weight 0 (E31).
- Hecke relations on RΓ, not only on H^i (E147). T_{ℓ,0}, T_{ℓ,1} and T_{ℓ,2} commute as endomorphisms of RΓ(Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) in the derived category, T_{ℓ,0} is invertible, and operators at different ℓ commute. So H^N → End_D(RΓ) is a ring map.
  - Proof route: compare the composite correspondences on the interior, where they are finite étale, then extend over the boundary. This extends B5's composition law from sections to RΓ.
  - State the relations in a form that HigherHidaAndColemanTheory can apply to 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω²(−D) on 𝔛^{≥1}_Kli(p) (Proposition 15.1.1). Commutation with U is that roadmap's own task (E147).
- Define the action on the canonical model over Q (B2–B3, C2–C3), so that its eigenvalue systems are algebraic. Theorem 5.3.1 in GSp4NonregularModularityLifting uses this.
- Operators at p with p inverted: T_{p,2} on H^i(X, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) ⊗ Q_p and U_{Kli(p),2} on H^i(X_Kli(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) ⊗ Q_p, each normalised by p^{−3} (§14.9, pp. 102, 104–105). Their eigenvalues come from SR.1–SR.4 (αδ = βγ, E24).
- Integral operators at p stay outside this roadmap: Lemma 14.9.1(a) in SiegelModularFormsModPn; Lemma 14.9.1(b), U with the I^{−3} twist, and T on RΓ(X) in HigherHidaAndColemanTheory.

Layer 4.
- Fix Q̄_p ≅ ℂ (p. 108). Θ_{π_f} is the character of H^{Np} on ⊗_{ℓ∤Np} π_ℓ^{GSp4(Z_ℓ)}.
- A character Θ: H^{Np} → ℂ is congruent to Θ_m when it takes values in Z̄_p and reduces to Θ_m. H^i(−)_m is the sum of the generalised eigenspaces for such Θ.
- Prove that the eigenvalues are p-integral. The prime-to-p correspondences over Z_p (C3 on C5's models at level K, and on ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary's at Klingen level) preserve the lattice given by the image of H^i(X, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)), and ℓ^{−3}, ℓ^{−6} ∈ Z_p^×.
- Prove H^i(X, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) ⊗_{Z_p} ℂ ≅ H^i(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)), and the same at Klingen level, equivariantly for H^{Np}, T_{p,2} and U_{Kli(p),2}. The inputs are:
  - the identification of the generic fibres with the canonical models (C5 at level K; at Klingen level, ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII for Y_Kli(p) and ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary for X_Kli(p));
  - flat base change;
  - GAGA (Complex Comparison PartII (ComplexComparisonPartII) C2–C3, which CG20 imports).
  So the localisation at m of the Z_p-module (IHG.2), tensored with Q̄_p, is the complex localisation above. §15.2.5 uses this at level K^pKli(p).

Layer 5.
- Theorem 6.2.2.1 as stated above. It is an input to CG20's Pilloni large-weight vanishing.
- Cite B3's pushforward to the minimal compactification, and prove Theorem 6.2.2.1 compatible with it on the generic fibre.

Layer 6.
- Harris's realization of limit-of-discrete-series forms in H^0 and H^1 of Ω^{(k,2)} (p. 2).
- H̄^i, the image of H^i(Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) → H^i(Ω^{(k,2)}) (p. 108).
- Theorem 15.2.3.1.
- π_f^K ⊂ H^0(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(λ2−λ1−1,2−λ2)}(−D)) for π = π_∞ ⊗ π_f cuspidal automorphic, with π_∞ = π(λ, C) a holomorphic (limit of) discrete series, λ = (λ1, λ2; −λ1 − λ2 + 3) and 0 ≥ λ2 > λ1 (p. 24).
- H^0(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) = ⊕π_f^K for k ≥ 0 and r ≥ 2, over the π_f with π(λ, C) ⊗ π_f cuspidal automorphic, where λ = (1 − k − r, 2 − r; k + 2r) (printed 1 − k + r, E30). This display is printed without multiplicities. State it with the multiplicity of π(λ, C) ⊗ π_f, as in Theorem 15.2.3.1, or cite multiplicity one from ML.4 (conditional).
Each of these is the Siegel instance of a CG20 layer-6 statement:
- H̄^i is interior-cohomology-and-limits;
- Harris's realization and π_f^K ⊂ H^0 are Theorem 5.2 and thm-5-2-1, with automorphic-representation-of-eigenform for the converse;
- the r ≥ 2 decomposition is Theorem 5.2(1) in degree 0;
- Theorem 15.2.3.1 is interior-cohomology-automorphic-description for ω(k+2,2).
Define H̄^i once. Derive Theorem 15.2.3.1 at any neat level from Theorem 5.2, Theorem 15.2.2.1 and Wallach's theorem, instead of stating a second copy.

Layers 7–8, general. This extraction's route critic moves five CG20 items here from GSp4NonregularModularityLifting: lemma-7-10-interior-equals-full, boundary-cohomology-vanishing, arthur-classes-b-f-excluded, case-a-cuspidal-limit-of-discrete-series and h1-h0-dimension-equality. This replaces CG20's "Lemma 7.10 stays". State each once, for m as above. GSp4NonregularModularityLifting relates its non-Eisenstein ideals to these. Everything that rests on boundary vanishing goes in layer 8, after that vanishing, so that CG20's layer numbering is kept.

Layer 7.
- Proposition 15.2.4.1, arthur-classes-b-f-excluded and case-a-cuspidal-limit-of-discrete-series.
- Import from ML.4 (this extraction's source items ext-arthur-classification-gsp4, arthur-classification-nongeneral-type-reducible, ext-schmidt-packet-types-with-limit-of-discrete-series and ext-bhr-archimedean-L-packet):
  - the classification, and multiplicity one for general type;
  - the reducibility of the Galois representations for types (b)–(f);
  - the types whose packets contain π(λ)^h;
  - Π_∞ = {π(λ)^g, π(λ)^h}.
  Layer 7 proves only their application to m.

Layer 8. In this order:
(i) π_*(Ω^{(k,2)}|_D) = ω^{k+2}(−cusp) for k ≠ 0, and ω^2 for k = 0, on the compactified modular curves S^{(1),⋆}_K (p. 109). Hence H^0(Ω^{(k,2)} ⊗ O_D) ≅ H^0(S^{(1),⋆}_K, ω^{k+2}(−cusp)), and ≅ H^0(S^{(1),⋆}_K, ω^2) for k = 0 (printed "if k = 2", E162).
(ii) T_{ℓ,2} = 2T_ℓ on that H^0 (Freitag IV, Satz 4.4; see Acceptance).
(iii) CG20's boundary-cohomology-vanishing, for all i and m as above. Pilloni's H^0(Ω^{(k,2)} ⊗ O_D)_m = 0 for every k ≥ 0 is its degree-0 case, which Pilloni proves from (i) and (ii):
  - An eigensystem on the boundary H^0 comes from an eigenform f. For k ≠ 0 it is cuspidal of weight k+2. For k = 0 it may also be an Eisenstein series of weight 2, whose ρ_f is a sum of two characters.
  - A congruence with Θ_m would give tr ρ̄(Frob_ℓ) = 2 tr ρ̄_f(Frob_ℓ) for all ℓ ∤ Np.
  - Since only T_{ℓ,2} is computed, conclude by Chebotarev and the linear independence of the characters of pairwise non-isomorphic absolutely irreducible representations. This works for every p: ρ̄ is absolutely irreducible of dimension 4, and every constituent of ρ̄_f has dimension ≤ 2. The alternative would be to compute T_{ℓ,0} and T_{ℓ,1} on the boundary as well.
(iv) lemma-7-10-interior-equals-full. Pilloni's injectivity of H^1(Ω^{(k,2)}(−D))_m → H^1(Ω^{(k,2)})_m is its i = 1 case (proof of Corollary 15.2.3.1, from the exact sequence of E157). State it once.
(v) Corollary 15.2.3.1, from Theorem 15.2.3.1 (layer 6) and (iv).
(vi) h1-h0-dimension-equality. For k ≥ R − 1 it follows from Corollary 15.2.3.1 and Proposition 15.2.4.1. CG20 proves it for all a ≥ 2.

Imports. CG18 and CG20 already import:
- AutomorphicBundles B2–B5;
- ShimuraCompactifications C1–C5, including C3 for the independence of Σ ([30] prop. 2.4, source-routed there as coherent-cohomology-independent-of-cone-decomposition) and C5 for X and X^⋆ at level K;
- A0-extension (f^!, traces, fundamental classes, Proposition 4.2.5.1);
- IHG.2;
- ComplexComparisonPartII C2–C3;
- ML.4;
- AF.1 and AF.4. From these this paper uses π(λ, C), π(λ)^h, π(λ)^g, the (𝔭_h, K∞)-cohomology of Harris [30] (printed (𝔭, K∞), E155) and Theorem 15.2.2.1 with V_{(−λ1+1,2;−c)} (E153, E159). They arrive through this extraction's source items def-pi-lambda-h-and-pi-lambda-g, limits-of-discrete-series-gsp4, holomorphic-limit-of-discrete-series, def-relative-lie-algebra-cohomology-p-K, ext-bhr-cohomology-of-limits-of-discrete-series and ext-bhr-uniqueness-for-large-weight.
New imports:
- Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: integral models and reduction (ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII), for Y_Kli(p) and Y_par.
- Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry, Part II: integral boundary charts of Hodge type (ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary), for X_Kli(p), X_par, X^⋆_Kli(p), X^⋆_par and the correspondences at Klingen level over Z_p. That roadmap constructs X^⋆_Kli(p) beside X^⋆_par; the paper uses it on pp. 71–72 and 101 without defining it.
- Smooth representations of local groups (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups) SR.1–SR.4. SR.2–SR.3 supply the Klingen invariants and parameters of §5.1.5 (E24).
- Integral Hecke actions, determinants and interpolation (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants) IHG.3, for m and the GSp4 Hecke polynomial.
- Galois representations attached to modular and Hilbert modular forms (AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations) R19.1, for ρ_f of cuspidal f.
- Arithmetic Galois representations and conductors (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations):
  - R01.1, for reduction, semisimplification and the linear independence of characters behind Brauer–Nesbitt;
  - R01.5, for Chebotarev recognition.
- The Chebotarev density theorem (tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/Chebotarev):
  - layer 4 (cyclotomic Galois characters), for the Eisenstein ρ_f when k = 0 and the GL1 pieces in layers 7–8;
  - layer 10 (Dirichlet-density Chebotarev).
Nothing is imported from HigherHidaAndColemanTheory, SiegelModularFormsModPn or GSp4NonregularModularityLifting.

Consumers (downstream; none is imported):
- Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory), the Part II of PadicFamilies that this extraction proposes. It uses:
  - the §4.3 correspondences and their composition in §§7, 10 and 15.1;
  - Lan's vanishing in §§8.2, 11 and 14.8;
  - the characteristic-0 T_{p,2} and U_{Kli(p),2} in §14.9;
  - the Remark 5.3.1 normalisation in §15.1;
  - layers 4 and 6–8 in §15.2.5.
- Algebraic modular forms, reduction and Serre weights, Part II: Siegel modular forms of genus two modulo p^n (SiegelModularFormsModPn). It proves that its integral T_{p,2} agrees with this one after inverting p.
- Minimal modularity lifting for GSp₄ in non-regular weight (GSp4NonregularModularityLifting). It states Pilloni's Theorem 5.3.1 on layer 3's Hecke action and imports the non-Eisenstein statements of layers 7–8.
- AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity (DESIGN-BCGP18, pending), through HigherHidaAndColemanTheory.

Acceptance.
- Pilloni's T_{ℓ,i} agree with CG18's T_γ and CG20's T_{x,j} on ω(k+r,r), up to a twist computed from Remark 5.3.1 and CG20's Remark 5.10.
- One theorem yields Lan vanishing at spherical, paramodular and Klingen level, over Z_p and modulo p^n.
- For k = 0 the boundary sheaf is ω^2, with no cusp twist, and T_{ℓ,2} = 2T_ℓ holds there.
- T_{ℓ,2} = 2T_ℓ on H^0(Ω^{(k,2)} ⊗ O_D) is checked for Sym^k ⊗ det^2 with the ℓ^{−3} normalisation of §5.3, at level K. Freitag's Siegelsche Modulfunktionen (Grundlehren 254) may treat only scalar weight. If IV, Satz 4.4 does not cover this case, prove the compatibility of the Φ-operator with T_{ℓ,2} for k > 0 directly, or take it from another source.
- For k ≥ R − 1, Corollary 15.2.3.1 and Proposition 15.2.4.1 give CG20's h1-h0-dimension-equality in weight ω(k+2,2). Check whether CG20's argument (Theorem 5.6, Clozel's purity lemma) removes the bound k ≥ R − 1.
routes.reason:
Several parts of the paper are general coherent cohomology of automorphic bundles on Siegel threefolds: Pilloni's §4.3 cohomological correspondences, the Hecke operators of §5.3 and §14.9 with p inverted, Lan's relative vanishing (Theorem 6.2.2.1), Harris's realization and interior cohomology, and the non-Eisenstein statements of §§15.2.3–15.2.4 (Corollary 15.2.3.1, Proposition 15.2.4.1, Eisenstein boundary). They are not steps of the higher Hida or higher Coleman argument.

AutomorphicBundles stops at sections and their Hecke action (B3–B5). No atlas layer plans these statements integrally or in positive degree. B3 plans only the characteristic-0 pushforward to the minimal compactification, which Theorem 6.2.2.1 cites and must agree with.

PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18 already proposes IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes as the Part II of AutomorphicBundles, covering coherent cohomology in every degree with Hecke operators. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 joined it with vanishing, Harris's comparison, discrete-series and boundary layers. A second Part II would give the same objects two owners, against PROTOCOL 15. So this route joins under the same id, parent and title and adds to layers 3–8. Its Siegel statements in layers 6–8 are instances of CG20's and are stated once.

The route critic puts the non-Eisenstein statements here, not in GSp4NonregularModularityLifting. HigherHidaAndColemanTheory needs them for Theorem 15.2.1 and cannot import that roadmap, because that roadmap imports it. So this roadmap imports only upstream proposals (ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII, ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary). HigherHidaAndColemanTheory, SiegelModularFormsModPn and GSp4NonregularModularityLifting import it. What is specific to the paper stays with them: the integral operators at p, the ordinary complexes and Theorem 15.2.1.

routes.title: Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: integral models and reduction
routes.brief:
Joins "Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: integral models and reduction" (ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII; parent ShimuraVarieties). It was proposed by PAPER-KISIN-MADAPUSIPERA-SHIN-22 and joined by PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25, PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26, PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18, PAPER-KISIN-17, PAPER-VANHOFTEN-24, PAPER-GLEASON-LIM-XU-26 and PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24. Those briefs use several titles; this entry uses the FKW24/KPZ26 title, and the design job settles one and merges the briefs. It starts where Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models (ShimuraVarieties) stops, after V8 and V8.general (the joined briefs import V1 and V4–V8). It also goes beyond PELModuli M2 (no level at p; an algebraic space until ShimuraCompactifications C5) and M4 (normalizations only).

Source: V. Pilloni, "Higher coherent cohomology and p-adic modular forms of singular weights", Duke Math. J. 169 (2020) 1647–1807, doi:10.1215/00127094-2019-0075. "p. N" is a page of the author's version of 17 June 2019; the journal's final revision could not be compared. sourceIssues numbers are PAPER-PILLONI-20's. Standing hypotheses (§6.1.1, p. 26): p is any prime, K = K^pK_p is neat and K_p = GSp4(Z_p). V = Z^4 with basis e_1, …, e_4 and the symplectic form J of §5.1 (p. 19): ⟨e_1,e_4⟩ = ⟨e_2,e_3⟩ = 1, and ⟨e_i,e_j⟩ = 0 for the other pairs i < j. Y_n = Y_K ⊗ Z/p^n, and likewise for the other models.

What this paper adds. The Kisin–Pappas brief already requires the Siegel (GSp) lattice-chain moduli at parahoric level "before normalization". This paper adds the genus-two Klingen and paramodular cases, and uses the Siegel-parahoric and Iwahori cases. Build all four as instances of that lattice-chain construction, not a second time, and prove they agree with the descriptions below.

Layer 1: moduli (pp. 20–21, 26–27, 36, 104).
- Functors. Y_K classifies triples (G, λ, ψ) up to prime-to-p quasi-isogeny (p. 26), and Y_Kli(p)_K, defined over Y_K, inherits this. Y_par,K classifies isomorphism classes. Use PELModuli M1's comparison of these functors so that p_2 is well defined. "Subgroup of order p" means a finite locally free subgroup scheme of rank p.
- Kli(p) is the set of elements of GSp4(Z_p) whose reduction lies in P_Kli(F_p), the stabilizer of ⟨e_1⟩ (p. 21). P. 20 prints "stabilizes P_W"; read "stabilizes W" (sourceIssues E21).
- p_1: Y_Kli(p)_K → Y_K is the moduli space of order-p subgroups H ⊂ G[p] (p. 26). The chain G → G/H → G/H^⊥ → G composes to multiplication by p, with ⊥ taken for the Weil pairing of λ on G[p].
- Y_par,K is the moduli space of (G', λ', ψ), where λ' is a Z_(p)^×-multiple of a polarization of degree p^2 (p. 26).
- Representability. Y_Kli(p)_K is the closed subscheme of the relative Hilbert scheme of G[p] → Y_K (R09.2) parametrizing finite locally free subgroup schemes of rank p, so p_1 is projective. Y_par,K is outside M2, whose good-prime hypotheses require an invertible polarization defect: prove that it is a quasi-projective scheme over Z_p, either as part of the lattice-chain construction or by Zarhin's trick into a principally polarized Siegel space of genus 16 (M5), as p. 29 does.
- p_2 sends (G, λ, H, ψ) to (G/H^⊥, λ', ψ'), where λ' descends p^2λ along G → G/H^⊥ and ψ' is induced by G[N] = (G/H^⊥)[N] for every N prime to p.
- Put G' = G/H^⊥. Prove (G')^t ≅ G/H; that K(λ') ⊂ G'[p] has rank p^2 (type (1, p)); and that there is a unique isogeny λ'^t: (G')^t → G' with λ'^t∘λ' = p. This is the map the paper calls the polarization λ^t (p. 36), not the transpose of λ'; p. 104 uses it, unnamed, as the degree-p^2 map (G')^t → G' of the universal chain. P. 36 prints its target as G (sourceIssues E50). Then G → G/H ≅ (G')^t → G' → G has degrees p, p^2, p (p. 104).
- Siegel-parahoric instance (reduction in the stabilizer of ⟨e_1, e_2⟩): C_{p,2} → Y_K, the moduli of totally isotropic subgroup schemes L ⊂ G[p] of rank p^2, with the isogeny G → G/L and the polarization of G/L descended from pλ (again a Z_(p)^×-multiple of a polarization of degree prime to p, principal when λ is), so that both projections land in Y_K (§14.9.2, p. 104). It is projective over Y_K (R09.2). ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary imports it for the compactified C_{p,2}.
- Iwahori instance: the moduli of flags H_1 ⊂ H_2 ⊂ G[p] of subgroup schemes of ranks p and p^2, with H_2 totally isotropic. SiegelModularFormsModPn imports it, with its local model (Layer 2), for the embeddings in the proof of Lemma 6.4.2 (p. 36).
- Generic fibres. Let V_1 = pe_1Z ⊕ e_2Z ⊕ e_3Z ⊕ e_4Z and K_par = GSp(V_1)(Z_p) (GSp'_4 of p. 27). The paper states (Y_{K,Z(p)} × C)^an ≃ S_K only at spherical level (p. 26). Prove that the generic fibres of Y_Kli(p)_K and Y_par,K are the base changes to Q_p of the canonical models of levels K^pKli(p) and K^pK_par, in the convention fixed in Layer 2 (with that of p. 27, Kli(p) = GSp4(Z_p) ∩ K_par). Identify p_1 ⊗ Q_p and p_2 ⊗ Q_p with the level maps of ShimuraVarieties V8, together with any central Hecke translation that the chosen normalizations introduce. IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes and HigherHidaAndColemanTheory use this for the ⊗C statements at Klingen level (pp. 102–103).
- Ownership. The subgroup-scheme moduli of Lagrangians in G[p] (CG20's β_{p,1}) and the finiteness statements of Layer 3 are owned here. CG20's SiegelModularFormsModPn layer 4 imports them. It keeps its β_{p,2} correspondence (isotropic subgroups of A[p^2], not a parahoric level) and the operators.

Layer 2: local geometry (pp. 26–27).
- Prove Proposition 6.1.4.1 (pp. 26–27) as printed: "The scheme Y_K is smooth over Spec Z_p. The schemes Y_par,K and Y_Kli(p)_K are regular schemes. They are flat, local complete intersections over Spec Z_p. The non smooth locus of Y_par,K consists of a finite set of characteristic p points." Import the first sentence from PELModuli M2 (smoothness) and ShimuraCompactifications C5 (scheme structure and quasi-projectivity). Derive the last sentence from the local-model diagram: L_0 below is fixed by the paramodular group scheme, so the non-smooth locus is the image of the fibre over L_0 and has dimension 0. Do not use the finiteness of the superspecial set, which SiegelModularFormsModPn owns.
- Paramodular local model (p. 27). It is the moduli space of rank-2 direct factors L ⊂ V_1 ⊗ Z_p that are totally isotropic for the restriction of J. It is regular. Its only point where it is not smooth over Z_p (the paper's "only singularity") is L_0 = ⟨pe_1, e_4⟩ ⊂ V_1 ⊗ F_p, the radical of the form on V_1 ⊗ F_p. The deformation ring at L_0 is Z_p[[X,Y,W,Z]]/(XY − WZ + p), with universal deformation ⟨pe_1 + Xe_2 + We_3, Ze_2 + Ye_3 + e_4⟩.
- The paper only cites Tilouine [79] (Doc. Math. 2006), §2.2, Thm 3, for Klingen level, and de Jong [17] (J. Algebraic Geom. 1993) and Yu [86] (Taiwanese J. Math. 2010), Thm 4.4, for paramodular level. Plan both local-model diagrams.
  - Paramodular: for the chain {p^kV_1, p^kV_1^∨}, identify this Grassmannian with the naive local model. It is flat, because it is cut out of Gr(2,4) over Z_p by one section of O(1) that is nonzero on the special fibre.
  - Klingen: use the self-dual periodic chain generated by Λ ⊂ V, where Λ = e_1Z ⊕ e_2Z ⊕ e_3Z ⊕ pe_4Z; its stabilizer in GSp4(Z_p) is Kli(p) of p. 21. The group Γ_Kli(p) of p. 27 stabilizes V_1 ⊂ V. Since V_1/pV = ⟨e_2, e_3, e_4⟩ = ⟨e_4⟩^⊥, its p-component is the conjugate of Kli(p) by w: e_1 ↦ e_4, e_4 ↦ −e_1 (fixing e_2 and e_3). This is a convention, not an error in the paper; fix one convention.
  - Prove that the naive Klingen local model is flat with reduced special fibre (Görtz, flatness of local models for the symplectic group, for symplectic lattice chains). Check that the cited results cover p = 2, since §6.1 allows any prime. Prove that it equals the local model of GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII, whose Kisin–Pappas lane plans symplectic chains and reduced special fibres.
  - Do the same for the Siegel-parahoric and Iwahori chains. For Iwahori level, recover the special-fibre strata of [62] (Pilloni, Duke Math. J. 157 (2011)), pp. 186–189, which SiegelModularFormsModPn uses in Lemma 6.4.2.
  - The codimension bullet of Layer 3 uses the reducedness of these special fibres.

Layer 3: maps between levels (interior part of §7.1, p. 38; pp. 60, 104).
- G → G' has degree p^3 and G' → G has degree p. p_1 forgets G' and p_2 forgets G.
- The non-smooth loci of Y_Kli(p)_K and Y_par,K lie in the non-ordinary part of the special fibre and have codimension ≥ 2. Take the codimension from the reduced special fibres of the local models (Layer 2), not from p-rank strata.
- At a geometric point x of Y_1, the fibre of p_1 is the set of order-p subgroup schemes of G_x[p]. It has 2p + 2 points if G_x is ordinary, 3 if G_x has p-rank 1, and 1 if G_x has p-rank 0 and a-number 1; it is a P^1 if G_x is superspecial (α_p × α_p ⊂ G_x[p]). So p_1 has finite fibres over the points of p-rank ≥ 1 (used on p. 60), all its fibres have dimension ≤ 1, and p_1 is not quasi-finite over the p-rank-0 locus Y_1^{=0}. HigherHidaAndColemanTheory combines this fibre bound with the dimension of the p-rank-0 locus (dimension 1; sourceIssues E48), which it imports from SiegelModularFormsModPn, for the codimension-2 claim in the proof of Lemma 14.9.2 (sourceIssues E143).
- At a geometric point (G', λ') of Y_par,1, the fibre of p_2 is the set of order-p subgroup schemes C ⊂ K(λ'), with G = G'/C. Every such C is isotropic for the pairing on K(λ'), so G'/C carries a polarization of degree prime to p and every C occurs.
