The generic degree of p_2 is p + 1, and its fibre is a P^1 where K(λ') ≅ α_p × α_p. Exhibit such points of p-rank 0 in Y_par,1 (expected over L_0), so that p_2 is not quasi-finite over Y_{par,1}^{=0}. P. 38 prints X_par^{=0} (sourceIssues E51).
- At a geometric point x of Y_1, the fibre of C_{p,2} → Y_K is the set of Lagrangian subgroup schemes of G_x[p]. It is finite when G_x has p-rank ≥ 1 (p. 104 uses this through the finiteness of (C_{p,2})^{≥1} → 𝔛^{≥1}).
- State these facts at geometric points, reading the p-rank and a-number from the Dieudonné module (R07.2). "Ordinary" and "non-ordinary" in the codimension bullet are read the same way. The loci Y_n^{=r}, Y_n^{≤r} and Y_n^{≥r} as subschemes, their dimensions and the superspecial set belong to SiegelModularFormsModPn.
- The compactified statements (the normal lci X's, the proper extensions of p_1 and p_2, footnote 9) belong to ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary.

Imports (all upstream; none of them imports this route):
- Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models (ShimuraVarieties) V5, V6 and V8.
- Siegel and PEL moduli problems (PELModuli) M1–M5.
- Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry (ShimuraCompactifications) C5, for the scheme structure and quasi-projectivity of Y_K. C5 is an atlas stage and does not import this route, so no cycle arises.
- Abelian Schemes And Arithmetic Moduli (AbelianSchemesAndArithmeticModuli) A2–A4.
- Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory) R07.1, R07.2 and R07.6.
- Algebraic moduli and representability for arithmetic geometry (AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry) R09.1, R09.2 and R09.6.
- Commutative algebra for deformation theory and patching (DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra) R03.3.
- Reductive groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models (ReductiveGroupsPartII) RG2.3, for the Klingen, paramodular, Siegel-parahoric and Iwahori group schemes of the local-model diagrams.
- GeometricSatakeLocalModelsPartII (parent GeometricSatakeAndFusion, "Geometric Satake over the Fargues–Fontaine curve"). PAPER-KISIN-ZHOU-25 proposed it as "Geometric Satake over the Fargues–Fontaine curve, Part II: integral local models and residue-field curves". PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-ZHOU-26, PAPER-KISIN-PAPPAS-18 and PAPER-GLEASON-LIM-XU-26 joined it under other subtitles, and the van Hoften and Zhu extractions import it. Use its symplectic-chain and reduced-special-fibre lane.
It imports no other Pilloni route.

Consumers (downstream; never imported):
- ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary: Y_Kli(p)_K, Y_par,K, p_1, p_2 and the chain; the local models and Proposition 6.1.4.1, used in the proof of Theorem 6.1.5.1(4) (p. 29); and the Lagrangian moduli, for the compactified C_{p,2}.
- IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes: Y_Kli and Y_par, and the generic-fibre identification at Klingen level.
- SiegelModularFormsModPn: Proposition 6.1.4.1 in Lemma 6.4.1 (p. 35); the paramodular chain (sourceIssues E50) and the Iwahori moduli and local model in Lemma 6.4.2 (p. 36); and the Lagrangian moduli and their finiteness (CG20's β_{p,1}).
- HigherHidaAndColemanTheory:
  - T_1' and T_2' (§7.1), and Lemma 7.1.1 (p. 38), which uses the normality of X_Kli(p) (from ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary, whose interior case is Proposition 6.1.4.1).
  - Lemma 10.2.2 (p. 59), which uses that 𝔛_Kli(p) is lci over Spf Z_p (Theorem 6.1.5.1(4); its interior case is Proposition 6.1.4.1). Through it, Lemma 10.3.1 (p. 60), which needs only the interior. There the Cohen–Macaulay source is the fibre product ℭ_𝔜(p^m), which Lemma 10.2.2 does not cover (sourceIssues E75), and the miracle-flatness citation is misprinted (E76). Its quasi-finiteness needs the finiteness of order-p subgroups at points of p-rank ≥ 1 (Layer 3). Its regular target 𝔜^{≥1}_Kli(p^m) is étale over the smooth p-rank ≥ 1 locus of Y_K (E75), so that regularity uses the smoothness of Y_K, not the regularity of Y_Kli(p)_K.
  - Lemma 14.9.2 (p. 103), through the fibres of p_1 (E143).
  - The ⊗C statements at Klingen level (pp. 102–103), through the generic-fibre identification.
- Through HigherHidaAndColemanTheory: GSp4NonregularModularityLifting and the pending AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity (DESIGN-BCGP18).

Acceptance tests:
- Z_p[[X,Y,W,Z]]/(XY − WZ + p) is regular of dimension 4 and has a singular special fibre.
- The displayed module is isotropic exactly when XY − WZ + p = 0.
- The special fibre of the paramodular local model is {L : L ∩ ⟨pe_1, e_4⟩ ≠ 0}, a Schubert divisor in Gr(2,4): irreducible, reduced, of dimension 3, and singular only at L_0.
- w (e_1 ↦ e_4, e_4 ↦ −e_1, fixing e_2 and e_3) preserves J and carries Λ to V_1.
- p_1 has generic degree p^3 + p^2 + p + 1, p_2 has generic degree p + 1, and C_{p,2} → Y_K has generic degree (p + 1)(p^2 + 1).
- An ordinary point of Y_1(F̄_p) has exactly 2p + 2 subgroups of order p, and a p-rank-1 point has exactly 3.
- The degrees p, p^2, p of G → (G')^t → G' → G multiply to p^4, the degree of [p] on an abelian surface.
routes.reason:
Pilloni's §6.1 builds integral models of the Siegel threefold at Klingen and paramodular level at p: their moduli interpretation, local models, regularity and lci, singular loci, and the maps p_1 and p_2 between levels. The paper also uses the Siegel-parahoric (Lagrangian) and Iwahori moduli (pp. 36, 104) and, at Klingen level, the comparison of the generic fibre with the complex Shimura variety (pp. 102–103). This mathematics lies in the direction of Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models (ShimuraVarieties), which stops at generic-fibre canonical models (V8), and the atlas does not plan it. PELModuli M2 requires no level at p and an invertible polarization defect, and gives an algebraic space that becomes a scheme only through ShimuraCompactifications C5. M4 allows only normalizations, with no moduli interpretation and no universal abelian scheme.

A proposal in this direction already exists: ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII, from PAPER-KISIN-MADAPUSIPERA-SHIN-22, joined by the Kisin–Zhou, Kisin–Pappas(–Zhou), Kisin, van Hoften, Gleason–Lim–Xu and Farb–Kisin–Wolfson extractions. Its Kisin–Pappas brief already requires the Siegel lattice-chain moduli at parahoric level before normalization, and local-model diagrams. PROTOCOL §15 gives each piece of mathematics one owner. So this route joins that proposal with the same id, parent and title; the joined briefs use several titles, and the design job settles one. It adds only the genus-two instances and the facts that the paper's other routes use.

Following the route critic, the compactifications go to ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary, which imports this route. The Hasse invariants and p-rank strata go to SiegelModularFormsModPn and HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T0. The cohomological use of p_1 and p_2 goes to HigherHidaAndColemanTheory. This route is upstream of every other Pilloni route and imports none of them. The sibling briefs import the Siegel-parahoric and Iwahori moduli from it (the compactification route for C_{p,2}, SiegelModularFormsModPn for Lemma 6.4.2), and the compactification route must not import SiegelModularFormsModPn, so this route owns them. CG20's SiegelModularFormsModPn then imports the Lagrangian moduli instead of building them. This route states its p-rank facts at geometric points, through R07.2, and leaves the p-rank loci as subschemes to SiegelModularFormsModPn, which keeps the dependency graph acyclic.

routes.title: Minimal modularity lifting for GSp₄ in non-regular weight
routes.brief:
Joins GSp4NonregularModularityLifting, a new roadmap proposed by PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 (CG20): same id and title, no parent. It lists what V. Pilloni, "Higher coherent cohomology and p-adic modular forms of singular weights", Duke Math. J. 169 (2020) 1647–1807, doi:10.1215/00127094-2019-0075, adds; the design job merges both briefs. Pages: author version of 17 June 2019; the paywalled final revision (15 Oct 2019) was not compared. sourceIssues are PAPER-PILLONI-20's unless marked CG20's.

Final statement, as printed. Theorem 5.3.1 (p. 25; also p. 2). Let K ⊂ GSp₄(A_f) be neat (§5.2.1), (k,r) ∈ Z≥0 × Z, N the product of the primes ℓ with K_ℓ ≠ GSp₄(Z_ℓ), and H^N = ⊗′_{ℓ∤N} H_ℓ with the §5.3 normalisation T_{ℓ,2} = ℓ⁻³T′_{ℓ,2}, T_{ℓ,i} = ℓ⁻⁶T′_{ℓ,i} (i = 0, 1). Let Θ: H^N → C be a system of eigenvalues on H^i(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,r)}) or on H^i(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)). Then the image of Θ generates a number field E. For every finite place λ of E there is a semisimple continuous ρ_{Θ,λ}: G_Q → GL₄(Ē_λ), unramified away from N and the prime p below λ, with det(1 − Xρ_{Θ,λ}(Frob_ℓ)) = Θ(Q_ℓ(X)) for all ℓ ∤ Np (geometric Frobenius).

Corrections.
- D = S^tor_{K,Σ} ∖ S_K (E29), and T′_{ℓ,i} maps p₂⋆Ω^{(k,r)} to p₁^!Ω^{(k,r)} (E32). Both are applied where IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes defines D (its notation) and the H^N-action (layer 3), and are imported here.
- The proof on p. 25 prints λ = (1−k−r, 2−r; k+2r) correctly. The p. 24 display prints 1−k+r (E30), and IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes (layer 6) corrects it.
- For r ≥ 2 the twist of Remark 5.3.1 makes the smallest expected Hodge–Tate weight 0 (E31). For r < 2 the expected weight r − 2 is negative.
- Theorem 5.3.1 is GL₄-valued. AG2.2 owns Theorem 5.1.7.1(5) and its correction E27. For an absolutely irreducible residual representation, the symplectic form comes from CG20's Lemma 6.9(2) (layer 2).

Additions, by CG20 layer:
- Layer 2.
  - Placement. Theorem 5.3.1 goes beside Proposition 6.6 and Lemma 6.9 (CG20 layer 2; Theorem 6.13 is in layer 3).
  - The proof of Theorem 5.3.1. Import H⁰(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) = ⊕π_f^K (r ≥ 2, λ corrected by E30) from IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes layer 6. For k ≥ 0 and r ≥ 3, Theorem 5.1.7.1 (AG2.2, AG2.5) then gives the theorem for the Θ occurring in H⁰(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)); the printed proof checks nothing more. The general case (the other degrees, the sheaf Ω^{(k,r)} without −D, and the other weights) follows from Pilloni–Stroh [63] by p-adic interpolation (Taylor [76] already treats degree-0 cuspidal cohomology). State [63] with its hypotheses and plan its proof here.
  - The number field E. Request from IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes layer 3, which owns the H^N-action, that the action be defined on the canonical models over Q (from its imports ShimuraCompactifications C2–C3 and AutomorphicBundles B2–B3). This gives a Hecke-stable Q-structure on H^i(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,r)}) and on H^i(S^tor_{K,Σ}, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)). Here, prove only that the eigensystems of a commuting family of endomorphisms of a finite-dimensional Q-vector space generate number fields, and deduce the first claim of Theorem 5.3.1.
  - Hasse-invariant congruences. Plan this argument once, in the generality of [63], taking the Siegel Ha and its lifts from SiegelModularFormsModPn. Where [63] covers CG20's torsion Hecke algebras T^an_μ(Q), derive Lemma 6.9(1) and Remark 6.10 from it. Otherwise, say which of the two uses the other.
  - Dictionary. Import Ω^{(k,r)} = ω(k+r,r) from IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes (layer 3). Import from the same layer the comparison of Pilloni's T_{ℓ,i} with CG20's T_{x,j}: T_{ℓ,2}↔T_{x,1}, T_{ℓ,1}↔T_{x,2} and T_{ℓ,0}↔S_x, up to the twist of Remark 5.3.1 and CG20's Remark 5.10. Import the conversion of det(1 − Xρ(Frob_ℓ)) = Q_ℓ(X) to det(X − r(Frob_x)) = Q_x(X) from IHG.3. Neither is proved here.
  - The de Rham property (p. 5). Eigenforms in H⁰(M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Z_p) are classical (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory). Pilloni says "one often knows" that their Galois representations, the ρ_{Θ,λ} of Theorem 5.3.1 in weight (k,2), are de Rham ([54], Prop. 4.16). State Mok's hypotheses exactly.
  - Remark 5.3.2 goes to ML.0.
    - Its de Rham, crystalline and Hodge–Tate-weight expectation (0, r−2, r+k−1, k+2r−3) is conjectural.
    - Its Newton-above-Hodge statement is V. Lafforgue's theorem [45] in cohomological weight (footnote 5: r ≠ 2, k+r ≠ 1, k+2r ≠ 3).
    - ML.0 registers the remark as a predicate on pairs (Θ, ρ) with det(1 − Xρ(Frob_ℓ)) = Θ(Q_ℓ(X)), without importing this roadmap. This roadmap imports ML.4, which has ML.0 as an input, so an import the other way would make a cycle.
  - The non-Eisenstein equivalence. Record that a maximal ideal m ⊂ H^{Np} supporting coherent cohomology, or HigherHidaAndColemanTheory's M, is non-Eisenstein (Definition 6.11) exactly when m = m_ρ̄ for an absolutely irreducible ρ̄ (IHG.3).
    - Here r̄_m comes from Theorem 5.3.1 by reduction and Brauer–Nesbitt, as in Lemma 6.9(1). When m occurs only in torsion cohomology, it goes through the Hasse-invariant congruences above.
    - "Non-Eisenstein ⇒ m = m_ρ̄ with ρ̄: G_Q → GSp₄(F̄_p)" uses Lemma 6.9(2), which rests on Arthur's classification and the Bellaïche–Chenevier sign theorem. So it carries Arthur's classification as a named hypothesis for as long as ML.4 keeps it conditional.
    - The converse uses Chebotarev and Brauer–Nesbitt.
    - The equivalence holds for every m obeying §15.2's rule, or once ℓ³Θ_m(T_{ℓ,0}) = ν(ρ̄(Frob_ℓ)) is added (E149, E150).
- Layer 8, comparisons:
  - (a) Pilloni 2012 ([61], pp. 5–6).
    - What it says. "Under many technical assumptions", a residually modular abelian surface arises from a p-adic modular form. Its Taylor–Wiles system lets Galois deformation rings act on H⁰(𝔛^{≥2}_{Kli}(p)_K, Ω^{(0,2)}(−D))^{ord′}. This is the module of ordinary p-adic forms of weight (0,2) on 𝔛^{≥2}_{Kli}(p)_K, the ordinary locus in 𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p)_K.
    - Why it works there. Congruences are unobstructed for these forms. In classical weight (0,2) they are obstructed, because H¹ does not vanish (E4).
    - What to do. State [61] with every hypothesis, taken from [61] itself, and plan its proof. Patch this module, which is M′ ⊗_{Λ₂,(0,2)} Z_p from HigherHidaAndColemanTheory layer 1, over R03.5. Use GlobalGaloisDeformations G7's deformation conditions and Taylor–Wiles primes ([61], proof of Prop. 5.6, which CG20 already sends to GlobalGaloisDeformations G7). Use CG20's layer-6 Taylor–Wiles levels where they match those of [61]. Take the remaining steps from [61].
  - (b) Calegari–Geraghty (p. 6) is Theorem 9.1 in weight (2,2), which is Pilloni's (0,2).
    - Pilloni calls the vanishing "in degree greater or equal than 2" unknown (p. 6).
    - In CG20 it is hypothesis (6) of Theorem 9.1: H²(X_i(Q), ω(2,2)(−∞)_k)_{m_∅} = 0 for every Q satisfying Assumption 6.12(2). Assumption 7.7 is its form at X_Δ(Q).
    - It is open in weight (2,2).
  - (c) HigherHidaAndColemanTheory owns the replacement H⁰(M ⊗^L_{Λ,0} Q_p/Z_p) (E3). DESIGN-BCGP18 owns its patching.

Amendment to CG20's layer 7 (route critic).
- Five items move, with CG20's E81–E83: lemma-7-10-interior-equals-full, boundary-cohomology-vanishing, arthur-classes-b-f-excluded, case-a-cuspidal-limit-of-discrete-series and h1-h0-dimension-equality.
- They go to layer 7 of Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes (IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes, proposed by PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-18). They are stated there for m = m_ρ̄ and imported here, and layer 7 applies them to CG20's non-Eisenstein ideals through the layer-2 equivalence.
- Lemma 7.9, Theorem 7.11 and its reduction to the dimension inequality stay in layer 7.
- AdjointSelmerGroupsFromModularityLifting imports Lemma 7.10 and the Arthur-type lemma from IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes, not from this roadmap.

Imports.
- Proposals, not atlas roadmaps:
  - Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory, proposed by this extraction, PAPER-PILLONI-20). This paper uses its degree-0 Siegel Hida theory (M′ and ord′, its layer 1) and Theorems 1.1–1.2.
  - CG20 already imports IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes and SiegelModularFormsModPn. From IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes this paper adds: the dictionary, D, the H^N-action, H⁰ = ⊕π_f^K, the Q-structure request and the moved layer-7 items. From SiegelModularFormsModPn it uses the Siegel Ha and its lifts, which CG20 already imports ("Hasse invariants"), now also for [63].
- Atlas roadmaps beyond CG20's:
  - Integral Hecke actions, determinants and interpolation (IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants) IHG.3.
  - Hodge–Tate theory, canonical subgroups, and automorphic period maps (HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups) T0 (Ha of a BT₁), for [63].
- CG20 already imports IHG.1, AG2.2, AG2.5, G7, R03.5 and ML.4, which this paper also uses. ML.0 is not imported.

Consumers:
- AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity (DESIGN-BCGP18, pending).
- Selmer groups, continuous integral cohomology, and Iwasawa cohomology, Part II: adjoint Bloch–Kato Selmer groups from modularity lifting (AdjointSelmerGroupsFromModularityLifting, proposed by PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20).

Acceptance tests:
- Theorem 5.3.1 for H¹(Ω^{(0,2)}(−D)).
- For k ≥ 0 and r ≥ 3, on cuspidal H⁰, Θ(Q_ℓ(X)) agrees with CG20 Proposition 6.8(2)'s λ_f(Q_x(X)) under the imported dictionary. The similitude check is AG2.2's: χ_p^{3−k−2r}·(finite), from Theorem 5.1.7.1(5) with E27, against Proposition 6.8(1).
- p odd and tr ρ̄(Frob_ℓ) = 0. The rule (owned by IHG.3) allows Θ_m(T_{ℓ,0}) = ±ℓ⁻³ν(ρ̄(Frob_ℓ)). The equivalence must hold for each resulting m that supports cohomology, and only one of them satisfies ℓ³Θ_m(T_{ℓ,0}) = ν(ρ̄(Frob_ℓ)).
routes.reason:
The route has four items, in two groups:
- Galois representations attached to Hecke eigensystems in the coherent cohomology of every weight, singular weights included: Theorem 5.3.1, and the de Rham property of the weight-(k,2) forms.
- Two GSp₄ modularity lifting theorems: Pilloni 2012 and Calegari–Geraghty.

CG20's proposal GSp4NonregularModularityLifting already owns this material: Taylor's congruence constructions (Proposition 6.6, Lemma 6.9, Theorem 6.13), the non-Eisenstein notion (Definition 6.11) and Theorem 9.1. So the route joins that proposal with the same id and title (PROTOCOL 15), rather than proposing a rival roadmap.

No atlas layer owns these items. AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (AG2.2, AG2.5, AG2.6) builds only regular polarized systems and proves de Rham only for them. CG20 sends only Mok's discrete-series case there. So Theorem 5.3.1 (singular weights, all degrees) and the de Rham property of limits of discrete series get one owner, here.

What upstream roadmaps own is imported, not planned again:
- from IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes: the Ω/ω dictionary, D, the H^N-action and H⁰ = ⊕π_f^K, with E29, E30 and E32 applied there;
- from IHG.3: the Hecke-polynomial conversion;
- from AG2.2: Theorem 5.1.7.1(5) with E27;
- from SiegelModularFormsModPn: the Siegel Hasse invariant.
Remark 5.3.2 is registered at ML.0, which must not import this roadmap: this roadmap imports ML.4, and ML.4 has ML.0 as an input.

The dependency order fixes the place:
- HigherHidaAndColemanTheory is upstream, because Pilloni 2012 needs its degree-0 Siegel Hida theory. HigherHidaAndColemanTheory states Theorem 1.2 for m_ρ̄ (IHG.3) and never imports this roadmap.
- IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes and SiegelModularFormsModPn are also upstream, and SiegelModularFormsModPn sends its Galois statements here.
- Following the route critic, CG20's Lemma 7.10 group moves to IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes, so that HigherHidaAndColemanTheory can use it without importing this roadmap.

Pilloni cites Pilloni 2012 and the Calegari–Geraghty theorem as motivation. Pilloni 2012 is a GSp₄ modularity lifting theorem for ordinary p-adic forms, which is this roadmap's subject. So the roadmap states it and plans its proof on HigherHidaAndColemanTheory's degree-0 Hida theory, with the Taylor–Wiles primes that CG20 already sends to GlobalGaloisDeformations G7. The Calegari–Geraghty theorem is Theorem 9.1 in weight (2,2).

Boxer–Pilloni, "Higher Hida theory for Siegel modular forms" (Invent. Math. 2026), extends the families to the whole weight space. It is a future source of HigherHidaAndColemanTheory, not of this roadmap. AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity (DESIGN-BCGP18) consumes both this roadmap and HigherHidaAndColemanTheory.

routes.title: Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry, Part II: integral boundary charts of Hodge type
routes.brief:
This route joins "Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry, Part II: integral boundary charts of Hodge type" (ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary; parent ShimuraCompactifications), proposed by PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24 and joined by PAPER-MAULIK-SHANKAR-TANG-22 (same id, parent and title); the design job merges the three briefs. Keep the existing briefs' statements (Madapusi Pera's charts, smooth 𝒮^tor) under their hyperspecial hypothesis. Add the Klingen and paramodular Siegel cases as separate layers whose models are normal and lci but not smooth.

Source: V. Pilloni, "Higher coherent cohomology and p-adic modular forms of singular weights", Duke Math. J. 169 (2020) 1647–1807, doi:10.1215/00127094-2019-0075. "p. N" is a page of the author's version of 17 June 2019 (the journal's final revision was not compared). sourceIssues numbers below are PAPER-PILLONI-20's.

First prerequisite: Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry (ShimuraCompactifications), whose C5 compactifies PEL moduli integrally only at good level (its p-power normalizations serve perfectoid towers); the earlier briefs add Hodge type at hyperspecial level. Pilloni's additions start there. They concern the Siegel threefold at Klingen and paramodular level at p, and the compactified T_{p,2}-correspondence C_{p,2} over Z_p. Standing hypotheses: K = K^pK_p neat, K_p = GSp4(Z_p) (sourceIssues E2: the introduction omits "neat"). The paper follows Faltings–Chai, Degeneration of abelian varieties (1990); Lan, Arithmetic compactifications of PEL-type Shimura varieties (2013) §6.2; Lan, Forum Math. Sigma 4 (2016) e1; Lan, IMRN 2017(11) 3237–3280, Thm 6.1 and Prop. 7.5; and Stroh, Bull. SMF 138 (2010) 259–315.

Layer P1, parahoric boundary charts (§6.1.5.1–6.1.5.3, pp. 27–29).
Imported: the groups Γ, Γ_Kli(p), Γ_par (PELModuli M0; ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3); the conical complex, P_W and P_{W,h} (C0–C1; P_{W,h} ⊂ P_W is the inverse image of M_{W,h}, sourceIssues E33); rational polyhedral, admissible and good cone decompositions and their refinements (C0); the hyperspecial tower M_{W,γ} → B_{W,γ} → Y_{W,γ} (C4–C5).
New here, for W ∈ ℭ and γ ∈ GSp4(A_f^p)/K^p:
- the towers M_{W,γ,Kli(p)} → B_{W,γ,Kli(p)} → Y_{W,γ,Kli(p)} and M_{W,γ,par} → B_{W,γ,par} → Y_{W,γ,par};
- for par: 1-motives with a polarization of degree Np², (N,p) = 1, whose toric part has character group ≅ V_1/W^⊥;
- for Kli(p): a Klingen structure on the base, depending on the position of W relative to V_1 (footnote 7, p. 28);
- M̄ and Z for these towers;
- the integral structures of T_{W,γ,Kli(p)} and T_{W,γ,par};
- condition 3 of "good" for H = Γ_Kli(p), Γ_par.
Corrections: the level structure is K^p-level, not K_p (sourceIssues E34); the abelian part has genus 2 − rank_Z W (sourceIssues E35); B_{W,γ,par} lies over Y_{W,γ,par} (sourceIssues E35, E37); the lattices printed in Sym²(V/W^⊥) ⊗ Q are character groups X^⋆(T), cones lie in X_⋆(T)_R, and smooth means the s_i extend to a Z-basis of X_⋆(T) (sourceIssues E36); condition 3 reads "If H = Γ (resp. Γ_par, resp. Γ_Kli(p))" (sourceIssues E38).

Level K (applies to P2–P4). At level K, (1), (4), X^⋆ and Ω^(k,r) on X are C5's (with AutomorphicBundles B3), and (2) is C3's on C5's models. At level K, the sourceIssues E40-corrected identity (Rπ)_*I' = I also belongs to C3, as its separate higher-direct-image theorem. This roadmap plans the Kli(p) and par cases.

Layer P2, compactifications (Theorem 6.1.5.1(1), (4), p. 29). As printed: "Let Σ be a good polyhedral cone decomposition which is Γ (resp. Γ_Kli(p), resp. Γ_par)-admissible. There is a toroidal compactification X_{K,Σ} of Y_K (resp. X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ} of Y_Kli(p)_K, resp. X_{par,K,Σ} of Y_{par,K}). It has a stratification indexed by Γ\Σ (resp. Γ_Kli(p)\Σ, resp. Γ_par\Σ)." The (σ,γ)-stratum is isomorphic to Z_{W,γ,σ} (resp. Z_{W,γ,Kli(p),σ}, resp. Z_{W,γ,par,σ}; the printed order is swapped, sourceIssues E39), and the completion along Z_{W,γ,σ} is that of M̄_{W,γ,σ} along Z_{W,γ,σ} (likewise for Kli(p), par). The boundary, the reduced complement of Y, is a relative Cartier divisor. (4): "If Σ is Γ (resp. Γ_Kli(p), resp. Γ_par)-admissible, then the toroidal compactification X_{K,Σ} of Y_K (resp. X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ} of Y_Kli(p)_K, resp. X_{par,K,Σ} of Y_{par,K}) is normal and a local complete intersection over Spec Z_p." In (2)–(4), Σ and Σ' are also good. P. 29 makes this a standing convention ("In the sequel of the paper we will consider mostly H-admissible rational polyhedral cone decompositions which satisfy these extra properties unless explicitly stated"), and (1) constructs the compactifications only for good Σ. Notation X, X_Kli(p), X_par (the printed list is permuted, sourceIssues E41).
Proof route (p. 29; the theorem is "a special case of" Lan IMRN 2017, Thm 6.1): X_{K,Σ} from Faltings–Chai. X_{par,K,Σ}: embed Y_{par,K} in a genus-16 principally polarized Siegel space by Zarhin's trick, compactify by Faltings–Chai, normalize. X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ}: Stroh 2010, or normalize a toroidal compactification of Y_{par,K} × Y_K. Parts (1)–(3) from Lan IMRN 2017 Thm 6.1 and Prop. 7.5. Part (4) from the charts, Proposition 6.1.4.1 and "our knowledge of modular curves". These are the rank-one chart bases: of level away from p at level K and for par (p. 28), and of level Γ0(p) in some Klingen cases (cf. p. 61).

Layer P3, functoriality (Theorem 6.1.5.1(2), (3), p. 29; §7.1, p. 38; §14.9.2, p. 104).
- (2): for a refinement Σ' of Σ (printed "Σ' ⊂ Σ"), a projective π: X_{K,Σ'} → X_{K,Σ} with (Rπ)_*O = O. The printed π^*I_{X_{K,Σ}} = I_{X_{K,Σ'}} is false whenever Σ' ≠ Σ; state (Rπ)_*I_{X_{K,Σ'}} = I_{X_{K,Σ}}, with only π^*I_{X_{K,Σ}} ⊂ I_{X_{K,Σ'}} (sourceIssues E40). This roadmap proves both statements for X_par and X_Kli(p).
- (3): for a Γ_Kli(p)-admissible refinement Σ' of a Γ- (resp. Γ_par-)admissible Σ, p_1 (resp. p_2) extends to X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ'} → X_{K,Σ} (resp. X_{par,K,Σ}).
- Over X_Kli(p) the interior chain extends to isogenies of semi-abelian schemes G → G' → G (G' the pullback by p_2 of the semi-abelian scheme over X_par) of degrees p³ and p, composing to multiplication by p (p. 38). The non-smooth loci of X_Kli(p) and X_par lie in the non-ordinary locus of the special fibre, also along the boundary, where the rank-one charts have modular-curve bases that are smooth over the ordinary locus: of level away from p for X_par (p. 28), and of level Γ0(p) in some Klingen cases (cf. the proof of Lemma 10.3.3, p. 61). They therefore have codimension ≥ 2, which is what is used. P. 38 prints "codimension 2", but the non-smooth locus of Y_par,K is a finite set of closed points (Proposition 6.1.4.1). Define the ordinary locus pointwise through R07.2, as the ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII brief does. p_1 and p_2 are not finite flat over the boundary (footnote 9, p. 38).
- For suitable Σ, Σ', Σ'', the toroidal Hecke correspondence p_1: C_{p,2,Σ''} → X_Σ, p_2: C_{p,2,Σ''} → X_{Σ'} over Z_p (Faltings–Chai, p. 253), where C_{p,2} parametrizes isogenies p_1^*G → p_2^*G whose kernel away from the boundary is a totally isotropic subgroup of order p² of p_1^*G[p]. This roadmap owns only C_{p,2} and its maps p_1, p_2. The operators are built elsewhere: T_{p,2} and U_{Kli(p),2} with p inverted in IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes; the integral action of T_{p,2} over the p-rank ≥ 1 locus (Lemma 14.9.1(a)) in SiegelModularFormsModPn; the I^{−3}-twisted U_{Kli(p),2} and the Klingen correspondence (𝔈_{p,2})^{≥1} in HigherHidaAndColemanTheory. The C_{ℓ,i}, ℓ ≠ p, come from C3 with C5.

Layer P4, sheaves and minimal compactifications (§6.2.1–6.2.2, p. 30; pp. 71–72, 101; footnote 27, p. 105).
- ω_G = e^*Ω¹, Ω^(k,r) = Sym^k ω_G ⊗ det^r ω_G and Ω^(k,r)(−D) for (k,r) ∈ Z_{≥0} × Z; on X_par through G'.
- On X_par, and on X_Kli(p) for p_1^*Ω^(k,r) and p_2^*Ω^(k,r), RΓ(Ω^(k,r)) does not depend on Σ, by π^*Ω^(k,r) = Ω^(k,r), (Rπ)_*O = O and the projection formula (p. 30 states this for X and X_par). Neither does RΓ(Ω^(k,r)(−D)), by the corrected (2) and the projection formula (p. 30 does not state this cuspidal case; sourceIssues E40).
- X^⋆ = Proj ⊕_{k≥0} H^0(X, ω^k) and X^⋆_par = Proj ⊕_{k≥0} H^0(X_par, ω^k), ω descending to ample sheaves, with π: X → X^⋆ and π_par: X_par → X^⋆_par. X^⋆ is C5's; X^⋆_par is new.
- X^⋆_Kli(p), which the paper uses (pp. 71–72, 101) but never defines. Construct it following Lan (Forum Math. Sigma 2016; IMRN 2017), as p. 30 does for X^⋆ and X^⋆_par, with π_Kli: X_Kli(p) → X^⋆_Kli(p). Prove a map X^⋆_Kli(p) → X^⋆ that is finite over the p-rank ≥ 1 locus, defined pointwise through R07.2 (p. 101 uses "proper and quasi-finite"). Prove that det ω_G and det ω_{G'} descend to invertible sheaves, so that det ω_G → det ω_{G'} descends (p. 101).
- Stroh, Astérisque 370 (2015) 269–304, Lem. 2.4.3: the universal order-p subgroup H over X_Kli(p) extends to a finite flat group scheme at the boundary.

Ownership: ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII keeps the interior models; the compactified clauses of its klingen-level-cover-XKli and setup-klingen-paramodular-correspondence belong here. The level-K clauses stay with ShimuraCompactifications C3/C5, as above. Theorem 6.2.2.1 (Lan's vanishing of R^iπ_*Ω^(k,r)(−D)) goes to IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes.

Imports:
- Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry (ShimuraCompactifications) C0–C5 (C2 for the generic fibres; C3 for refinements, Hecke maps and the level-K clause (2); C4 for 1-motives; C5 for the good-level X_K, X^⋆).
- Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models, Part II: integral models and reduction (ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII): Y_Kli(p)_K, Y_{par,K}, the interior maps p_1, p_2 and chain G → G' → G, local models and Proposition 6.1.4.1, and the moduli of Lagrangian subgroups of G[p] (an instance of the Siegel parahoric lattice-chain moduli that the Kisin–Pappas brief plans there).
- Siegel and PEL moduli problems (PELModuli) M0–M5 (M0 for the similitude groups; M5 for Siegel moduli in every genus, used by Zarhin's trick).
- Shimura data, Hermitian domains, and adelic level structures (ShimuraData) D5 (neatness).
- Reductive groups, Part II: local structure and arithmetic models (ReductiveGroupsPartII) RG2.3 (Klingen and paramodular group schemes).
- Finite flat group schemes and integral p-adic Hodge theory (FiniteFlatGroupsAndIntegralPadicHodgeTheory) R07.1 (finite flat subgroups, the extension of H) and R07.2 (pointwise p-rank and ordinary locus).
- Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms (AutomorphicBundles) B3.
- Complex Shimura varieties and canonical models (ShimuraVarieties) V2.

Consumers (downstream, never imported):
- Algebraic modular forms, reduction and Serre weights, Part II: Siegel modular forms of genus two modulo p^n (SiegelModularFormsModPn);
- Automorphic bundles and classical automorphic forms, Part II: integral coherent cohomology and Hecke-equivariant perfect complexes (IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes);
- Hida and Coleman families, period modules, and family L-functions, Part II: higher Hida and higher Coleman theory for coherent cohomology (HigherHidaAndColemanTheory). It imports X^⋆_Kli(p) from here, not from C5 (its item two-affine-covering-of-p-rank-one-locus-and-overconvergent-subcomplex);
- through it, Minimal modularity lifting for GSp₄ in non-regular weight (GSp4NonregularModularityLifting) and the pending AbelianSurfacesPotentialModularity (DESIGN-BCGP18).
Consumers take X_K, X^⋆ and the other level-K statements from ShimuraCompactifications C3/C5.

Acceptance tests:
- rank W = 0, 1, 2 gives genus 2, 1, 0 and chart dimension 3, rank-one bases being modular curves, of level Γ0(p) in some Klingen cases (footnote 7, p. 28; see also the proof of Lemma 10.3.3, p. 61);
- p_1: X_Kli(p) → X is compatible, chart by chart, with C4–C5's level-K charts, and p_2: X_Kli(p) → X_par with the paramodular charts;
- X_Kli(p)_{K,Σ}[1/p] and X_{par,K,Σ}[1/p] are C2's toroidal compactifications at the corresponding levels, base changed to Q_p;
- subdividing a smooth two-dimensional cone of a Γ_Kli(p)- or Γ_par-chart gives π^*I ≠ I' but (Rπ)_*O(−D') = O(−D);
- X^⋆_par ⊗_{Z_p} C (via an embedding Q_p ↪ C) is V2's Baily–Borel compactification of Y_{par,K}(C), and Ω^(k,r) on X_par[1/p] is B3's canonical extension.
routes.reason: Toroidal compactifications and boundary geometry (ShimuraCompactifications) compactifies PEL moduli integrally only at good level in C5. Pilloni's Theorem 6.1.5.1, its 1-motive charts and the minimal compactification X^⋆_par work at Klingen and paramodular level at p over Z_p, and §14.9.2 uses the compactified T_{p,2}-correspondence C_{p,2} over Z_p, whose interior is the moduli of Lagrangian subgroups of G[p]. There the models are normal and lci but not smooth, and the paper also uses a Klingen-level minimal compactification X^⋆_Kli(p) that it never defines. That is new mathematics in the direction of ShimuraCompactifications, so it needs a Part II (PROTOCOL 15). ShimuraCompactificationsPartIIHodgeTypeIntegralBoundary already exists as that Part II: PAPER-FARB-KISIN-WOLFSON-24 proposed it and PAPER-MAULIK-SHANKAR-TANG-22 joined it, and it owns the integral boundary beyond C5. The Siegel datum is of Hodge type, so this paper joins it and widens its level hypothesis at p instead of opening a second Part II; the existing hyperspecial statements keep their hypothesis. The route does not go to the integral-models Part II ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII. That would make it a second owner of integral compactifications; the level-K clauses of Theorem 6.1.5.1 stay with C3/C5 and are imported. ShimuraVarietiesHondaTatePartII keeps the interior models, and this route imports them. It also imports C0–C5, PELModuli M0–M5, ShimuraData D5, ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.3, R07.1–R07.2, B3 and V2. It imports none of its consumers (SiegelModularFormsModPn, IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes, HigherHidaAndColemanTheory), so no cycle arises; p-rank loci are defined pointwise through R07.2 rather than imported from SiegelModularFormsModPn. The sheaves ω_G, Ω^(k,r) on X_par, X^⋆_Kli(p) and Stroh's extension of H belong here because they are statements about the semi-abelian scheme and subgroups at the boundary.

R3 ('the affinoid coherent-sheaf equivalence, acyclicity and the comparison needed for finite affinoid covers') must add the integral sheaves of §3 (pp. 11–15): O^+ and O^{++}, with sections A° and A°° on affinoids; Proposition 3.1.1 (Čech computes H^i of O^+, O^{++}); Bartenwerfer's bounded torsion of H^i(O^+) on smooth affinoids and vanishing of H^i(O^{++}) with smooth formal model (Theorem 3.1.1, Corollary 3.1.1); for F^+ ⊂ F locally free, Lemmas 3.2.1–3.2.3 and Proposition 3.2.1 (H^i(F) → lim H^i(F/p^nF^+) surjective, bijective for proper 𝒳); base change for O^{++}/p^n (Lemma 3.3.1, Proposition 3.3.1); Proposition 3.4.1 (O^{++} ≅ Rf_*O^{++} for smooth toric refinements; its proof reduces the stalk of R^if_*(O^{++}/p) at a point to the stalk at its maximal generisation by van der Put, [82], Proposition 1.4.10 and Example 1.5.2, p. 15), which imports the toric vanishing π_*O = O, R^iπ_*O = 0 from ShimuraCompactifications C3 and uses Scholze's comparison theorem (Forum Math. Pi 1, 2013, Theorem 9.1; [70]). From §§12–13: formal Banach sheaves and small ones (pp. 76, 82), AIP's Theorem A.1.2.2 and Proposition A.1.3.1 (pp. 82–83), relatively compact affinoid neighbourhoods (p. 87). R2 ('admissible formal schemes ... generic-fibre functor') gets (𝒳, O^+) ≅ lim of formal models, H^i(O^+) = colim H^i(O_𝔛), Raynaud's refining models (pp. 12–13; the colimit formula is Fujiwara–Kato's Proposition 3.1.10, [19]); R0 ('finite maps') gets descent of admissible opens along finite flat maps (p. 78). Corrections: I_𝔛 need not be coherent (sourceIssues E10); those limits are colimits (E11); in Proposition 3.2.1 ℱ lives on the normalisation, use Ȟ_𝒰 and c ∈ O_k (E12, E13), and injectivity needs k discretely valued or algebraically closed, else a boundedness argument (E14); fix the sign in Lemma 3.2.3 (E15); Proposition 3.4.1 needs f_*(O^{++}/p) = O^{++}/p (E16) and p̲ = λ(p), λ interior to σ (E17). Sources to add: Bartenwerfer (1979; entry corrected in E169), van der Put (1982), Fujiwara–Kato (Foundations of rigid geometry, cited as a preprint, [19], Proposition 3.1.10), Andreatta–Iovita–Pilloni (2015, Appendix A), Lütkebohmert (1990), Conrad (2006), Scholze (Forum Math. Pi 1, 2013, Theorem 9.1). This paper adds the reciprocal form of §5.1.3 (p. 21): H_ℓ = Z[T_{ℓ,0}^{±1}, T_{ℓ,1}, T_{ℓ,2}] with T_{ℓ,2} = [diag(ℓ,ℓ,1,1)], T_{ℓ,1} = [diag(ℓ²,ℓ,ℓ,1)], T_{ℓ,0} = [ℓ], and Q_ℓ(X) = 1 − T_{ℓ,2}X + ℓ(T_{ℓ,1} + (ℓ²+1)T_{ℓ,0})X² − ℓ³T_{ℓ,2}T_{ℓ,0}X³ + ℓ⁶T_{ℓ,0}²X⁴. The node proves Q_ℓ(X) = X⁴Q_x(1/X) with T_{x,1} = T_{ℓ,2}, T_{x,2} = T_{ℓ,1}, S_x = T_{ℓ,0}, so that one polynomial is planned. It also adds the maximal ideal of §15.2 (p. 107): for ρ̄: G_Q → GSp4(F̄_p) continuous, absolutely irreducible and unramified outside pN, m = ker Θ_m ⊂ H^{Np}, where Θ_m(Q_ℓ(X)) = det(1 − Xρ̄(Frob_ℓ)) for ℓ ∤ Np, with geometric Frobenius (Remark 5.1.7.1, p. 23). Corrections: read Frob_ℓ for 'Fob_ℓ' (sourceIssues E149); for odd p the rule fixes Θ_m(T_{ℓ,0}) only when tr ρ̄(Frob_ℓ) ≠ 0, so add ℓ³Θ_m(T_{ℓ,0}) = ν(ρ̄(Frob_ℓ)), or let m be any maximal ideal satisfying the rule, as Theorem 1.2 does (sourceIssues E150). SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 supplies Θ_ℓ(Q_ℓ(X)) = det(1 − Xc_{Θ_ℓ}). Source to add: Genestier–Tilouine (Astérisque 302, 2005, p. 193 and Remark 3, p. 196). Consumers: IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes, GSp4NonregularModularityLifting, and HigherHidaAndColemanTheory (the PadicFamilies Part II on higher Hida and Coleman theory), which states Theorem 15.2.1 for this m.

D5 ('Construct ... all Siegel data') already receives the genus-two root data in PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20's coordinates. This paper's §5.1.1 (p. 20) uses other coordinates, on which every weight in its §§5 and 15 depends: X*(T) = {(a1,a2;c) : c ≡ a1 + a2 mod 2}, with (a1,a2;c) sending diag(st1, st2, st2^{−1}, st1^{−1}) to s^c t1^{a1} t2^{a2}, basis e1 = (1,0;1), e2 = (0,1;1), e3 = (0,0;2) = ν. D5 imports these lattices, X_*(T), the coroots and the based root datum from ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.5, which states them in the paper's coordinates, and records for the Siegel datum the positive system, simple roots, compact root and ρ. The node states the change of coordinates to CG20's. It must use the positive system of the lower-triangular Borel, the only one consistent with §5.1.6, §15.2.1 and the matrix of the self-duality i: positive roots {e2−e1, −2e1+e3, −e1−e2+e3, −2e2+e3}, simple roots α1 = e2 − e1 and α2 = −2e2 + e3 (the base RG2.5 states), and ρ = (−2,−1;0); p. 20 prints e1 − e2 for e2 − e1 and ρ = (−1,−2;0) (sourceIssues E20). D5 keeps the tie to the Shimura datum: α1 is the compact root and, with Remark 5.1.2.1, the noncompact positive roots lie in g_C/p_Si. For the Siegel datum itself read h(a+ib) = a·1_4 + bJ (pp. 23, 107 print a1_2; E148). Consumers: AutomorphicFormsOnReductiveGroups AF.1/AF.4, IntegralCoherentHeckeComplexes, and HigherHidaAndColemanTheory (the PadicFamilies Part II on higher Hida and Coleman theory).

A4 ('Prove the Serre–Tate equivalence for deformations of abelian schemes with endomorphism and polarization structures') gets its standard consequence, Katz's canonical coordinates, which the proofs of Lemmas 7.1.1 and 7.1.2 (§7.1, pp. 39–40) use: for an ordinary abelian surface with a polarization of degree prime to p (§6.1.1; the principal case is an instance) over an algebraically closed field k of characteristic p, with T ≅ Z_p² the Tate module of the étale quotient, the formal deformation space is Hom(Sym²T, Ĝ_m), with ring W(k)[[X,Y,Z]] and Serre–Tate parameter the symmetric matrix (X Z; Z Y); deformations of an isogeny are the pairs of deformations whose parameters are compatible with it. A4 should state this for polarized ordinary abelian schemes in general, since the paper also needs it at paramodular level, where the parameter at an ordinary point of X_par is (X pZ; Z Y). The trace computations built on these charts belong to HigherHidaAndColemanTheory (the PadicFamilies Part II on higher Hida and Coleman theory), with their own corrections (sourceIssues E53, E54). No recorded mistake concerns the Serre–Tate statement itself. Source to add: Katz, Serre–Tate local moduli (LNM 868, 1981), cited by the paper as [39]. Consumer: HigherHidaAndColemanTheory (the operators T and U at ordinary points).

L0 plans the orthonormal-basis theorem only for Banach spaces over a p-adic field: 'For Banach spaces whose nonzero norm values lie in the coefficient value group, prove the orthonormal-basis theorem ... by lifting a basis of the integral lattice modulo varpi and completing the successive expansions'. This route widens L0's scope beyond Banach spaces over a p-adic field. The proof of Lemma 2.3.1 (§2.3, p. 10) needs the same statement over a complete Noetherian local ring R with finite residue field, here the local factors Z_p[[T]] of Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]], which are not discrete valuation rings: if M is flat and m_R-adically separated and complete and {e_i} lifts a basis of M/m_R M, then (r_i) ↦ Σ r_i e_i is an isomorphism from the m_R-adic completion of ⊕_I R, the families with r_i → 0, onto M. L0 should prove it once in this form, with the p-adic-field case as R = O. The proof: M/m^n M is flat, hence free, over the Artinian ring R/m^n, and one passes to the limit. If the design job would rather keep L0 to Banach spaces, the commutative-algebra home is DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.1 ('Complete local coefficient categories'), and L0 then cites it for R = O. Corrections: the paper writes the completion of R^I; read the free module R^(I) = ⊕_I R (sourceIssues E8). For odd p the ring Λ is only semi-local, so the statement is applied factor by factor (E5). Source to add: Matsumura, Commutative Ring Theory (Theorem 7.10: a flat module over a local ring with nilpotent maximal ideal is free), a book the paper cites for another result. Consumers: DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra P7 (Lemma 2.3.1, minimal complexes) and PadicFamilies L0a.

S1 ('Extend the construction to the minimal compactification using the boundary/normalization construction of the source') and S3 ('Construct the extension to the compactification in the precise Hodge-type form provided by the source, distinguishing auxiliary normalized compactifications from the canonical minimal one') get the finite-level statement that §12.9.1 (p. 81) takes from Scholze ('[71], p. 72', with Pilloni–Stroh, Theorem 1.16): there is N such that for n ≥ N there are a normal admissible formal scheme 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−HT} with generic fibre 𝒳(p^n)^⋆ and a projective map 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod} → 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−HT}; det ω_G^mod descends to an ample invertible sheaf on 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−HT}; and for every ε > 0 there is n(ε) ≥ N such that for n ≥ n(ε) there are sections s_{i,j}, 1 ≤ i,j ≤ 4, with s_{i,j} = HT(e_i) ∧ HT(e_j) in det ω_G^mod/p^ε. The layer records 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−HT} as an auxiliary normalized model in S3's sense: only its generic fibre is the minimal compactification 𝒳(p^n)^⋆. It imports 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod}, det ω_G^mod and the descended Λ²HT from HodgeTateAndCanonicalSubgroups T5. The affine opens 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^{⋆−HT} cut out by these sections, and Lemma 12.9.1.3 (p. 81), belong to HigherHidaAndColemanTheory (the PadicFamilies Part II on higher Hida and Coleman theory), with that lemma's correction (sourceIssues E102); no recorded mistake concerns the statement routed here. Already a source: Scholze, On torsion in the cohomology of locally symmetric varieties (Ann. of Math. 182, 2015), the roadmap's selected source for the Siegel construction; the locus to register is its p. 72. Source to add: Pilloni–Stroh (Ann. Math. Québec 40, 2016, Theorem 1.16). Consumer: HigherHidaAndColemanTheory (§12.9: Proposition 12.9.1, vanishing of cuspidal overconvergent cohomology above degree 1).

SF.2 ('construct sheaf cohomology, localization') gets the depth statement of SGA 2, Exposé III, §3, which the proof of Lemma 14.9.2 (p. 103) cites: if F is locally free on a Cohen–Macaulay scheme Y and Z ⊂ Y is closed of codimension at least 2, then H^i_Z(Y, F) = 0 for i ≤ 1, so H^0(Y, F) ≅ H^0(Y∖Z, F) and H^1(Y, F) ↪ H^1(Y∖Z, F). The paper applies it to the formal schemes 𝔛 and 𝔛_Kli(p) with Z the p-rank-0 locus, so the layer must also state it for Noetherian formal schemes and for the locally free coefficients Ω(−D)/p^n on the Cohen–Macaulay reductions mod p^n. PAPER-CALEGARI-GERAGHTY-20 already asks SF.2 for the H^0 part over O/ϖ^m for SiegelModularFormsModPn; this paper adds the injectivity on H^1, and SiegelModularFormsModPn plans Hartogs in that form for all n. Correction: 𝔛^{≥1} and 𝔛_Kli(p)^{≥1} are opens whose complements, the p-rank-0 loci in the special fibre, have codimension 2, not opens of codimension 2 (sourceIssues E143). Depth and the Cohen–Macaulay property come from DeformationAndDerivedPatchingAlgebra R03.3. Source to add: SGA 2 (Grothendieck, Advanced Studies in Pure Math. 2, 1968), Exposé III; the paper's entry says 'Bois Maris' for Bois Marie (E170). Consumers: SiegelModularFormsModPn (Hartogs), and HigherHidaAndColemanTheory (the PadicFamilies Part II on higher Hida and Coleman theory), whose Lemma 14.9.2 proves only the Klingen twist by I^{−3}.

RG2.5 ('Construct a pinned split dual group over ℤ from the dual root datum'; 'Prove compatibility with ... the split torus/GL_n examples') gets the GSp4 example of §5.1.1 (p. 20): the map i: X*(T) → X_*(T) with matrix ((1,1,1),(1,0,1),(1,1,2)) in the bases e1, e2, e3 and f1, f2, f3 is an isomorphism of based root data (X*(T), Δ, X_*(T), Δ^∨) ≅ (X_*(T), Δ^∨, X*(T), Δ), exchanging long and short roots, and so identifies the dual group of GSp4 with GSp4 over ℤ, hence GSp4(C). The paper cites Roberts–Schmidt, Lemma 2.3.1. RG2.5 states the based root datum (X*(T), Δ, X_*(T), Δ^∨) itself, in the paper's coordinates: X*(T) = {(a1,a2;c) : c ≡ a1 + a2 mod 2} with basis e1 = (1,0;1), e2 = (0,1;1), e3 = (0,0;2); X_*(T) = {(b1,b2;d) ∈ ½Z³ : b1+d, b2+d ∈ Z}, with pairing a1b1 + a2b2 + cd and dual basis f1 = (1,0;0), f2 = (0,1;0), f3 = (−½,−½;½); and the corrected base α1 = e2 − e1, α2 = −2e2 + e3, α1^∨ = f2 − f1, α2^∨ = −f2 (sourceIssues E20; p. 20 prints α1 = e1 − e2, α1^∨ = f1 − f2, α2^∨ = f2). With the printed base, i is not based; for the corrected base the printed matrix gives i(α1) = −f2 = α2^∨ and i(α2) = f2 − f1 = α1^∨, so the matrix stays as printed. ShimuraData D5 imports these lattices, the coroots and the based root datum from here and adds only what depends on the Siegel datum. The example should be verified beside the GL_n one, since IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.3 and SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 read Satake parameters as conjugacy classes in GSp4(C) through i. Source to add: Roberts–Schmidt (Local newforms for GSp(4), LNM 1918, 2007). Consumers: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.4 (twisted Satake for GSp4), IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.3, ShimuraData D5 (lattices, coroots, based root datum), and AutomorphicGaloisRepresentationsPartII (ρ valued in GSp4).

sourceIssues.locator: §1 Introduction, p. 2 of the author version (17 June 2019), last lines of the paragraph before Theorem 1.1. This defines the T used in Thm 1.1(2), Remark 1.1 and the p. 4 control theorem. HAL v3 (6 Jan 2018) does not have this sentence. Its introduction names only U ('an Hecke operator U at p associated to the double classe K_Kli(p)diag(1,p,p,p^2)K_Kli(p)', v3 p. 2), and its Thm 1.1 uses a bare 'ord'. So the sentence is new in the author version. HAL v3 §7 also lacks the comparison T = T_{p,1} + (1+p+p^2+p^3)T_{p,0} that the author version gives on p. 37.
sourceIssues.printed: There is also a corresponding Hecke operator T at p associated to the double coset K_p diag(p^2, p, p, 1)K_p which acts on the cohomology of X_K.
sourceIssues.correction: Suggested rewording: 'There is also a corresponding Hecke operator T at p, a modification of the double coset operator T_{p,1} = K_p diag(p^2,p,p,1)K_p, which acts on the cohomology of X_K. T is the normalized composite of the parahoric double cosets GSp4(Z_p)diag(p,p,p,1)GSp4'(Z_p) ⋆ GSp4'(Z_p)diag(p,1,1,1)GSp4(Z_p) (§7). It acts as p^{3-r}(T_{p,1} + (1+p+p^2+p^3)T_{p,0}), with T_{p,0} = pK_p. For r = 2 and k ≥ 2 it is congruent to pT_{p,1} mod p, so its ordinary part is that of the normalized double coset operator.' Besides the Hecke-algebra identity, the normalization p^{3-r} (a factor p when r = 2) is needed. K_p diag(p^2,p,p,1)K_p and K_p diag(1,p,p,p^2)K_p are indeed the same double coset: the two matrices are Weyl-conjugate with the same similitude p^2.
sourceIssues.reason:
Checked on the page images of pp. 2, 3, 4, 37 and 38.
(1) The discrepancy is real. §7, p. 37 says 'The Hecke operator T is related to the classical Hecke operator T_{p,1} = GSp4(Z_p)diag(1,p,p,p^2)GSp4(Z_p) … This suggests to replace T_{p,1} by a composition (denoted T) of two double cosets', and 'an elementary computation reveals that T = T_{p,1} + (1+p+p^2+p^3)T_{p,0}'. p. 38: 'The Hecke operator T that we use acts like p^{3-r}(T_{p,1} + (1+p+p^2+p^3)T_{p,0})'. The body then works only with T = T1∘T2 (p. 39 'We let T = T1 ◦ T2'; §8; §11.1.1).
(2) I checked the identity by counting degrees, using footnote 8's chains G → G/H1 → (G/H1)/H2. There are 1+p+p^2+p^3 choices of H1 and p+1 of H2. H2 ≠ G[p]/H1 gives L = ker of type (1,p,p,p^2), each counted once, so deg T_{p,1} = p(1+p+p^2+p^3). H2 = G[p]/H1 gives multiplication by p, counted 1+p+p^2+p^3 times. The eigenvalue formula on p. 38 also checks out: p^{3-r}[p^{-1}Σ − p^{-3}αδ + (1+p+p^2+p^3)p^{-3}αδ] = p^{2-r}Σ + p^{1-r}(1+p+p^2)αδ.
(3) The p. 2 sentence is written in parallel with the one for U, where 'associated to' is meant literally: §10, p. 57 says U 'corresponds to the operator p^{3-r}U_{Kli(p),1}'. Read the same way, the sentence identifies T with the normalized double coset operator, and that is inaccurate. The difference p·(1+p+p^2+p^3)·T_{p,0} is nonzero.
(4) Case for the defence. The sentence says 'associated to', not 'equal to'. The introduction itself, on p. 4, says T is built from the factorization diag(p^2,p,p,1) = diag(p,p,p,1)·diag(p,1,1,1) as T1 and T2. §7 gives the exact definition and states the relation. So the intended meaning is clear from context, which makes this a slip or imprecision (misprint class), not a false statement.
(5) Consequences: none. For r = 2, v(αδ) = k+1, so the normalized term p(1+p+p^2+p^3)T_{p,0} has eigenvalue (1+p+p^2+p^3)p^{-2}αδ, of valuation k−1. The paper itself notes (p. 38) 'T and pT_{p,1} are congruent modulo p for k ≥ 2'. Integrally, this term is p^{k-1} times an automorphism, because the central element p acts through a prime-to-p central automorphism of X_K. Theorem 1.1(2) and Remark 1.1 assume k > p+1 ≥ 3. So the T-ordinary part equals the pT_{p,1}-ordinary part, and both results are true under either reading. Nothing later in the paper uses the intro sentence; every proof uses the T of §7.

review.reason: Confirmed, and the paper contradicts itself. The introduction (p. 2) reads `There is also a corresponding Hecke operator $T$ at $p$ associated to the double coset $K_p\mathrm{diag}(p^2,p,p,1)K_p$ which acts on the cohomology of $X_K$', while \u00a77 (p. 37) opens `The Hecke operator $T$ is related to the classical Hecke operator $T_{p,1}=\mathrm{GSp}_4(\Z_p)\mathrm{diag}(1,p,p,p^2)\mathrm{GSp}_4(\Z_p)$. The naive attempt to directly define $T_{p,1}$ on the integral cohomology of vector bundles does not seem to work because we are unable to properly define and study an integral moduli space associated with $T_{p,1}$: the cocharacter $t\mapsto\mathrm{diag}(t^2,t,t,1)$ is not minuscule. We proceed differently, making use of a factorization in $\GL_4(\Q_p)$'. So $T$ is precisely not the double-coset operator the introduction names it as.

sourceIssues.locator: §1 (Introduction), p. 2, the paragraph that sets up Theorems 1.1 and 1.2 (author version, 17 June 2019). HAL v3 (p. 2) has the same omission, worded slightly differently: "a toroidal compactification of the Siegel threefold of level some open subgroup K = ∏ K_ℓ ⊂ GSp4(A_f) such that K_p = GSp4(Z_p)". That version also drops "compact".
sourceIssues.printed: We denote by X_K → Spec Z_p a toroidal compactification of the Siegel threefold of level given by an compact open subgroup K = ∏_ℓ K_ℓ ⊂ GSp4(A_f) such that K_p = GSp4(Z_p).
sourceIssues.correction: Read "given by a neat compact open subgroup K = ∏_ℓ K_ℓ ⊂ GSp4(A_f) such that K_p = GSp4(Z_p)". This is the standing hypothesis of §5.2.1 (p. 23) and §6.1.1 (p. 26). A second option, also adding "for a good polyhedral cone decomposition", is not needed. Theorem 1.1 is about cuspidal cohomology, and by Theorem 6.1.5.1(2) (Rπ_*O = O and, in the form corrected in sourceIssues E40, (Rπ)_*I_Σ' = I_Σ, plus the projection formula and common refinements) that cohomology does not depend on which toroidal compactification is chosen. So the minimal correction is the single word "neat".
sourceIssues.reason:
The omission is real. I checked the page images of p. 2 of the author version and of the HAL v3 intro. The list of conditions on K is only "compact open, K = ∏K_ℓ, K_p = GSp4(Z_p)", and "neat" does not appear. Everything the proof uses is built for neat K. The only occurrences of "neat" in the paper are p. 23, §5.2.1 ("Let K ⊂ GSp4(A_f) be a neat compact open subgroup. We let S_K = …") and p. 26, §6.1.1 ("Let K ⊂ GSp4(A_f) be a neat compact open subgroup. We assume that K = K^p K_p and that K_p = GSp4(Z_p)"). Y_K, the compactifications of Theorem 6.1.5.1, the Hecke correspondences and all later sections rest on §6.1.1. That includes Theorems 11.2.1 and 11.3.1 and Theorem 14.8.1, which together give Theorem 1.1 (p. 73: "In order to complete the proof of theorem 1.1 …"), and Theorem 15.2.1, which gives Theorem 1.2. The paper has no descent to non-neat level; no text mentions stacks, coarse spaces or taking invariants.

The defence is partial but substantial. (i) In the paper's own terminology, "the Siegel threefold of level K" is only ever defined for neat K (§5.2.1, §6.1.1). The same intro sentence also speaks of "the semi-abelian scheme" over X_K and "the relative Cartier divisor of the boundary", which assume a fine moduli scheme. A careful reader therefore infers neatness, and the intended meaning is clear from context. §15.1 and §15.2 (pp. 106–107) likewise reintroduce "K = ∏K_ℓ … a compact open subgroup. We assume as usual that K_p = GSp4(Z_p)" without saying "neat". There it plainly means the standing assumption of §6.1.1. (ii) Read literally for a non-neat K, such as level 1 with X_K taken as a Faltings–Chai stack, the claims are not proved. When p divides the order of the finite quotient K/K', taking invariants is not exact. The perfect amplitude-[0,1] claim of Theorem 1.1 and the integral statement in point 2 would then need an argument the paper does not give. When p does not divide that order, a descent argument works easily, but none is written.

So this is a genuine slip in the printed statement, not a mathematical failure. It is a misprint rather than a gap, and it affects nothing rather than a stated result, because under the intended hypothesis the proved results are exactly Theorems 1.1 and 1.2. Nothing later relies on the intro passage with non-neat K; the only back-reference, on p. 6, just uses the complex M.

sourceIssues.printed: As a replacement of H^0(X_K, Ω^{(0,2)}(−D) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p), we suggest to use H^0(M ⊗^L_{Λ,2} Q_p/Z_p) where M is the complex provided by theorem 1.1. The point is that p-divisible classes in H^0(M ⊗^L_{Λ,2} Q_p/Z_p) do come from cohomology classes in H^0(X_{Kli}(p)_K, Ω^{(0,2)}(−D)) and thus from classical automorphic forms.
sourceIssues.correction: Both occurrences should read H^0(M ⊗^L_{Λ,0} Q_p/Z_p), i.e. specialise M at k = 0 (weight (0,2)), not at k = 2 (weight (2,2)).
sourceIssues.reason:
I checked the printed text on a 300 dpi page render. Both occurrences clearly show the subscript "Λ,2" under ⊗^L; this is not an artefact of the text layer.

The paper's own conventions:
- p. 3 says: "For each integer k, there is a map k : Λ → Z_p extending the character z ↦ z^k of Z_p^×".
- Theorem 1.1(1) says: M ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Q_p = RΓ(X_{Kli}(p)_K, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D) ⊗_{Z_p} Q_p)^{U−ord}, where Ω^{(k,2)} comes from Sym^k St ⊗ det^2 St.
- p. 3 also says M is the U-ordinary part of the cohomology of F^κ ⊗ Ω^{(0,2)}(−D).
- §9.4 (p. 56) gives F^{n,n}_k ≅ (ω_{H_n})^k, which is the highest-weight quotient of Ω^{(k,0)}.
- Theorem 11.3.1(3) (p. 71) gives f RΓ(X^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) ≃ f RΓ(X^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), F^κ ⊗ ω^2(−D)) ⊗^L_{Λ,k} Z_p.

So ⊗_{Λ,2} specialises to Ω^{(2,2)} (Sym^2 ⊗ det^2). The paragraph is about Ω^{(0,2)} = det^2, the abelian-surface weight, which is k = 0.

I redid the check that the claim holds after the correction. Let M_0 = M ⊗^L_{Λ,0} Z_p. It is perfect over Z_p with amplitude [0,1], so there is an exact sequence 0 → H^0(M_0) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p → H^0(M_0 ⊗^L Q_p/Z_p) → H^1(M_0)[p^∞] → 0. The last term is finite, so the maximal p-divisible subgroup is H^0(M_0) ⊗ Q_p/Z_p. Also H^0(M_0) ⊗ Q_p = H^0(X_{Kli}(p)_K, Ω^{(0,2)}(−D) ⊗ Q_p)^{U−ord} by Theorem 1.1(1) at k = 0. This is exactly the stated claim, and with k = 2 it would concern Ω^{(2,2)} instead. Part (2) of Theorem 1.1 (k > p+1) plays no role here.

The slip may come from BCGP-style notation, where abelian surfaces have weight (2,2). In this paper, however, the weight is Ω^{(k,r)} = Sym^k ⊗ det^r and specialisation is written ⊗_{Λ,k}, so the text is wrong under its own conventions.

HAL v3 (printed p. 5) has the identical text with "Λ,2" in both places, and its Theorem 1.1 uses the same ⊗^L_{Λ,k} and z ↦ z^k convention. I could not check the published Duke text.

sourceIssues.locator: §1 (Introduction), p. 6, lines 1-3 of the page. HAL v3 has the same text (printed p. 5).
sourceIssues.printed: Congruences are unobstructed for ordinary p-adic modular forms, while they are for classical modular forms in weight (0, 2) because of the non vanishing of H^1. The classical Taylor-Wiles method requires unobstructed congruences.
sourceIssues.correction: ... while they are obstructed (or: while they are not unobstructed) for classical modular forms in weight (0,2) because of the non vanishing of H^1.
sourceIssues.reason: Under ordinary English ellipsis, 'while they are' repeats the predicate 'unobstructed'. The sentence would then say that congruences are unobstructed for classical forms too, which contradicts both 'while' and the causal clause 'because of the non vanishing of H^1'. The next sentences say the classical Taylor-Wiles method 'requires unobstructed congruences' and that Calegari-Geraghty modify it 'in order to apply it in obstructed situations'. So the intended word is 'obstructed', and it is missing. The slip is only in the motivational introduction.

review.reason: Confirmed verbatim: `Congruences are unobstructed for ordinary $p$-adic modular forms, while they are for classical modular forms in weight $(0,2)$ because of the non vanishing of $H^1$.' Under the ordinary reading of the ellipsis the sentence asserts the opposite of what `while' and the causal clause require, and the next sentences \u2014 `The classical Taylor-Wiles method requires unobstructed congruences' and the appeal to Calegari\u2013Geraghty for obstructed situations \u2014 settle the intended sense.

sourceIssues.locator: §2, standing hypothesis, p. 7 (author version, 17 June 2019), as applied with R = Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]] (defined in §9.3, p. 56) in §11.3: Theorem 11.3.1(1),(2) (p. 71) and its proof (last line of p. 72: "We deduce from lemma 2.1.2 ..."). HAL v3 has the same text: the §2 hypothesis (HAL v3, printed p. 6, PDF p. 7) and the same "We deduce from lemma 2.1.2" step (HAL v3, printed p. 62, PDF p. 63).
sourceIssues.printed: p. 7 (§2, opening): "In this section, R is a complete local noetherian ring with maximal ideal 𝔪_R. We assume moreover that R/𝔪_R is a finite field. We develop a theory of ordinary (or Hida) projectors for certain complexes of R-modules." p. 56 (§9.3): "Let Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]] and κ : Z_p^× → Λ^× is the universal character." p. 72 (proof of Thm 11.3.1, last line): "We deduce from lemma 2.1.2 that U is locally finite on RΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω^2(−D))." p. 71, Thm 11.3.1(2): "The complex fRΓ(𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p), 𝔉^κ ⊗ ω^2(−D)) is a perfect complex of Λ-modules concentrated in degree [0, 1]."
sourceIssues.correction: State §2 for a complete semi-local noetherian ring R whose residue ring R/rad(R) is finite. Take m_R to be the Jacobson radical rad(R), and let "perfect" mean a bounded complex of finite projective (not finite free) R-modules. Equivalently, use the fact that such an R is a finite product ∏ R_{m_i} of complete local rings with finite residue fields, and apply §2 factor by factor. For p odd, Λ = ∏_{χ mod p−1} e_χΛ with e_χΛ ≅ Z_p[[T]], so applying §2 factor by factor is right and minimal. Replacing m_R by the Jacobson radical is not enough alone. The basis argument of Lemma 2.3.1 must be done factor by factor, and the "finite free" in the definition of C_perf / Prop. 2.2.1 must become "finite projective".
sourceIssues.reason:
(1) Checked on the rendered pages: the §2 standing hypothesis requires R to be local. Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]]. For odd p, Z_p^× ≅ μ_{p−1} × (1+pZ_p). X^{p−1}−1 splits into distinct linear factors over Z_p by Hensel's lemma, so Z_p[μ_{p−1}] ≅ Z_p^{p−1}, and Λ ≅ Z_p[[T]]^{p−1}. So Λ has p−1 maximal ideals and is not local. The paper allows any p: it treats p = 2 and p ≥ 3 separately elsewhere (p. 37: "When p ≥ 3 ... When p = 2"), and footnote 23 uses residue classes mod p−1. For p = 2, Λ is local.
(2) §2 really is used with R = Λ, not R = Z_p. Local finiteness over Z_p would fail for Λ-linear U on a module like Λ, because F_p[[Z_p^×]] is infinite-dimensional. The topology on 𝔉^κ = lim_n 𝔉^κ_{∞,n} (p. 56) comes from ker(Λ → Λ_n), which for n = 1 is the Jacobson radical. The step "We deduce from lemma 2.1.2 ..." reduces modulo colim_m RΓ(X_1, 𝓕^k_{m,1} ⊗ ω^2). That is M ⊗ Λ/m_k with m_k = ker(Λ → F_p, [z] ↦ z^k mod p), and this maximal ideal depends only on k mod (p−1). So Lemma 2.1.2, stated for local R, is used outside its hypotheses. Read literally, one fixed k > p+1 only gives local finiteness on the e_{χ_k}-component. Theorem 11.3.1(2), perfectness over Λ, likewise needs Prop. 2.2.1 over the non-local Λ.
(3) The repair is routine. Every §2 proof works factor by factor on e_χΛ. For example, Lemma 2.3.1 picks a basis of M/𝔪_R over the residue field, which needs locality, and this can be done on each factor. Since k > p+1 is arbitrary, every class mod p−1 is covered. The stated results stand. What is missing is a justification in the proof. 1. The mismatch is real. For p odd, Z_p^× = μ_{p−1} × (1+pZ_p), so Λ = Z_p[μ_{p−1}][[T]]. Also Z_p[μ_{p−1}] ≅ Z_p^{p−1}, because x^{p−1}−1 splits into distinct factors over Z_p. So Λ has p−1 maximal ideals and is not local. For p = 2, Λ = Z_2[{±1}][[T]] is local, so the problem only arises for odd p. The paper allows odd p, and it handles weights in residue classes mod p−1 (footnote 23, p. 91). Nothing in the paper extends §2 to semi-local rings. The only mention of semi-locality is for the Hecke algebra in §15.2, via [41] lem. 2.12.

2. The defence mostly works, so this is only a gap. The proofs of Lemmas 2.1.1–2.1.3 and Prop. 2.2.2 never use locality; they go through word for word with m_R = rad(Λ) = (p, [γ]−1). The paper's own argument on p. 72 in fact uses this reading. By §9.3, F^{∞,1}_κ = colim_m F^{m,1}_κ is 𝔉^κ reduced modulo ker(Λ → Λ_1 = F_p[(Z/p)^×]) = rad(Λ), and Λ_1 ≅ F_p^{p−1}. So F^{∞,1}_κ = ⊕_{k mod p−1} F^{∞,1}_k. The proof establishes local finiteness for every k > p+1, which covers every residue class mod p−1, before invoking Lemma 2.1.2. The ideals ker(Λ→Λ_n) also define the rad(Λ)-adic topology. So Thm 11.3.1(1) is correct once Lemma 2.1.2 is read with the Jacobson radical.

3. What does not carry over. Lemma 2.3.1 (and so Prop. 2.3.1) picks a basis of M/m_R over the field R/m_R, but Λ/rad(Λ) is not a field. Prop. 2.2.1 relies on [55] (Mumford) lem. 1, p. 44. Over a non-local ring that lemma gives a first term that is finite flat, i.e. projective, not free. So Thm 11.3.1(2), which the proof never argues explicitly and which presumably comes from Prop. 2.2.1 over Λ, holds in the standard sense of "perfect" (finite projective). It need not hold in §2's literal sense ("complexes of finite free R-modules"). A complex of finite free Λ-modules in [0,1] has the same Euler characteristic on every component. Nothing forces that here: Prop. 13.4.1 only says the relevant dimension difference is locally constant on each residue class mod p−1.

4. What uses the passage: Thm 11.3.1(1) and (2); through them Thm 1.1 (a perfect complex of Λ-modules), §15.2 (the perfect complex f RΓ(...)_m), and Thm 15.2.1. Thm 15.2.1's proof specializes at an arbitrary large weight k, so it works on every component. Every stated result stays true with the standard meaning of "perfect" once §2 is extended as above (a routine extension). So the damage is confined to the proof.

review.reason: Confirmed as a gap, and every link in the chain is verbatim on the page. §2 opens (p. 7) `In this section, $R$ is a complete local noetherian ring with maximal ideal $\fm_R$. We assume moreover that $R/\fm_R$ is a finite field.' §9.3 (p. 56) sets `$\Lambda=\Z_p[[\Z_p^\times]]$'. Theorem 11.3.1(2) (p. 71) concludes that `$f\mathrm{R\Gamma}(\mathfrak X^{\geq1}_{\mathrm{Kli}}(p),\mathcal F^\kappa\otimes\omega^2(-D))$ is a perfect complex of $\Lambda$-modules concentrated in degree $[0,1]$', which is §2's theory applied with $R=\Lambda$. For odd $p$, $\Z_p^\times\cong\mu_{p-1}\times(1+p\Z_p)$ and $X^{p-1}-1$ splits into distinct linear factors over $\Z_p$ by Hensel, so $\Z_p[\mu_{p-1}]\cong\Z_p^{p-1}$ and $\Lambda\cong\Z_p[[T]]^{p-1}$: it has $p-1$ maximal ideals and is not local. So §2's standing hypothesis fails at the one place it is used with $\Lambda$. The recorded repair — semi-local $R$ with $\fm_R$ the Jacobson radical and `perfect' meaning finite projective rather than finite free — is the right shape, and the same structural point is what E91 and E165 turn on.

sourceIssues.locator: §2.2, proof of Proposition 2.2.1, p. 9 (first displayed formula of the proof)
sourceIssues.printed: 0 → 𝔪_R^n/𝔪_R^{n−1} ⊗_R M^• → M^•/𝔪_R^n → M^•/𝔪_R^{n−1} → 0   (displayed formula, proof of Proposition 2.2.1, author version p. 9, introduced by "We have short exact sequences of complexes"; checked on a 400 dpi crop of the page image)
sourceIssues.reason: I rendered p. 9 at 400 dpi and it reads exactly as quoted, with 𝔪_R^n/𝔪_R^{n−1} in the first term. So this is not a text-layer artefact. Because 𝔪^n ⊂ 𝔪^{n−1}, the printed quotient 𝔪^n/𝔪^{n−1} does not make sense, and no convention in the paper would make it correct. Redoing the computation degreewise: the surjection M^i/𝔪^n M^i → M^i/𝔪^{n−1} M^i has kernel 𝔪^{n−1}M^i/𝔪^n M^i. Tensoring 0 → 𝔪^n → 𝔪^{n−1} → 𝔪^{n−1}/𝔪^n → 0 with the flat module M^i gives 𝔪^{n−1}/𝔪^n ⊗ M^i ≅ 𝔪^{n−1}M^i/𝔪^n M^i, since 𝔪^k ⊗ M^i ≅ 𝔪^k M^i by flatness. This gives the corrected sequence, which is what the induction in the proof needs. 𝔪^{n−1}/𝔪^n is a finite-dimensional R/𝔪-vector space, because R is noetherian. So 𝔪^{n−1}/𝔪^n ⊗ M^• is a finite direct sum of copies of M^• ⊗ R/𝔪, and its cohomology is finite. The same paper has the correct form in Lemma 2.1.2 on p. 8: "𝔪_R^{n−1}/𝔪_R^n ⊗_R M → M/𝔪_R^n → M/𝔪_R^{n−1} → 0". HAL v3 has the identical misprint in the same proof, on printed p. 7 (PDF p. 8): "0 → 𝔪_R^n/𝔪_R^{n−1} ⊗_R M^• → M^•/𝔪_R^n → M^•/𝔪_R^{n−1} → 0". Its Lemma 2.1.2 is also correct there. This correction is right. The error does not affect the argument: the intended sequence is clear from context and from Lemma 2.1.2, and the proof works with it. Proposition 2.2.1 is correct as stated. Proposition 2.2.2 and later results that use it are unaffected.

sourceIssues.locator: §2.2, proof of Proposition 2.2.2, p. 9 (author version of 17 June 2019). In HAL v3 it is printed p. 8 (PDF p. 9), with the same statement number and identical wording.
sourceIssues.printed: "We now prove by descending induction on i that H^i(C(f)) = 0. Assume this holds for i ≥ n + 1. Using the spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = Tor^R_{−p}(H^q(M^•), R/m_R) ⇒ H^{p+q}(M^• ⊗_R R/m_R) we see that H^n(C(f))/m_R ↪ H^n(C(f)/m_R) = 0. By Nakayama's lemma, we deduce that H^n(C(f)) = 0." (Checked on the page image at 110 and 220 dpi; the page has the subscript R on ⊗, i.e. ⊗_R.)
sourceIssues.correction: Replace M^• by C(f) in the displayed spectral sequence. It should read: "Using the (Künneth) spectral sequence E_2^{p,q} = Tor^R_{−p}(H^q(C(f)), R/m_R) ⇒ H^{p+q}(C(f) ⊗_R R/m_R) we see that H^n(C(f))/m_R ↪ H^n(C(f)/m_R) = 0."
sourceIssues.reason: In Prop. 2.2.2, M^• is the source of f : M^• → N^•. The displayed formula is copied word for word from the display in the proof of Prop. 2.2.1, where M^• was the complex of that proposition. As printed, it is the spectral sequence of the source complex, and that says nothing about H^n(C(f)). I redid the argument. C(f) is a bounded complex of flat modules, so C(f) ⊗_R R/m_R computes the derived tensor product, and the Künneth spectral sequence (Weibel 5.6.4, which the paper cites as [83]) gives E_2^{p,q} = Tor_{−p}(H^q(C(f)), k) for p ≤ 0. The term E_2^{0,n} = H^n(C(f))/m_R has no outgoing differentials, because they land in columns p > 0, which are zero. Its incoming differentials are d_r from E_r^{−r, n+r−1}, which are subquotients of Tor_r(H^{n+r−1}(C(f)), k) with r ≥ 2. These vanish by the induction hypothesis, since n+r−1 ≥ n+1. So the edge map H^n(C(f))/m_R → H^n(C(f)/m_R) is injective, and its target is 0 because the cone of f⊗1 is acyclic. H^n(C(f)) is finite by Prop. 2.2.1, so Nakayama gives H^n(C(f)) = 0. The descending induction can start because C(f) is bounded. So the argument is correct once C(f) replaces M^•. The index Tor_r(H^{n+r−1}(C(f))) used above is right. Only the name of the complex is wrong, so this is a misprint. The same text appears in HAL v3.

sourceIssues.printed: Let {e_i}_{i∈I} ∈ M^I be a lift of {ē_i}_{i∈I}. Denote by \widehat{R^I} the m_R-adic completion of R^I. The map R^I → M corresponding to {e_i}_{i∈I} induces an isomorphism \widehat{R^I} → M by Nakayama's lemma and the flatness assumption on M.
sourceIssues.correction: Replace R^I by the free module R^{(I)} = ⊕_{i∈I} R. Its m_R-adic completion \widehat{R^{(I)}} is the module of families (r_i) with r_i → 0 along the filter of complements of finite subsets. The map (r_i) ↦ Σ r_i e_i then gives an isomorphism \widehat{R^{(I)}} → M.
sourceIssues.reason: In the same sentence the paper writes {e_i}_{i∈I} ∈ M^I, so X^I means the product (families). Read that way, R^I is the product ∏_I R, which causes two problems. (a) (r_i) ↦ Σ r_i e_i is not defined on it for infinite I. (b) Taking a completion would do nothing, because ∏_I R is already m_R-adically complete: m_R^n is finitely generated, so m_R^n ∏R = ∏ m_R^n. The claimed isomorphism would also be false. For R = Z_p, I = ℕ and M the completion of ⊕_ℕ Z_p, M/pM ≅ ⊕_ℕ F_p has countable dimension, but ∏_ℕ Z_p / p = ∏_ℕ F_p has uncountable dimension. The intended reading, the completed direct sum, is clear: the proof talks of completing R^I and later of columns that 'tend to 0 in R (for the filter of the complements of the finite subsets)'. The proof is correct with that reading.

sourceIssues.locator: §3.1, proof of Proposition 3.1.1, second paragraph, p. 12 of the author version (PDF p. 12). HAL v3 has the same sentence word for word ("There is a surjective map of coherent sheaves over X : OX → OX̄red and we denote by IX its kernel"), but it sits in the paragraph just before Proposition 3.1.1 on printed p. 10 (PDF p. 11), followed by "If X has reduced special fiber then IX = mOk OX".
sourceIssues.printed: There is a surjective map of coherent sheaves over 𝔛 : 𝒪_𝔛 → 𝒪_{X̄^{red}} and we denote by 𝔍_𝔛 its kernel.
sourceIssues.correction: Delete "coherent" and read: "There is a surjective map of sheaves of 𝒪_𝔛-modules 𝒪_𝔛 → 𝒪_{X̄^{red}}; we denote by 𝔍_𝔛 its kernel." The two sheaves are coherent over 𝔛 only when k is discretely valued. The rest of the proof stands as printed.
sourceIssues.reason:
I transcribed the sentence from the page rendered at 250 dpi. §3.1 lets k be "a complete non-archimedean field" with no discreteness assumption. The section's results are also used later over non-discretely valued fields: Corollary 3.1.1 is applied "over the non-archimedean field (k(x), k(x)+)" for a maximal rank-1 point x (proof of Prop. 3.4.1, p. 15).

Counterexample: take k = C_p and X = Spa(C_p, O_{C_p}), which is separated and of finite type. It has the formal model 𝔛 = Spf O_{C_p}, whose underlying space is a single point. Then X̄ = Spec(O_{C_p}/m) = Spec F̄_p, which is already reduced. So the printed map is O_{C_p} → F̄_p on global sections, and its kernel is 𝔍_𝔛 = m_{C_p}.

For 𝒪_{X̄^{red}} to be a coherent 𝒪_𝔛-module, the kernel of 𝒪_𝔛 → 𝒪_{X̄^{red}} must be of finite type. On a one-point space that means m_{C_p} must be a finitely generated O_{C_p}-module. It is not. In a valuation ring every finitely generated ideal is principal. If m = (π), then |π| would be the largest absolute value below 1. But |p^{1/n}| = p^{-1/n} tends to 1, so no such largest value exists. Equivalently, F̄_p = O_{C_p}/m is not finitely presented. The claim that this is a map of coherent sheaves is therefore false for non-discretely valued k. For discretely valued k it is true, because 𝔛 is then noetherian.

The mistake is harmless. The proof uses only two facts, and neither needs coherence:
1. 𝒪^{++} = colim 𝔍_𝔛.
2. Čech cohomology equals cohomology for 𝔍_𝔛 on separated models.
Fact 2 follows because H^i(𝔘, 𝔍) = 0 for i > 0 on an affine 𝔘 = Spf A. This comes from the exact sequence 0 → 𝔍 → 𝒪_𝔛 → 𝒪_{X̄^{red}} → 0. Both 𝒪_𝔛 and the quasi-coherent sheaf 𝒪_{X̄^{red}} on the affine scheme have no higher cohomology. Also A → (A/mA)_red is surjective on sections, so H^1(𝔘, 𝔍) = 0 as well. The colimit result cited as [19] prop. 3.1.10 applies to arbitrary sheaves. So this is a false side remark, not a failed step. I class it as an error rather than a misprint because the word states a property that fails, rather than being a typing slip. The defence fails. §3.1 says "Let k be a complete non-archimedean field" and puts no discreteness hypothesis on k. The paper uses §3 over non-discretely valued fields: Corollary 3.1.1 is applied over completed residue fields k(x) in the proof of Prop. 3.4.1 (p. 15), and Lemma 3.2.2 is applied to cohomology over C_p in §13.3 (p. 89). No convention makes 𝒪_{X̄^{red}} coherent over 𝔛. It is generated by one section, 1, whose annihilator is 𝔍_𝔛, so coherence would need 𝔍_𝔛 to be of finite type.

Simplest counterexample: 𝔛 = Spf O_k. Then 𝔍_𝔛 = m_{O_k}. For a non-discrete valuation, m_{O_k} is not finitely generated, because a finitely generated ideal of a valuation ring is principal. So k̃ = O_k/m is finitely generated but not finitely presented over the coherent ring O_k, and is not coherent.

The same failure happens on every formal model 𝔛 of every non-empty X. Suppose 𝔍_𝔛 = (f_1,…,f_r) on an affine Spf A. Each f_j has some power in mA, so its sup norm on the generic fibre is below 1. Every element of (f_1,…,f_r)A then has sup norm at most max_j |f_j|_sup < 1. But m ⊂ 𝔍_𝔛 contains constants a with max_j |f_j|_sup < |a| < 1, which is a contradiction. The HAL v3 sentence "𝔍_𝔛 = m_{O_k}𝒪_𝔛" shows the same thing directly. When O_k is a DVR, A is noetherian and the statement is true.

Why this is harmless: the proof never uses coherence. Repeating the proof of the first isomorphism needs only three facts.
(a) 𝒪_𝒳^{++} = colim_𝔛 𝔍_𝔛. Elements of 𝔍_𝔛 have a power in m𝒪_𝔛, so they have |f| < 1. Conversely, a section with |f| < 1 on an affinoid is topologically nilpotent, so it lies in 𝔍_𝔛 on a suitable model.
(b) [19] prop. 3.1.10 and the reduction to finite coverings. These are purely topological statements.
(c) H^i(𝔘, 𝔍_𝔛) = 0 for i > 0 on affine opens 𝔘 = Spf A (so H^i = Ȟ^i on the separated 𝔛). This follows from 0 → 𝔍 → 𝒪_𝔘 → 𝒪_{Ū^{red}} → 0. Here 𝒪_𝔘 is acyclic on affines (it is lim 𝒪/ϖ^n, with Mittag-Leffler), 𝒪_{Ū^{red}} is quasi-coherent on the affine scheme Ū^{red}, and A → (A/mA)_red is surjective.

Consequences: Proposition 3.1.1 is correct for arbitrary k with the word "coherent" deleted. Deleting that word is the right, minimal correction. Prop. 3.1.1 itself is never cited later in the paper; a search of the whole author version finds no citation. Prop. 3.4.1 uses Corollary 3.1.1, whose proof relies on [26] and Theorem 3.1.1, not on Prop. 3.1.1. The mistake is nonetheless real, because Prop. 3.1.1 itself is stated for arbitrary k. It is a false descriptive claim rather than a typographical slip, so I class it as an "error" with affects "nothing". Some readers might call it a misprint, since the intended meaning ("surjective map of sheaves") is clear.

sourceIssues.printed: There is an isomorphism in the category of locally ringed spaces (𝒳, O^+_𝒳) = lim_𝔛(𝔛, O_𝔛) where 𝔛 runs over all formal models of 𝒳 (see [69], thm. 2.22). By [19], prop. 3.1.10, we deduce that H^i(𝒳, O^+_𝒳) = lim_𝔛 H^i(𝔛, O_𝔛). ... It follows that Ȟ^i(𝒳, O^+_𝒳) = lim_𝔛 Ȟ^i(𝔛, O_𝔛).
sourceIssues.correction: H^i(𝒳, O^+_𝒳) = colim_𝔛 H^i(𝔛, O_𝔛) and Ȟ^i(𝒳, O^+_𝒳) = colim_𝔛 Ȟ^i(𝔛, O_𝔛): direct limits over the filtered system of formal models, with pullback transition maps H^i(𝔛, O_𝔛) → H^i(𝔛', O_{𝔛'}) for 𝔛' → 𝔛.
sourceIssues.reason: The paper writes 'colim' for direct limits throughout: O^{++}_𝒳 = colim_𝔛 I_𝔛 later in this same proof, colim_n on pp. 13-14, and many more. It writes 'lim' for inverse limits: lim_n in §3.2, and lim_𝔛(𝔛, O_𝔛) for the space itself. Cohomology is contravariant in 𝔛, so the groups H^i(𝔛, O_𝔛) form a direct system. For a limit of quasi-compact quasi-separated spaces, cohomology of the colimit of pulled-back sheaves is the colimit of the cohomologies; that is the cited result. An inverse limit is not the right object. The next step, Čech cohomology computed with finite coverings, also commutes with filtered colimits. The intended meaning is clear and the proof is fine with colim.

review.reason: Confirmed. Page 12 prints both `we deduce that $H^i(\mathcal X,\mathcal O^+_{\mathcal X})=\lim_{\mathfrak X}H^i(\mathfrak X,\mathcal O_{\mathfrak X})$' and `It follows that $\check H^i(\mathcal X,\mathcal O^+_{\mathcal X})=\lim_{\mathfrak X}\check H^i(\mathfrak X,\mathcal O_{\mathfrak X})$'.
