The difference from p·Id is Id. Now M = H^0(𝔛^ord, Ω^(k,r)) is nonzero, p-torsion-free and p-adically separated. So M ≠ p^k M for every k ≥ 1, and Id is not ≡ 0 mod p^k. The statement is vacuous only for k = 0, and the lemma sets no condition on k.

**The proof fails at the same place.** L_0 ⊂ G[p^0] is 0 and T^{0,et} = Id, so all p+1 multiplicative H satisfy H ∩ L_0 = {0}, not p of them. For n ≥ 1 the count of p is right: L_n ∩ G[p]^0 is the line μ_{p^n}[p] = μ_p inside μ_p², and H must avoid it, which leaves p choices.

**Defences tried, none works:**
- Normalisations: the powers U^0 and T^0 are the identity whatever normalisation U and T carry (p^{3−r}U_{Kli(p),1} and p^{−3−r}).
- Tr: it is the plain trace map, as stated. Rescaling it by 1/(p+1) would break the cases n ≥ 1.
- i: it is the canonical pullback from p. 67.
- The rank: the paper's own count of p+1 is correct.

So "n ≥ 1" is the right and minimal fix, and it changes nothing downstream.

So I record "a stated result", with the reach stopping at the lemma itself; no later result depends on n = 0. It also spells out a second silent step, f∘T''' = f∘U, which the printed "fT'''U^{-1}G = fUU^{-1}G" needs as well.

The r in point 6 is not unbound: the theorem opens with "For k > p + 1 and r ≥ 2 :", so r is the theorem's general r ≥ 2. The misprint still stands, for these reasons:

Its hypotheses are exactly those of Corollary 11.1.3.1(5), with the same range k ≥ C and r ≥ 2 as point 7. The mod-p reduction of fN^• is f(N^•/p) by Lemma 2.1.4. For $r\geq3$ point 7 is also a formal consequence of points 4 and 5 together with the properness of $\mathfrak X$, so the gap is real only at $r=2$, which is the case the paper goes on to need. The finding's replacement is the right one and uses only results already available at that point.

sourceIssues.correction:
The gap concerns only the Igusa-type sheaves on p. 72. Before [50] Thm 8.6 can be used for F^κ_{m,n} ⊗ ω^2(−D), its hypothesis has to be checked: the sheaf must be formally subcanonical in the sense of [50] Def. 8.5, and the theorem, which is stated for sheaves on the whole toroidal compactification, has to be localised to the open X^{*,≥1}_{Kli}(p). This needs an argument because the sheaf is only quasi-coherent: f: X^{≥1}_{Kli}(p^m)_n → X^{≥1}_{Kli}(p)_n is affine and étale but not finite (Lemma 9.1.1.1, Remark 9.1.1.2).

A sufficient sketch:
- Every boundary fibre of π lies in the ≥1 locus, and G has constant multiplicative rank along it. So over the formal completion along a fibre, H_m lies in the multiplicative part of G̃[p^m], which is pulled back from C_{Φ,δ}. Hence X^{≥1}_{Kli}(p^m) and IG(p^m) become finite étale there, with trivial tame part and unipotent (p-power) monodromy. This gives E_0 a finite filtration with constant graded pieces, as Def. 8.5(2) requires.
- Alternatively, split the sheaf along Ha. Over the ordinary locus the covers are finite étale (deeper-level Lan models). Over V(Ha^l), f is étale and universally bijective, so it is an isomorphism.

No change to any statement is needed.

(1) The cited theorem is not limited to automorphic vector bundles at spherical and paramodular level. That description fits only the paper's restatement, Thm 6.2.2.1. Its Thm 8.6 applies to any quasi-coherent sheaf E on M^tor_{H,Σ} that is "formally canonical (resp. formally subcanonical) over R" (Def. 8.5). It works at any neat level H and over any O_{F_0,(p)}-algebra R. So Ω^{(k,r)}(−D) on the Klingen-level compactification is covered. The paper itself uses this for X_Kli(p) → X*_Kli(p) in §14, where it shows that X^{≥1}_Kli(p) is the preimage of X*^{≥1}_Kli(p). Colimits and the quotients by Ha^l then follow from the long exact sequence. So the citation in the proof of Thm 11.2.1 is not a gap.

(2) For Thm 11.3.1 the citation does not apply as written. Lan's Def. 8.5(2) requires, at each boundary point x̄, a finite filtration of E_{0,x̄} whose graded pieces are pullbacks of finite R-modules. So E must be of finite type near the boundary.
- As an O-module, F^κ_{m,n} is the pushforward along X^{≥1}_Kli(p^m)_n → X^{≥1}_Kli(p)_n (and the finite Igusa torsor). That map is affine, étale and quasi-finite but not finite: Remark 9.1.1.2 says it is an isomorphism over the p-rank-1 locus and has degree p or p+1 over the ordinary locus. The p-rank-1 locus meets the boundary (toric rank 1 with supersingular abelian part). There, for m ≥ 2, F^κ_{m,n}⊗ω^2(−D) is not of finite type, because an affine quasi-finite map with a coherent pushforward would be finite. So it is not formally subcanonical.
- The Ha-torsion right-hand sheaves do not have the form in Def. 8.5(2) either.
- The paper checks none of this, and F^κ_{m,n} exists only on the p-rank ≥ 1 open.

The conclusion that is actually needed is very likely true and can be recovered as described in the correction. So this is a gap in the proof, not an error in any stated result. Defence, part 1. The citation in the proof of Thm 11.2.1 is not a gap. The cited theorem is not only about automorphic vector bundles on the spherical and paramodular compactifications; that describes only the paper's own restatement, Thm 6.2.2.1 on p. 30. [50] itself (Lan, IMRN 2017; author's compilation read from kwlan.org) is much more general:
- Thm 8.6 reads: "Suppose R is an O_{F0,(p)}-algebra, and suppose that E is a quasi-coherent sheaf over M^tor_{H,Σ} that is formally canonical (resp. formally subcanonical) over R ... Then R^i(∮_{H,Σ})_* E(−nD′) = 0 for all i > 0 and n > 0 (resp. n ≥ 0)."
- The introduction states that the models work "when the image H^p of H under G(Ẑ) → G(Ẑ^p) is neat ... regardless of the levels and ramifications involved at p."

The paper's proof of Thm 6.1.5.1 (p. 29) says that X_Kli(p) is built in [49] and [50] by normalisation, and on p. 101 the paper itself applies [50] to X_Kli(p) → X*_Kli(p). (There it cites "thm. 8.9", but 8.9 is a Remark in [50].) Ω^{(k,r)}(−D) is the subcanonical extension of an automorphic bundle, which is the intended case. Three further points are formal:
- X^{≥1}_{Kli}(p) is the preimage of the open X^{*,≥1}_{Kli}(p) (p. 101), and relative vanishing is local on the target.
- Reduction mod p^n follows from flatness.
- R^iπ_* commutes with the Ha-colimit, and the quotient term follows from the long exact sequence.

So the p. 71 claim, and its implicit use in Cor. 11.1.3.1, is covered by the cited source.

Part 2, what remains. On p. 72 the sheaf F^κ_{m,n} = (π_{m,n})_*(O_{IG(p^m)_n} ⊗ Λ_n)[κ_{m,n}] is a pushforward along a non-finite affine étale map, so it is not coherent. It exists only on the open X^{≥1}_{Kli}(p)_n, whereas Thm 8.6 is stated for sheaves on all of M^tor, where H_1 need not be multiplicative at the boundary. The paper never checks Def. 8.5 for it, and Lan's proof via [17, Thm 3.9] works with formal completions along fibres; for a non-coherent sheaf that step does not follow formally. The paper itself takes a separate argument for the analogous non-finite sheaves in Part III: Prop. 12.9.2.1, plus smallness via [3] A.1.3.1 in Lemma 12.9.2.1. That contrast suggests the one-line citation on p. 72 is not enough. My local analysis (see the correction) indicates the vanishing is true, so this is an omitted verification rather than an error.

Consequences. The acyclic resolutions give the two-term flat complexes behind Thm 11.3.1 (U locally finite; fRΓ perfect over Λ in degrees [0,1]; the control maps 3 and 4). These feed Thm 1.1 and §14.8. Because the missing step can be filled, only the proof is affected.

Repair: only the Thm 11.3.1 citation needs one. Affineness from Lemma 9.1.1.1 plus the local structure at the boundary is the right approach and close to minimal, but it needs to be combined with [50] Def. 8.5, as described above.

sourceIssues.correction:
Add a proof of point 2. The following argument is close to minimal.

(i) Pass to the limit over n in the resolutions, as in the proof of Thm 11.2.1. This gives a two-term representative M• in degrees [0,1]. Its terms are Λ-flat and complete, because 𝔉^κ is invertible over O ⊗̂ Λ (§9.3). So M• lies in C^flat(Λ), and fM• is a termwise direct summand of it.

(ii) For p odd, write Λ = Z_p[μ_{p−1}] ⊗ Z_p[[1+pZ_p]] ≅ ∏_{i mod p−1} Λ_i, using the idempotents of Z_p[μ_{p−1}]. Each Λ_i ≅ Z_p[[T]] is complete local noetherian with residue field F_p. For p = 2, Λ ≅ Z_2[C_2][[T]] is already local.

(iii) For each i, choose k ≡ i mod p−1 with k ≥ C. Then e_i fM• ⊗ Λ_i/m_i = fM• ⊗_{Λ,k} F_p. The mod-p quasi-isomorphism proved just above (equivalently, point 3 ⊗^L F_p) identifies this with fRΓ(X^{≥1}_{Kli}(p)_1, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)). That complex has finite cohomology by Cor. 11.1.3.1(5), or by Thm 11.2.1(7) together with point 3.

(iv) Prop. 2.2.1 over Λ_i then shows that e_i fM• is quasi-isomorphic to a perfect complex in degrees [0,1]. Taking the product over i, fM• is perfect over Λ in degrees [0,1].

Only finiteness of the cohomology mod m_i is needed. The amplitude [0,1] comes from the representative itself.

I read the rendered pp. 69–73, 56 and 7, and checked the HAL v3 text. The proof of Theorem 11.3.1 builds the acyclic resolution. It proves the mod-p quasi-isomorphism fRΓ(X_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)) → fRΓ(X_1, 𝓕^k_{1,1}⊗ω²(−D)) for k > p+1, then the identity f colim_m RΓ(X_1, 𝓕^k_{m,1}⊗ω²(−D)) = fRΓ(X_1, Ω^{(k,r)}(−D)). Lemma 2.1.2 then gives point 1, and the case k > p+1 is removed. The only closing sentence covers "the points 3 and 4". Point 2 (perfectness over Λ, amplitude [0,1]) is never mentioned. The tools it needs, Prop. 2.2.1 and Cor. 11.1.3.1(5) (or Thm 11.2.1(7)), are not cited in the proof. Prop. 2.2.2, which is cited, is a quasi-isomorphism criterion and does not give perfectness. So a stated result is asserted with no proof: this is a gap in the sense of PROTOCOL §18.

There is also a second problem. §2 is set up only for a complete local noetherian R with finite residue field. Λ = Z_p[[Z_p^×]] ≅ Z_p[μ_{p−1}] ⊗ Z_p[[1+pZ_p]] ≅ ∏_{p−1} Z_p[[T]] is only semi-local for p odd. So "locally finite" (Def. 2.1.1), Lemma 2.1.2 and Props 2.2.1–2.2.2 do not literally apply over Λ. Working over R = Z_p instead fails: the ordinary part mod p is a finite F_p[[T]]-module, not a finite F_p-module. The fix is routine: decompose by the idempotents and work factor by factor. Every ingredient of the repair is already in the paper, so the result stands and 'affects' is 'nothing'. My confidence is medium only because this is a minor omission in the write-up rather than a failing step. Defence attempted and failed.

(a) The proof establishes point 1: "We deduce from lemma 2.1.2 that U is locally finite …". Its only other conclusion is the closing sentence, which names points 3 and 4 only. Point 2 is never mentioned. The proof does not cite Prop. 2.2.1, which is the only perfectness criterion in §2. Unlike the proof of Thm 11.2.1 ("They are objects of C^flat(Z_p) by construction"), it also never says that the limit complex is Λ-flat and complete.

(b) A charitable reading does not rescue it. The proof of Thm 11.2.1 itself gets its perfectness point 7 "by another application of proposition 2.2.2", which should be 2.2.1. So "proposition 2.2.2" in the closing sentence might loosely stand for §2.2 as a whole. Even so, that sentence claims only points 3 and 4.

(c) The intended argument is the one given in the correction. The introduction (p. 3) says the integral control theorem for k ≫ 0 is used "to show that M is a perfect complex". It is not carried out anywhere else in the paper. Footnote 24 on p. 101 cites "theorem 11.3.1, point 2" as the place where the degrees [0,1] are established.

(d) The fix works, so the statement is true. For each maximal ideal of Λ one picks k ≥ C in the matching class, which is always possible. Reduction modulo that ideal gives fRΓ(X^{≥1}_{Kli}(p)_1, Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)), by the mod-p comparison proved in the text on pp. 72–73. That complex is finite by Cor. 11.1.3.1(5), and Prop. 2.2.1 applies.

(e) The semi-local point is correct. For p odd, μ_{p−1} ⊂ Z_p and p−1 is prime to p, so Z_p[μ_{p−1}] ≅ Z_p^{p−1} and Λ ≅ Z_p[[T]]^{p−1}. This ring is not local, while §2 assumes a complete local noetherian ring. Applying §2 factor by factor is routine. The same issue affects the use of Lemma 2.1.2 for point 1; this overlaps with sourceIssues E5.

- Thm 1.1 (M is perfect of amplitude [0,1]).
- Lemma 14.8.4 (Euler characteristics are "locally constant functions of k … by theorem 11.3.1").
- Footnote 24.
- §15.2: the Hecke-generated subalgebra is a finite Λ-algebra, the localisation uses [41] lem. 2.12, and Thm 15.2.1 concerns the Euler characteristic of the perfect complex, hence Thm 1.2.

All of these stand once point 2 is supplied as above. I set 'affects' to 'the proof' rather than 'nothing': as written, the proof of Thm 11.3.1 does not prove one of its four points, although no stated result fails.

review.reason: Confirmed as a gap, and it is visible from the shape of the printed proof. Theorem 11.3.1 has four numbered points, point 2 being `The complex $f\mathrm R\Gamma(X^{\geq1}_{\mathrm{Kli}}(p),\mathfrak F^\kappa\otimes\omega^2(-D))$ is a perfect complex of $\Lambda$-modules concentrated in degree $[0,1]$'. The proof runs from p. 71 to p. 73 and ends `Moreover, proposition 2.2.2 and theorem 11.2.1 imply directly the points 3 and 4 of the theorem.' Point 1 is settled in the paragraph before; point 2 is never returned to. The correction's argument is the natural one and uses only results the paper has: the limit of the resolutions gives a two-term $\Lambda$-flat representative, $\Lambda\cong\prod_{i\bmod p-1}\Lambda_i$ with $\Lambda_i\cong\Z_p[[T]]$ local for $p$ odd, and point 3 with Cor. 11.1.3.1 gives finiteness of the cohomology mod $\mathfrak m_i$, which is exactly the input Prop. 2.2.1 needs. The amplitude comes from the representative, so no separate argument is needed for it.

sourceIssues.locator: §12.2.2, proof of Lemma 12.2.2.1, p. 74 (author version, 17 June 2019); HAL v3 §12.2.2, Lemma 12.2.2.1, PDF p. 64
sourceIssues.printed: Author version p. 74, checked on the page image: "Let us assume that c, f are units for example. We deduce that HT(e_2) = \frac{a}{c} HT(e_3) and that Fil^{can}_ε is generated by HT(e_2), a direct factor is provided by the submodule generated by HT(e_4). □". Earlier in the proof the matrix of HT is the 2×4 matrix with rows (0 a c e) and (0 b d f), and the proof gives "ad − bc = 0" and "cf − de is a unit in R_ε". HAL v3 (hal-01393374v3, PDF p. 64, checked on the page image) has the same text word for word, except that it writes "sub-module" and says "the matrix of Hodge-Tate".
sourceIssues.correction: "... We deduce that HT(e_2) = (a/c) HT(e_3) and that Fil^{can}_ε is generated by HT(e_3), a direct factor is provided by the submodule generated by HT(e_4)."
sourceIssues.reason: I redid the computation. The columns of the printed 2×4 matrix are HT(e_1) = 0, HT(e_2) = (a,b), HT(e_3) = (c,d) and HT(e_4) = (e,f). The relation ad − bc = 0 agrees with J from §5.1: J = [[0,A],[−A,0]] with A antidiagonal, so e_1 pairs with e_4 and e_2 pairs with e_3. A Lagrangian kernel containing e_1 therefore lies in ⟨e_1,e_2,e_3⟩. Suppose c is a unit. Then b = ad/c, so HT(e_2) = (a, ad/c) = (a/c)·HT(e_3), as printed. Hence Fil^can_ε = ⟨HT(e_2), HT(e_3)⟩ = R_ε·HT(e_3). This is free of rank one because c is a unit. HT(e_3) and HT(e_4) form a basis of R_ε^2 because det[[c,e],[d,f]] = cf − de is a unit, so HT(e_4) spans a direct complement. HT(e_2) = (a/c)HT(e_3) generates Fil only when a is a unit, and nothing forces that. So the printed "generated by HT(e_2)" is wrong under the stated assumptions; the correct generator is HT(e_3). The same holds in the other case (d, e units), where HT(e_2) = (b/d)HT(e_3). The paragraph right after the proof supports this reading: X(p^n,ε) is covered by X(p^n,ε,e_2) and X(p^n,ε,e_3), where HT(e_2), respectively HT(e_3), generates Fil. The case the proof treats (cf − de a unit) is exactly the HT(e_3) chart. The HT(e_2) chart corresponds to af − be being a unit; minors that use column 1 vanish, and ad − bc = 0. This is not a text-layer artefact: the page images of both versions clearly print HT(e_2). The lemma's statement still holds (locally free of rank one, locally a direct summand), because the corrected argument proves it. The later uses at pp. 81–84 (the X(p^n,ε,e_2)^?, X(p^n,ε,e_3)^? covering and the Mayer–Vietoris-type sequence) depend only on the lemma and the covering, both of which are correct. So the misprint is a one-symbol slip (e_2 for e_3) and affects nothing downstream.

review.reason: Confirmed, and I redid the computation. The proof prints `Let us assume that $c,f$ are units for example. We deduce that $\mathrm{HT}(e_2)=\frac ac\mathrm{HT}(e_3)$ and that $\mathrm{Fil}^{\mathrm{can}}_\epsilon$ is generated by $\mathrm{HT}(e_2)$, a direct factor is provided by the submodule generated by $\mathrm{HT}(e_4)$.' With the printed matrix the columns are $\mathrm{HT}(e_2)=(a,b)$ and $\mathrm{HT}(e_3)=(c,d)$, and the relation $ad-bc=0$ with $c$ invertible gives exactly $\mathrm{HT}(e_2)=(a/c)\mathrm{HT}(e_3)$, so the first half is right; but that same relation makes $\mathrm{HT}(e_2)$ a multiple of $\mathrm{HT}(e_3)$, and $a$ need not be a unit, so the rank-one sheaf generated by $\mathrm{HT}(e_2)$ and $\mathrm{HT}(e_3)$ is generated by $\mathrm{HT}(e_3)$. The complement is right as printed, since $\det(\mathrm{HT}(e_3),\mathrm{HT}(e_4))=cf-de$ is the unit the proof has just assumed. So the one symbol to change is the generator, as the finding says.

sourceIssues.locator: §12.4 (Group action), p. 75, 2nd paragraph, first line (author version). This is not in HAL v3: HAL v3 (printed p. 64 = PDF p. 65) reads 'We let 𝔗_{w'} be the formal scheme in groups defined by ...' with no range for w'. The slip was introduced in the author version.
sourceIssues.printed: "For all rational numbers w' ≥ 0, we let 𝔗_{w'} be the formal group scheme defined by 𝔗_{w'}(R) = Z_p^×(1 + p^{w'}R) for all R in Adm. We let 𝔗^0_{w'} be the connected component of the identity in 𝔗_{w'}. For all R in Adm, 𝔗^0_{w'}(R) = 1 + p^{w'}R."
sourceIssues.correction: For all rational numbers w' > 0
sourceIssues.reason: For w' = 0 the definition does not give a group. Take R = O ∈ Adm: 1 + p^0 R = 1 + O = O, which contains 0, so 𝔗_0(O) = Z_p^× · O = O is not a subgroup of O^×. Formally, 1/(1+X) does not converge in O⟨X⟩, so R ↦ 1 + R is only a formal monoid. For w' > 0, p^{w'}R is topologically nilpotent in the p-adically complete R, so 1 + p^{w'}R is a group. Every later use has w' > 0: §12.3 says 'positive rational numbers w' ≤ w', and §12.6.2 says '0 < w' ≤ w ≤ ε', which governs §§12.6–14. The intended range is therefore clearly w' > 0.

sourceIssues.printed: "Using a covering as in section 12.5, 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'}|_{Spf R} is identified with the set of matrices (1 0; p^w𝔅(0,1)_R 1) × (1 + p^{w'}𝔅(0,1)_R). The action of 𝔗^0_w is on the right term. It follows that 𝔊^{κ_A,w}(Spf R × Spf A) ≃ R⊗̂A⟨X⟩."
sourceIssues.correction: The action of 𝔗^0_{w'} is on the right term.
sourceIssues.reason: On the same page, π_1 : 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'} → 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w} is a 𝔗^0_{w'}-torsor, and 𝔏^{κ_A} = ((π_1)_*O ⊗̂ A)^{𝔗^0_{w'}}, with invariants 'taken with respect to the diagonal action of 𝔗^0_{w'}'. The right factor is 1 + p^{w'}𝔅(0,1)_R = 𝔗^0_{w'}, on which 𝔗^0_{w'} acts simply transitively. That simple transitivity is what gives 𝔊^{κ_A,w}(Spf R × Spf A) ≃ R⊗̂A⟨X⟩. 𝔗^0_w is only a subgroup (w ≥ w'), and its invariants alone would not give that isomorphism. The subscript should be w'.

sourceIssues.printed: We let π_3 : 𝔛(p^n,ε) → 𝔛_Kli(p^n,ε) be the finite projection. The sheaf (π_3)_⋆𝔊^{κ_A,w} is 𝔗_{w,n}-equivariant. We define a Banach sheaf 𝔉^{κ_A,w} = ((π_3)_⋆𝔊^{κ_A,w})^{𝔗_{w,n}} = (π_⋆𝒪_{𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'}} ⊗̂ A)^{𝔗_{w,n}} over 𝔛_Kli(p^n,ε) × Spf A.
sourceIssues.correction: Replace 𝔗_{w,n} by 𝔗_{w',n}, as defined in §12.4. This is essential in the second expression, (π_⋆𝒪_{𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'}} ⊗̂ A)^{𝔗_{w',n}}. It is harmless but consistent in the other two places. This matches the analytic definition on p. 79, (π_⋆𝒪_{𝓕𝓛^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'}} ⊗̂ A)^{𝒯_{w',n}}.
sourceIssues.reason:
§12.4 (p. 75) defines 𝔗_{w',n} = 𝔗_{w'} ×_{𝔗_{w'}/𝔗^0_{w'}} 𝔎𝔩𝔦(ℤ/p^nℤ). It says that the 𝔗^0_{w'}-action on 𝔉𝔏^+_{n,ε,w,w'} (a 𝔗^0_{w'}-torsor over 𝔉𝔏_{n,ε,w}) extends to an action of 𝔗_{w',n}. With the dummy variable renamed, 𝔗_{w,n} is a subgroup of 𝔗_{w',n} that contains only 𝔗^0_w ⊆ 𝔗^0_{w'}.

First expression: 𝔗^0_{w'} already acts trivially on 𝔊^{κ_A,w} = (π_2)_⋆((π_1)_⋆𝒪 ⊗̂ A)^{𝔗^0_{w'}}, and 𝔗_{w,n} maps onto 𝔎𝔩𝔦(ℤ/p^n). So ((π_3)_⋆𝔊)^{𝔗_{w,n}} equals the 𝔎𝔩𝔦-invariants, which equal ((π_3)_⋆𝔊)^{𝔗_{w',n}}. That expression is therefore correct even as printed.

Second expression: this one is wrong for w' < w. In the local chart of §12.5, 𝔉𝔏^+ = 𝔉𝔏 × (1 + p^{w'}𝔅(0,1)). Invariants of 𝒪 ⊗̂ A under the diagonal action of 𝔗^0_w = 1 + p^w(·) only impose κ_A-equivariance along the smaller group. They give a strictly larger sheaf, namely functions on the 𝔗^0_{w'}/𝔗^0_w-torsor 𝔉𝔏^+/𝔗^0_w, not π_⋆𝔏^{κ_A}. With 𝔗_{w',n} one gets the intended sheaf, as in the p. 79 definition.

The cause is a leftover from HAL v3, where w and w' played swapped roles (𝔏^{κ_A} was defined with 𝔗^0_w). A separate minor point, not part of this issue: π in the second expression is the map to 𝔛(p^n,ε) (p. 76), so strictly one means π_3∘π.

sourceIssues.printed: p. 78 (checked on the page image at 110 and 250 dpi): "Let us denote by 𝓕𝓛^+ → 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n, e_1)^+ the moduli space of flags (a locally direct summand of rank 1 in this case) Fil ω_G of ω_G together with a trivialization ρ ∈ Grω_G = ω_G/Filω_G^(18)." and "Lemma 12.7.2.2. — The space 𝓕𝓛^+_{n,ε,w,w'} descends to an open-subspace of 𝓕𝓛^+ → 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n, e_1)^+ that we denote by 𝓕𝓛^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'}. This is the space of flags Filω_G ⊂ ω_G and trivialization ρ ∈ Gr_{ω_G} which satisfy the following conditions : — (Filω_G ∩ ω_G^{mod,+})_w = Fil^{can}_w, — The trivialization ρ belongs to ω_G^{mod,+}/(Filω_G ∩ ω_G^{mod,+}) and reduces to the element HT_4(1) of Gr^{can}_{w'}." In both places the second argument is an italic e with subscript 1 (e_1), not ε.
sourceIssues.correction: Replace 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n, e_1)^+ with 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n, ε)^+ in both places.
sourceIssues.reason: The page image confirms the printed e_1 in both places; this is not a text-layer artefact. Under the paper's own notation the second argument of 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n, ·) is the rational number ε ∈ [0, n−1/(p−1)] ∩ Q. See §12.7.1, p. 77: "We denote by 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε) ⊂ 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n) the quotient of 𝒳(p^n,ε) by 𝔎𝔩𝔦(Z/p^n) and by 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε)^+ ⊂ 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n)^+ the quotient of 𝒳(p^n,ε) by 𝔎𝔩𝔦(Z/p^n)^+". e_1 is the first basis vector of (Z/p^nZ)^4 (§12.2.2). The only spaces indexed by basis vectors are 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i) for i ∈ {2,3}, which take three arguments. No 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n, e_1) is defined anywhere: a search of the text finds only these two occurrences. ε is the right base, for three reasons. (1) FL^+_{n,ε,w,w'} lies over 𝒳(p^n,ε), which is the space that is quotiented to give 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε)^+. (2) The second condition uses HT_4(1). On p. 78 this map is defined only "Over 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε)^+ … obtained via the map ψ", where ψ is the universal trivialization of H_n^D. So the base has to be the '+' space at level ε. (3) The companion Lemma 12.7.2.1, immediately before, descends to FL → 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε). The notation cannot be read charitably. P_Kli is the stabiliser of ⟨e_1⟩ (§5.1.2, p. 20), but that is already encoded in the subscript "Kli", and "e_1" is not an admissible value for the ε slot. Even if one read it as 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n)^+, the notation is still undefined; ε is the reading that agrees with everything around it. Nothing downstream uses 'e_1'. On p. 79 the projection is π : FL^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'} → 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε), the composite through the '+' space, followed by T_{w',n}-invariants. Corollary 13.2.2.1 (p. 86) uses only FL^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'}. The proof of Lemma 13.3.2.1 (p. 89) defines its own FL^+ as the G_m-torsor over FL → 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε). That is a separate minor inconsistency ('+' vs no '+'), not part of this finding. So the slip changes no statement or argument. HAL v3 has the same text: PDF p. 68 (printed p. 67), "Let us denote by 𝓕𝓛^+ → 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n, e_1)^+ the moduli space of flags …" and "Lemma 12.7.2.2. — The space 𝓕𝓛^+_{n,ε,w',w} descends to an open-subspace of 𝓕𝓛^+ → 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n, e_1)^+ …". The v3 lemma has a different subscript order and a condition "ρ reduces to the element HT(1)", but the e_1 slip is the same.

sourceIssues.locator: §12.8.2, proof of Proposition 12.8.2.1, p. 79 (author version, 17 June 2019); in HAL v3 it is the same proposition number on printed p. 68 (PDF p. 69)
sourceIssues.printed: "The 𝒰-Čech complex of the sheaf ℒ^{κ_A} ⊗ ω^r is a bounded complex of projective Banach A[1/p]-modules which computes RΓ(𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε), 𝒢^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r). The group 𝔎𝔩𝔦(ℤ/p^nℤ) acts on this complex and the direct factor of invariants computes the cohomology RΓ(𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε), ℱ^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r)." (checked on the page rendered at 300 dpi: the subscript "Kli" is clearly printed on 𝒳 in the first RΓ)
sourceIssues.correction: "... which computes RΓ(𝒳(p^n,ε), 𝒢^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r) (= RΓ(ℱℒ_{n,ε,w}, ℒ^{κ_A} ⊗ ω^r))". The subscript Kli should be dropped from 𝒳.
sourceIssues.reason: The paper puts 𝒢^{κ_A,w} on the full level space, not on the Klingen quotient. On p. 78 it says: "We denote by 𝒢^{κ_A,w} the Banach sheaf generic fiber of 𝔊^{κ_A,w} over 𝒳(p^n,ε) × Spa(A[1/p],A)". Here 𝔊^{κ_A,w} = (π_2)_* ℒ^{κ_A} over X(p^n,ε) × Spf A (§12.6.2, p. 76). The Klingen-level sheaf is the separate sheaf ℱ^{κ_A,w} = ((π_3)_* 𝔊^{κ_A,w})^{T_{w,n}}, with π_3 : X(p^n,ε) → X_{Kli}(p^n,ε) (p. 77). The display just above the proposition (p. 79) is exactly the corrected identity: RΓ(𝒳(p^n,ε), 𝒢^{κ_A,w}⊗ω^r) = RΓ(ℱℒ_{n,ε,w}, ℒ^{κ_A}⊗ω^r). The proof takes a covering 𝒰 of ℱℒ_{n,ε,w}, so its Čech complex computes RΓ(ℱℒ_{n,ε,w}, ℒ^{κ_A}⊗ω^r), which equals RΓ(𝒳(p^n,ε), 𝒢⊗ω^r). The next sentence takes 𝔎𝔩𝔦(ℤ/p^nℤ)-invariants to reach the Klingen level. That step only makes sense if the complex is still at full level 𝒳(p^n,ε), which matches the second display, RΓ(𝒳_{Kli}, ℱ⊗ω^r) = RΓ(𝔎𝔩𝔦(ℤ/p^nℤ), RΓ(ℱℒ_{n,ε,w}, ℒ⊗ω^r)). The same pattern appears in Corollary 12.9.2.1 on p. 80: H^i(𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε), ℱ⊗ω^r(−D)) = H^0(Kli(ℤ/p^n), H^i(𝒳(p^n,ε), 𝒢⊗ω^r(−D))). One charitable reading is RΓ(𝒳_{Kli}, (π_3)_*𝒢), which gives the same thing because π_3 is finite. But the paper always writes that pushforward explicitly, so as printed the formula names a space the sheaf does not live on. It is a subscript slip, not a mathematical error: the corrected argument goes through unchanged. HAL v3 (printed p. 68, PDF p. 69) has the identical sentence ("𝒰-Chech complex ... computes RΓ(𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε), 𝒢^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r)"), so the slip was there in 2018 and was not fixed by June 2019. Whether the Duke version fixes it cannot be checked because that text is paywalled.

sourceIssues.reason:
The symbol 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^{⋆−mod} is not defined anywhere. The only occurrences of '⋆−mod' attached to (p^n,ε,e_i) are these two. The paper defines 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod}, the space 𝔛(p^n,ε)^⋆ ⊂ 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod} (p. 80), and the opens 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^⋆ ⊂ 𝔛(p^n,ε)^⋆ (p. 81, top).

The fibre product on the right is the locus of 𝔛(p^n)^{⋆−mod} where s_{i,4} generates and s_{1,j} ∈ p^ε det ω^{mod}. Since s_{i,j} ≡ HT(e_i)∧HT(e_j) mod p^ε, this is exactly 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^⋆: the condition HT(e_1)∧HT(e_j) ≡ 0 mod p^ε plus the requirement that HT(e_4)∧HT(e_i) generates.

The lemma is used, through Theorem 12.9.2.1, in the proof of Lemma 12.9.2.1 (p. 83) for affine coverings of 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^⋆. HAL v3's proof also writes 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^⋆. The intended object is therefore clear.

sourceIssues.printed: Proof. The formal scheme 𝔛(p^n,ε) carries a stratification indexed by a subset of the set of all Lagrangian locally direct factors W of V = ℤ^4. […] The case W = {0} corresponds to the open and dense stratum with complement the boundary D. […] We now deal with the case W is one-dimensional. […] In the case W is two dimensional, …
sourceIssues.correction: '… indexed by a subset of the set of all totally isotropic locally direct factors W of V = ℤ^4.'
sourceIssues.reason:
V = ℤ^4 carries a symplectic form of rank 4, so a Lagrangian direct factor has rank exactly 2. The strata listed immediately afterwards, however, are W = {0}, W one-dimensional and W two-dimensional. Only the last of these are Lagrangian.

The paper's own boundary index set is 'the set of totally isotropic direct factors W ⊂ V' (§6.1.5.2, p. 27; see also §5.1.2). The standard stratification of a toroidal compactification of a Siegel threefold is indexed the same way. The word 'Lagrangian' is therefore a slip for 'totally isotropic', and the intended meaning is clear from the list that follows.

sourceIssues.reason:
I rendered pp. 82–83 at 130 and 250 dpi. Item 1 has no hat, while item 2 has one.

(a) The missing completion in item 1 is a notational slip. The theorem on formal functions computes the completion of the coherent sheaf R^iπ_*𝒪(−D) along the image of ℨ_W/Γ_W, which is finite over Spf 𝒪. The toroidal fibre over a 0-dimensional cusp is the union of strata whose cones meet the interior of the positive cone. That union is closed and equals ℨ_W/Γ_W. So the completion equals H^i of the completion of 𝔛 along ℨ_W/Γ_W. By the p. 82 sentence, that is the completion of 𝔐̄_W/Γ_W along ℨ_W/Γ_W. The paper itself separates 𝔐̄_W/Γ_W from this completion on p. 82. Moreover, the uncompleted quotient is not a reasonable object: Γ_W acts on the torus part M_W by group automorphisms and fixes the identity section, so it does not act freely or properly there. AIP's own version ([3] p. 678) says "it suffices to prove that H^q(Z̃_{V'}, 𝒪_{Ẑ}(−D)) = 0", with Z̃_{V'} = Ẑ_{V'}/Γ, the completed object. So the intended meaning is clear from context: a misprint. The same applies to the self-referential definition under item 2.

(b) The "repeat the arguments" step is not a genuine gap. The "equivalent to" step is correct once the completions are read in. The two local statements depend only on the local structure that Pilloni records from [63] thm 4.1:
- Two-dimensional W: this stratum lies in the ordinary locus, where 𝔛(p^n,ϵ) → 𝔛(p^n) is an open immersion. The local model is the completion along ℨ_W of a relative torus embedding for a torus isogenous to Hom(Sym²V/W^⊥, G_m), divided by a neat Γ_W. This is exactly AIP's situation with trivial abelian part. Their Kempf-type argument (Γ-admissible polarization function h, the finite flat maps Φ_ℓ, and the round-down ⌊ℓ^{-1}sD_h⌋ = −D) needs only the fan and the lattice. Replacing the lattice by an isogenous one (adjoining p^n-th roots of the q-parameters) rescales h and changes nothing.
- One-dimensional W: the fan is R_{≥0} and Γ is trivial, since GL_1 is {±1} and the level is neat. 𝔐̄_W is a line-bundle total space over the elliptic curve 𝔅_W (a G_m-torsor with 0 adjoined). The completed cohomology is ∏_{k≥1} H^i(𝔅_{W,x}, N^k), where N is the conormal bundle, which is isogenous to 𝒪(2O) and has positive degree. Hence H^1 = 0 by cohomology and base change on an elliptic curve, which is the [Mum70]-vanishing step of AIP's proof.

§12.9.1 says openly that it "follows [3] section 8 closely". Deferring a verbatim-applicable argument to one's own earlier paper is not an unproved step. Neither the level p^n, nor ω^mod, nor the Hodge–Tate condition enters the local models in a way that breaks the argument. Checked against AIP [3] (author PDF, pp. 46–50). Its proof of 8.2.2.4 reads: "By the theorem of formal functions it suffices to prove that H^q(Z̃_{V'}, O_{Ẑ_{V'}}(−D)) = 0." In AIP, Ẑ is the formal completion and Z̃ = Ẑ/Γ. D sums D_ρ over all rays ρ, explicitly "not simply over the set Σ(1)^o as in the definition of W_Σ". Pilloni's 𝔷_W is a "closed codimension 1" subscheme and its quotient by Γ_W is the closed W-stratum, so it is AIP's W (the interior-ray part), not D. The divisor D_ρ of a boundary ray, such as ρ = x², meets 𝔷_W: the orbit of the cone ⟨x²,y²⟩ lies in both. So O(−𝔷_W) differs from O(−D) on the completion, and item 1 as printed is the wrong group. Also, 𝔐̄_W/Γ_W without completion is not even defined, because Γ_W does not act properly on the torus part; the preceding sentence uses the completion. The intended object is clear from context, since the proposition is about O(−D) and item 2 correctly uses O(−𝔅_W), the full complement. So this is a misprint.

Defence of the "repeat the arguments" step:
(i) W two-dimensional. Pilloni states on p. 82 that the boundary lies in the ordinary locus, where 𝔛(p^n,ε) → 𝔛(p^n)^mod is an open immersion and 𝔛(p^n)^mod → 𝔛(p^n) is an isomorphism. So ω^mod and the HT condition play no role there. The model is the normalisation of the toroidal compactification at full level p^n: a torus embedding with the character lattice uniformly rescaled, which is still smooth for the fan. AIP's own 8.2.2.4 already treats such a normalised level-p^n model, X_1(p^n)(v). Its inputs all survive a finite normalisation: a smooth admissible decomposition, a polarisation function h, the [C-S] splitting, freeness of Γ, and ampleness of O(D'_h) (from FC V.5.8, or AIP's alternative argument via the boundary).
(ii) W one-dimensional. The torus has rank 1 and Γ_W is trivial. The completion is a line bundle over the elliptic curve 𝔅_W completed along its zero section. The cohomology of O(−𝔅_W) is then the product over k ≥ 1 of H^i(𝔅_W, L^k), with L isogenous to O(2O) and hence ample. This vanishes by Mumford §16, which is the argument AIP use in their first proof of Thm 8.2.2.3.
One caveat the text does not address: §12.1 takes O = O_{C_p}, which is not noetherian, so EGA III formal functions needs a routine descent to a finite extension. Everything is finitely presented, so this is standard.

Downstream use: Lemma 12.9.2.1 (p. 83) → Cor. 12.9.2.1 → Prop. 12.9.1 (vanishing of H^i_cusp for i > 1) → §13. The intended statement is right and the proof goes through with the corrected item 1, so nothing downstream is affected.

sourceIssues.reason:
The proof only establishes acyclicity for the two pieces. It says "We deduce from thm 12.9.2.1 that Čech(𝔘_i, …)[1/p] is concentrated in degree 0" for i ∈ {2,3}. That rests on Lemma 12.9.1.3, which gives each 𝔛(p^n,ε,e_i)^⋆ a projective map to an affine that is an isomorphism on generic fibres. The Čech complex of 𝔘 = 𝔘_2 ∪ 𝔘_3 is quasi-isomorphic to the Mayer–Vietoris total complex [Čech(𝔘_2) ⊕ Čech(𝔘_3) → Čech(𝔘_2∩𝔘_3)]. Acyclicity on the pieces alone gives exact sequences 0 → H^0 → H^0(X_2)⊕H^0(X_3) → H^0(X_23) → H^1 → 0 and H^{j+1}(FL) ≅ H^j(X_23) for j ≥ 1. So the claimed concentration in degrees 0 and 1 is equivalent to H^j(X_2∩X_3, π_⋆𝒢⊗ω^r(−D)) = 0 for j ≥ 1, and the text never states or proves this.

Defence attempted. The intersection is not affine, because the pieces themselves are only projective over affines, not affine. It is affinoid on the generic fibre, but π_⋆𝒢 is a Banach sheaf on the minimal compactification, not a coherent sheaf. Being affinoid therefore gives no acyclicity; Theorem 12.9.2.1 with a formal model is what supplies it. The strategy in the §12.9 introduction ("covered by two affines") shows this is what the author meant. The analogous argument in §14 (proof on p. 91 onward) has no such gap, because there the covering opens are genuinely affine and D(s_1)∩D(s_2) = D(s_1 s_2). Here the gap is filled by one line, since Theorem 12.9.2.1 applies to the intersection exactly as to the pieces (see the correction). So the step is asserted without justification, but it is true.

Downstream: Lemma 12.9.2.1 → Corollary 12.9.2.1 → Proposition 12.9.1 (vanishing of H^i_cusp(†,κ_A,r) for i > 1) → §13.4 (C_cusp(A_l) concentrated in degrees 0 and 1; Proposition 13.4.1) and footnote 24 in §14. None of these is endangered, because the gap is routinely filled.

sourceIssues.locator: §13.1.1 (Slope decomposition), condition 4 in the definition of an h-slope decomposition, p. 84 of the author version (17 June 2019). HAL v3: §13.1.1, printed p. 72 (PDF p. 73), same wording.
sourceIssues.printed: 4. For any polynomial Q with roots of valuation strictly greater than h, the restriction of Q^⋆(U) to M^{>h} is an invertible endomorphism. Here Q^⋆ is the reciprocal of Q.
sourceIssues.correction: Minimal fix: replace "with roots of valuation strictly greater than h" by "with roots of valuation ≥ −h". This is Urban's "Q of slope ≤ h" ([81] §2.3.1), whose reciprocal Q^⋆ has all its roots of valuation ≤ h. An equivalent form: P(U)|_{M^{>h}} is invertible for every nonzero polynomial P whose roots (in k̄) all have valuation ≤ h. Variants of this correction that add the side condition "Q(0) a unit" or "Q(0) ≠ 0" are also right and equivalent; these side conditions are harmless but not needed. Rescaling Q does not affect invertibility, and a root 0 (valuation +∞ ≥ −h) only lowers the degree of Q^⋆.
sourceIssues.reason:
The printed text matches the page image at 150 dpi exactly. In HAL v3 condition 4 is word-for-word the same; only condition 3 differs, lacking "(in an algebraic closure of k)". The text layers of HAL v1 and v2 give the same condition 4.

Why the printed condition fails:
- The paper uses "reciprocal" in the standard sense, X^d Q(1/X) (compare §5.1.5, p. 23: "the roots of the reciprocal of Θ(Q_ℓ(X))").
- For Q = c∏(X−α_i) this gives Q^⋆(U) = c∏(1−α_i U). Its invertibility only says that U − β is invertible for β = 1/α_i, and these have v(β) < −h. That is the wrong condition.

Counterexample: k = Q_p, M = k^2, U = diag(1,p), h = 1/2.
- Decomposition A: M^{≤h} = 0 and M^{>h} = M. Condition 3 is vacuous. For condition 4, Q^⋆(U) = diag(c∏(1−α_i), c∏(1−pα_i)). Here v(α_i) > 1/2, so 1−α_i and 1−pα_i are units, and a root α_i = 0 gives a factor 1.
- Decomposition B: M^{≤h} = ke_1 (eigenvalue 1, valuation 0 ≤ 1/2) and M^{>h} = ke_2. It also satisfies conditions 1–4 as printed.
- So the uniqueness asserted right after the definition ("By [81], coro. 2.3.3 ... it is unique") is false under the printed definition.
- Reading "reciprocal" as 1/Q does not rescue it. Then Q(U) must be invertible when v(root) > h, and Q = X−p kills e_2, so neither A nor B qualifies and no decomposition exists at all.

Checked against [81] (Urban, Ann. of Math. 174 (2011), §2.3.1, from the Annals PDF):
- Urban says Q is of slope ≤ h "if Q(0) ∈ O_L^× and if the roots of Q^*(X) := X^d Q(1/X) ... have their slope ... less or equal to h".
- His condition (4) reads: "For any polynomial Q of slope ≤ h, the restriction of Q^*(u) to M_2 is an invertible endomorphism of M_2".
- So Urban requires roots of Q of valuation ≥ −h, not > h, and the proposed correction states exactly that.
- Equivalence with the P(U) form: P ↦ P^⋆ is a bijection, up to scalars, between polynomials with P(0) ≠ 0 and roots of valuation ≥ −h and polynomials with roots of valuation ≤ h, and P^⋆⋆ = P.
- Under the corrected condition, uniqueness holds even with Pilloni's condition 3. Take P = the characteristic polynomial of U on M_1. P(U) kills M_1 and is invertible on M_2'. This forces M_1 ⊂ M_1', and M_2 ⊂ M_2' follows the same way.
- In the counterexample the correction rules out A: Q = 1−X gives Q^⋆(U) = diag(0, p−1).

Why it affects nothing:
- The intended notion is clear from the citation of [81] and from the use of Serre [72] and Coleman [14] for existence.
- The later uses all rely on the standard notion: Prop. 13.1.3.1, §13.2–13.3, Lemma 14.7.1, Rem. 14.8.1 (H^{>0} = (1−f)H) and "0-slope decomposition is functorial" (§14, near p. 107).
- The Duke version was not available to compare. The printed text matches the page image at 130 dpi. The paper defines "reciprocal" as X^d Q(1/X). This is its only meaning in the paper: the Hecke polynomial Q_ℓ(X) = 1 − T_{ℓ,2}X + … has "reciprocal" with roots the Hecke parameters (§5.1.5, p. 23; also p. 32).

Defence attempts, all failing:
(a) Literal reading. For Q = c∏(X−α_i) with v(α_i) > h, Q^⋆(U) = c∏(1−α_iU). Its invertibility only excludes eigenvalues 1/α_i, which have valuation < −h, so this is the wrong condition.
(b) "Roots" read as roots of Q^⋆ (valuation > h). Then eigenvalues of valuation > h are excluded from M^{>h}, the opposite of what is wanted.
(c) Reading Q(U) in place of Q^⋆(U) gives the same opposite condition.
No sign convention rescues it: v(p) = 1 is fixed on the same page.

Counterexamples to the uniqueness claimed in the next line (I checked both):
- M = k, U = 1, h = 0. Both (M^{≤0}, M^{>0}) = (M, 0) and (0, M) qualify, since Q^⋆(1) = c∏(1−β_j) is a unit when v(β_j) > 0.
- M = k², U = diag(1, p), h = 1/2. Both (0, M) and (ke₁, ke₂) qualify.
Under the printed definition, existence also fails for h < 0. Take M = k, U = 1, h = −1. Condition 3 forces M^{≤−1} = 0, and Q = X − 1 (root of valuation 0 > −1) gives Q^⋆(U) = 1 − U = 0. So the claim in §13.1.3 that [72] gives a slope decomposition would also fail as printed.

Urban's definition, checked in the local copy of Ann. Math. 174, §2.3.1: Q is of slope ≤ h if Q(0) ∈ O_L^× and the roots of Q*(X) := X^d Q(1/X) have valuation ≤ h. His condition (4) is "For any polynomial Q of slope ≤ h, the restriction of Q*(u) to M_2 is an invertible endomorphism". This is exactly the correction.

Uniqueness holds under the corrected definition together with Pilloni's condition 3. Let P be the characteristic polynomial of U on M₁. Its roots are nonzero, since condition 3 excludes eigenvalue 0 (valuation +∞). P(U) kills M₁ and is invertible on M₂', which gives M₁ ⊂ M₁'. The argument is symmetric, and M₂ ⊂ M₂' follows the same way.

Later uses, all of which import the standard notion from its sources:
- the uniqueness sentence ([81] Cor. 2.3.3) and the definition of M^{=h} and M^{<h} (p. 84);
- existence via [72] and Prop. 13.1.3.1 via [14] Part A (pp. 84–85);
- the finite slope part in Cor. 13.2.4.2 (p. 87);
- (M^•)^{≤h} for a compact operator in Lemma 14.7.1 and Thm 14.7.1 (p. 99);
- "0-slope decomposition is functorial" (p. 102), which is [81] Lemma 2.3.2.
Nothing in the paper argues from condition 4 as printed. Every claim is right for the intended notion, which the citation of [81] identifies. So this is a sign or inequality slip in the definition ("≥ −h" printed as "> h"), not a failing step. It affects nothing, though a formaliser must use the corrected definition. It is not an "error" affecting "a stated result": the uniqueness claim after the definition is false only under the literal misprinted definition; it is true under the intended one.

sourceIssues.locator: §13.2.1, proof of Lemma 13.2.1.1, last paragraph of p. 85 of the author version. HAL v3 (printed p. 74 = PDF p. 75) has the same sentence. Its preceding sentence is worded '(In case G and G_1 have bad reduction, …)'.
sourceIssues.printed: In case G and G_1 are semi-abelian scheme, one can interpret T_p(G) and T_p(G_1) as the Tate modules of the corresponding 1-motives. We take a basis of T_p(G) ≃ ℤ_p^4 and T_p(G_1) ≃ ℤ_p^4 lifting the basis of G[p^n] and G_1[p^n] provided by the moduli problems. For suitable basis of ω_G and ω_{G_1} respecting the canonical filtration, this diagram is isomorphic to
sourceIssues.correction: Choose bases e_1,…,e_4 of T_p(G) and f_1,…,f_4 of T_p(G_1), adapted to ξ, so that ξ = diag(1,p,p,p^2) (i.e. f_1 = ξ(e_1)) and e_1 lifts a generator of H_n ⊂ G[p^n]. Then f_1 lifts a generator of the level subgroup H_{n+1} = t_2-image ⊂ G_1[p^{n+1}].
sourceIssues.reason:
The moduli problems here are the Klingen-level ones. By p. 77, 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε) 'parametrizes pairs (x,H_n)', and t_2 lands in 𝒴_Kli(p^{n+1}). So no basis of G[p^n] is provided, only the cyclic subgroup H_n. For G_1 the relevant level is p^{n+1}, not p^n: the next page speaks of 'the group generated by the image [1,p,p,p^2](e_1) in G_1[p^{n+1}]'.

Moreover, if bases of G[p^n] and G_1[p^n] were both prescribed independently, ξ could not in general be put in diagonal form. The subsequent computation needs exactly the diagonal form plus the fact that e_1 lifts a generator of H_n, which gives p_1(e_1) ∈ p^ε.

The intended choice exists. Write T = T_p(G) ⊂ T_1 = T_p(G_1) with T_1/T ≅ L. The vector e_1 is primitive in T_1, because p^{-1}e_1 mod T lies in H_n[p] \ {0} and L ∩ H_n = 0. Take elementary-divisor bases (p,p,p^2) of T/ℤ_p e_1 ⊂ T_1/ℤ_p e_1, lift them, and correct the lifts in T by multiples of e_1. This gives ξ = diag(1,p,p,p^2) with f_1 = e_1.

A charitable reading is also possible: lift the geometric point to full level 𝒳(p^n), resp. 𝒳(p^{n+1}). Under it the sentence is merely loose rather than false. Either way, the intended argument is clear from the rest of the proof. Hence this is a misprint (imprecise wording), not a gap. Confidence is medium because the classification between an imprecision and a misprint is a judgement call.

sourceIssues.locator: §13.2.1, definition of the correspondence and proof of Lemma 13.2.1.1, p. 85 of the author version. The same text is in HAL v3 (printed pp. 73–74 = PDF pp. 74–75), apart from the wording '(G,H_n) ∈ 𝒴_Kli(p^n)'.
sourceIssues.printed:
p. 85: 'There is a Hecke correspondence t_1 : C|_{𝒴_Kli(p^n)} → 𝒴_Kli(p^n) where C|_{𝒴_Kli(p^n)} is the moduli space of (G, H_n, L) where (G, H_n) is a point of 𝒴_Kli(p^n) and L ⊂ G[p^2] is a totally isotropic subgroup which is locally for the étale topology isomorphic to (ℤ/pℤ)^2 ⊕ ℤ/p^2ℤ and L ∩ H_n = {0}. The map t_1 sends (G, H_n, L) to (G, H). There is a map t_2 : C_n|_{𝒴_Kli(p^n)} → 𝒴_Kli(p^{n+1}) defined by mapping (G, H_n, L) to (G/L, p^{−1}H_n + L/L).'

Proof of Lemma 13.2.1.1: 'Let (K, 𝒪_K) be a rank one point of C_n corresponding to an isogeny ξ : G → G_1.'
sourceIssues.correction: t_1(G,H_n,L) = (G,H_n). The map is t_2 : C|_{𝒴_Kli(p^n)} → 𝒴_Kli(p^{n+1}), (G,H_n,L) ↦ (G/L, ([p]^{-1}(H_n) + L)/L). In the proof, read 'a rank one point of C_ε'.
sourceIssues.reason:
(1) 'H' is not defined in §13; the level subgroup here is H_n. '(G,H)' is a leftover from the Klingen-level-p correspondence of §10 ('The construction is parallel to section 10').

(2) 'C_n' is not defined in §13. There the objects are C|_{𝒴_Kli(p^n)}, its compactification C, and C_ε = C ×_{t_1} 𝒳_Kli(p^n,ε), which is the space Lemma 13.2.1.1 is about. The parallel proof of Lemma 13.2.2.1 (p. 86) says 'a rank one point of C_ε'. The symbol C_n is later defined in §14.2 for a different object (the n-fold iterate of the correspondence over 𝒳_Kli(p)).

(3) 'p^{-1}H_n + L/L' is shorthand with missing parentheses for the image in G/L of [p]^{-1}(H_n) + L. I checked that this is the right level-p^{n+1} subgroup. L ≅ (ℤ/p)^2 ⊕ ℤ/p^2, so L[p] has order p^3. Since L ∩ H_n = 0, L[p] ⊕ H_n[p] = G[p]. Then L ∩ [p]^{-1}(H_n) = L[p], because pL ⊂ L meets H_n trivially. The image therefore has order p^{n+4}/p^3 = p^{n+1}.

The image is generated by the class of any y with py generating H_n. That class has order p^{n+1}, because p^n y ∈ H_n \ {0} is not in L. So the image is cyclic, as a Klingen p^{n+1} structure must be. It agrees with p. 86, 'the group generated by the image [1,p,p,p^2](e_1) in G_1[p^{n+1}]'.

All of these are notational slips with clear intended meaning.

𝒳(p^{n+1}) → 𝒳_{Kli}(p^{n+1}) ×_{𝒳_{Kli}(p^n)} 𝒳(p^n) is generically a covering with group ker(Kli(ℤ/p^{n+1}) → Kli(ℤ/p^n)), so ℱℒ_{n+1,ε+1,w+1} is not a subspace of it and '\overline{𝒰_i} ⊂ 𝒰'_i' makes no sense. The translates added are under 𝔎𝔩𝔦(ℤ/p^{n+1}ℤ), and the displayed factorization takes (Čech(𝒰',…))^{𝔎𝔩𝔦(ℤ/p^{n+1}ℤ)}, so stability under 𝔎𝔩𝔦(ℤ/p^{n+1}ℤ) is what is needed. 𝔎𝔩𝔦(ℤ/p^nℤ) does not even act on this fibre product. The intended meaning is clear from the first paragraph and from the factorization.

Finally, the trace map Tr : (t_1)_⋆𝒪_{C_ε} → 𝒪_{𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε)} restricts to Tr : (t_1)_⋆𝒪^{++}_{C_ε} → 𝒪^{++}_{𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε)}" (author version p. 88, read from the page image at 110 and 250 dpi; (22) is a footnote mark)
sourceIssues.reason: I checked the page image (p. 88). The printed chain "R^i(t_1)_⋆𝒪^{++}_{C_ε} = (t_1)_⋆𝒪^{++}_{C_ε} = 0 for all i > 0" is what is on the page; it is not a text-layer artefact. The middle term has no index i, so read literally the chain says two things: the pushforward (t_1)_⋆𝒪^{++}_{C_ε} is 0, and R^i equals R^0. Both are wrong. The pushforward is not zero: the very next sentence defines the restricted trace Tr : (t_1)_⋆𝒪^{++}_{C_ε} → 𝒪^{++}_{𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε)} on it, and that trace is what builds p^3U on the ++ complexes. The cited result, Proposition 14.4.1.1(2) (p. 94), says R(t_{n,1})_⋆𝒪^{++} = (t_{n,1})_⋆𝒪^{++}. That means the higher direct images vanish; it does not mean the pushforward itself vanishes. Also, on p. 85 (§13.2.1) the paper recalls "the map (t_1)_⋆𝒪_C → R(t_1)_⋆𝒪_C is a quasi-isomorphism." So the author meant R^i(t_1)_⋆𝒪^{++}_{C_ε} = 0 for i > 0 and ran together two ways of writing it. The proposed correction fits the paper's own conventions. HAL v3 has a similar slip: its PDF p. 78 (printed p. 77) reads "R^i(t_1)_⋆𝒪^{++}_{C_ε} = (t_1)_⋆𝒪_{C_ε} = 0 for all i > 0", with no ++ on the middle term. The author version added the ++ but still left the equation "= (t_1)_⋆… = 0" in place. The proof only needs the vanishing of R^i for i > 0, so the argument goes through as intended. No later result depends on the literal reading. One separate point, not part of this misprint and not assessed: Proposition 14.4.1.1(2) is stated for t_{n,1} : C_n → 𝒳_{Kli}(p), while it is applied here to C_ε → 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε). So the scope of the citation is a separate question.

sourceIssues.correction: Minimal fix: state Prop. 14.4.1.1(2) for any Klingen level p^n (n ≥ 1), for the map t_1 : C_{Σ'} → 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n)_Σ of §13.2.1, with Σ' chosen smooth, because Prop. 3.4.1 needs that and §13.2.1 does not say it. The conclusion is R(t_1)_⋆𝒪^{++}_C = (t_1)_⋆𝒪^{++}_C, i.e. R^i(t_1)_⋆𝒪^{++}_C = 0 for i > 0. The proof is word for word the same. The 𝒪-version is the "standard computation" already recalled on p. 85. The ++-version comes from the local toroidal charts (Kuga–Sato variety times a torus), Props. 3.4.1 and 3.3.1, the p-dévissage, and the factorisation of t_1 as C_{Σ'} → C_Σ → 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n)_Σ (a change of cone decomposition, then a finite map). Restricting over 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε) needs no extra work: higher direct images are local on the target and C_ε = t_1^{-1}(𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε)).

I rendered pp. 85, 88, 92 and 94 and checked the text. In §13 the correspondence depends on n. On p. 85, C|_{Y_Kli(p^n)} is 'the moduli space of (G, H_n, L) where (G, H_n) is a point of Y_Kli(p^n)', and t_1 : C_{Σ'} → 𝒳_Kli(p^n)_Σ. The proof of 13.3.1.1 uses t_1 : C_ε → 𝒳_Kli(p^n, ε) and needs R^i(t_1)_⋆𝒪^{++}_{C_ε} = 0 for i > 0.

Prop. 14.4.1.1 is stated only for t_{n,1} : C_n → 𝒳_Kli(p), the n-fold iterate of the U-correspondence at Klingen level p. §14.1 says: '𝒳_Kli(p) is the analytic Siegel threefold of Klingen level at p'. In the remark on p. 92, the author identifies C_1 with 'the correspondence C|_{Y_Kli(p)} considered in section 13.2.1', which is §13's C in the case n = 1 only.

The case n > 1 cannot be avoided. On p. 55, ε lies in [0, n − 1/(p−1)], and §13.2.2 requires w ≤ ε. A w-analytic κ may need w ≥ 1, which forces n > 1. Cor. 13.2.4.2 allows changing (n, ε, w) only among admissible triples.

As stated, 14.4.1.1 does not formally imply the level-p^n claim. On the abelian locus, C^{(p^n)} = C_1 ×_{Y_Kli(p)} Y_Kli(p^n): because H_n is cyclic, L ∩ H_n = 0 exactly when L ∩ H_n[p] = 0. But no base-change result is available for the ++ sheaves or across the toroidal boundary. So the cited proposition does not cover the step as written.

The step is nonetheless very likely true. The proof of 14.4.1.1 uses nothing specific to level p. The author also 'recall[s]' the non-++ statement (t_1)_⋆𝒪_C ≅ R(t_1)_⋆𝒪_C at level p^n on p. 85, without a reference. So this is a minor gap: the cited result is stated for a different space. The proof is affected, but the stated result is not.

Footnote 22 only addresses circularity. It does not address the level. Lemma 14.3.1(2), cited in the same sentence, is fine: it is a pointwise statement about L alone, so it transfers via (G, H_n, L) ↦ (G, H_n[p], L).

A separate, unrelated slip: the printed '(t_1)_⋆𝒪^{++}_{C_ε} = 0' should read 'R(t_1)_⋆𝒪^{++} = (t_1)_⋆𝒪^{++}, i.e. R^i = 0 for i > 0'. Defence first.
(i) For n = 1 the citation is literally correct. §14.2 (p. 92) says C_n|_{𝒴_Kli(p)} is "obtained by iterating n times the correspondence C_1|_{𝒴_Kli(p)} (which is the correspondence C|_{𝒴_Kli(p)} considered in section 13.2.1)". So the author treats the §13.2.1 correspondence as the level-p^n member of the same family.
(ii) Nothing in the proof of 14.4.1.1 (pp. 94–95) depends on the level. On the interior t_1 is finite. The boundary input is the toroidal chart computation (Prop. 3.4.1, Prop. 3.3.1) plus a finite map g. Footnote 22 points the reader to that proof.
(iii) §13.2.1 (p. 85) already "recall[s] that the map (t_1)_⋆𝒪_C → R(t_1)_⋆𝒪_C is a quasi-isomorphism" at level p^n.
So the mathematics is not in doubt.

The defence still does not make the text literally right.
- The ++-statement is stated and proved only for t_{n,1} : C_n → 𝒳_{Kli}(p). Here it is applied to the level-p^n map t_1 : C_ε → 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε), and no level-p^n ++-statement appears anywhere.
- Taking n = 1 does not cover the use. §13 needs general n: w-analytic κ needs w ≤ ε ≤ n − 1/(p−1), and §13.4 takes n, ε, w large.
- Base change from level p does not give it formally either. On the interior, C at level p^n is C_1 ×_{Y_Kli(p)} Y_Kli(p^n), because H_n is cyclic, so L ∩ H_n = 0 exactly when L ∩ H_n[p] = 0. But the content sits at the boundary, and R(t_1)_⋆𝒪^{++} does not formally commute with that finite base change.
So a reader must redo the proof at level p^n. That makes it a genuine but minor gap: a citation used beyond its stated scope, filled routinely.

Consequences. The vanishing is needed to identify RΓ(C_ε, t_1^⋆(−)^{++}) with RΓ(𝒳, (t_1)_⋆t_1^⋆(−)^{++}), so that the ++-trace can define p^3U on the ++ complexes. That gives slopes ≥ −3 in all degrees in Prop. 13.3.1.1. The degree-0 bound (slopes ≥ 0) uses a separate q-expansion argument and is unaffected. Downstream: Prop. 13.3.1.1 → Cor. 13.3.3.1 (pp. 90–91) → Cor. 14.7.1 (p. 100) and Lemma 14.8.4 (p. 102, "with equality if k ≥ 3 by corollary 13.3.3.1") → the main classicity and dimension results. The extension is routine, so no stated result is affected, and affects = the proof. Confidence is medium only because it is a judgement call whether a verbatim-transferable citation counts as a gap.

sourceIssues.correction:
Two auxiliary statements are needed, and the paper proves neither.

(a) A bounded-torsion Čech-vs-derived comparison (a version of Lemma 3.2.2) for the ++-lattice F^{κ,w,++}⊗(ω^{++})^r of the Banach sheaf F^{κ,w}⊗ω^r on X_Kli(p^n,ε). Refine the covering so that each member pulls back to X(p^n,ε) as an affinoid over which FL^+_{n,ε,w,w'} is trivialised. There F^{κ,w,++} is locally the completed direct sum of copies of O^{++} (Lemma 12.6.2.1, generic fibre, since |κ|=1 on T^0_{w'}). At Klingen level it is the Kli(Z/p^n)-invariants of its pushforward along the finite map π_3.
- Bartenwerfer's constant (Thm 3.1.1) works uniformly for completed direct sums: reduce mod p^m, commute cohomology with direct sums on qcqs spaces, then take R lim as in §3.2.
- O^{++} differs from m·O^+ by torsion killed by p.
- Taking invariants under a finite group of order N costs at most N-torsion.

(b) The ++-part of Prop. 14.4.1.1(2) for the level-p^n correspondence t_1 : C → X_Kli(p^n) of §13.2.1, together with its completed-pullback version R(t_1)_⋆t_1^*F^{κ,w,++} = (t_1)_⋆t_1^*F^{κ,w,++}. This version is what the construction of p^3U actually needs. The printed proof of 14.4.1.1(2) (toroidal charts via Prop. 3.4.1 and Prop. 3.3.1, then a finite map) goes through word for word.

This is the minimal fix. An alternative, shorter correction (move to FL_{Kli,n,ε,w} and the line bundle L^κ, then apply Thm 3.1.1) is not enough by itself. It also needs bounded torsion for R^iπ_⋆L^{κ,++} along π : FL_{Kli,n,ε,w} → X_Kli(p^n,ε), or p^3U rebuilt on RΓ(FL, L^{κ,++}). The paper states only the rational vanishing, and only at Siegel level (p. 79).

Separate misprint on p. 88: "R^i(t_1)_⋆O^{++}_{C_ε} = (t_1)_⋆O^{++}_{C_ε} = 0 for all i > 0" should read "R(t_1)_⋆O^{++}_{C_ε} = (t_1)_⋆O^{++}_{C_ε}, i.e. R^i(t_1)_⋆O^{++}_{C_ε} = 0 for i > 0". HAL v3 has "= (t_1)_⋆O_{C_ε} = 0".
sourceIssues.reason:
I checked this on page images of pp. 12–13, 88, 89 and 94 and on HAL v3 pp. 76–77. Both citations go beyond the printed statements.

(1) Lemma 3.2.2 is proved under the standing assumption on p. 12: "Let F be a locally free sheaf of O_X-modules. We assume that there exists F^+ ⊂ F a locally free sheaf of O_X^+-modules such that F = F^+ ⊗ O_X". Its statement on p. 13 needs "a finite affinoid covering of X, such that F^+|_U is trivial". Its conclusion is about F^+ and F/p^nF^+, not about a ++-lattice. On p. 89 it is applied to F^{κ,w,++} ⊗ (ω^{++})^r, where F^{κ,w} = (π_⋆O_{FL^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'}} ⊗̂ A)^{T_{w',n}} is a Banach sheaf (p. 79). That sheaf is not locally free, and it is a ++-lattice, not an O^+-lattice. The covering is chosen only so that FL_{Kli,n,ε,w} is affinoid over each U. At Klingen level, triviality on U is not established: Fil^can is only étale-local, and FL descends from X(p^n,ε) (Lemma 12.7.2.1). The proof of 3.2.2 bounds H^k(U_J, F^+) by Thm 3.1.1 applied to a finite free sheaf, so it does not literally cover this case.

(2) Prop. 14.4.1.1(2) (p. 94) says: "Let t_{n,1} : C_n → X_Kli(p). Then we have ... R(t_{n,1})_⋆O^{++}_{C_n} = (t_{n,1})_⋆O^{++}_{C_n}". Here C_n (§14.2) is the n-fold iterate of the correspondence at Klingen level p. On p. 88 it is applied to t_1 : C_ε → X_Kli(p^n,ε), the level-p^n correspondence of §13.2.1. The O-version at level p^n is "recalled" in §13.2.1, but the ++-version is nowhere stated at that level. This is the only explicit citation of 14.4.1.1 in the paper. Constructing p^3U on RΓ(F^{κ,w,++} ⊗ (ω^{++})^r) also needs the corresponding vanishing for the completed pullback t_1^*F^{κ,w,++}, which is not covered either.

Both uses go beyond the hypotheses of the cited results, and the paper gives no argument for the extensions. So this is a genuine, if minor, gap in the proof as printed, not a text-layer artefact. The fix in the correction is sound: Bartenwerfer's constant is uniform on completed direct sums, and invariants under a finite group cost bounded torsion. The proofs of §3.2 and §14.4.1 adapt without new ideas, so the statement is not in doubt.

Dependence: Prop. 13.3.1.1 (slopes ≥ −3 in all degrees) is used in the proof of the sheaf-level classicity theorem on pp. 90–91 ("This follows from proposition 13.3.1.1, proposition 13.3.3.1, and corollary 13.3.2.1"), and through it in the later classicity results. Because the gap can be filled routinely, no stated result is affected. The degree-0 claim (slopes ≥ 0) uses a separate q-expansion argument and does not depend on these citations. HAL v3 (printed pp. 76–77) has the same text: "We now deduce from lemma 3.2.2 that the map ... has kernel and co-kernel of bounded p-torsion", with the same citation of Prop. 14.4.1.1, whose statement there (p. 82) is identical. I rate confidence medium only because it is a judgement call whether a routine extension of a cited lemma counts as a gap. I checked this on page images of pp. 12–13, 76–79, 85–95 and 99, and of HAL v3 pp. 11, 76–77 and 82.

Defences I tried, and why each fails:

(1) Lemma 3.2.2 under its own hypotheses. p. 12: "Let F be a locally free sheaf of O_X-modules. We assume that there exists F^+ ⊂ F a locally free sheaf of O_X^+-modules such that F = F^+ ⊗ O_X". p. 13: "Let U be a finite affinoid covering of X, such that F^+|_U is trivial." The conclusions concern F^+ and F/p^nF^+.
- Here F^{κ,w} = (π_⋆O_{FL^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'}} ⊗̂ A)^{T_{w',n}} (p. 79) is a Banach sheaf. Locally it is a completed direct sum, not a direct sum, so it is not locally free even in the infinite-rank algebraic sense.
- The lattice used is F^{κ,w} ∩ O^{++} (p. 88), not an O^+-lattice.
- The covering is chosen only so that FL_{Kli,n,ε,w} is affinoid over each U, not so that the lattice is trivial. At Klingen level, analytic-local triviality is not even established: Fil^can is étale-local (p. 78), and FL_Kli is obtained by descent (Lemma 12.7.2.1).
- The proof of 3.2.2 bounds H^k(U_J, F^+/p^n) by Thm 3.1.1 for a finite free sheaf, so it does not literally apply. For completed sums, a uniform bound needs the R lim arguments of §3.2, because Bartenwerfer's c(X) depends on the affinoid.

(2) Is the step avoidable? No. The argument needs the cokernel of H^i(C^{•,++}) → H^i(X, F^{++}⊗…) to be bounded, so that the p^3U-stable image of H^i(X, F^{++}⊗…) in H^i(C^•)^{=a} is bounded. The kernel bound is not needed. Building p^3U directly on Čech complexes would need the same comparison on C_ε, since t_1 is not finite on the compactification.

(3) Prop. 14.4.1.1(2) under its own hypotheses. It is stated for t_{n,1} : C_n → X_Kli(p). §14.2 says that C_1 is the correspondence of §13.2.1, so the citation is literally correct only when the Klingen level is p^1. Proposition 13.3.1.1 needs level p^n with n large (w-analyticity forces w ≤ ε ≤ n − 1/(p−1)). Deducing it by base change along X_Kli(p^n) → X_Kli(p) is not automatic: the map is not known to be flat at the boundary, and this is the ++ lattice. The proof does carry over word for word, so this half is a citation stretch. The completed-pullback vanishing for t_1^*F^{κ,w,++} is also unstated.

Conclusion: the paper as printed supplies no argument, but the missing pieces follow routinely from §3.2, §3.4 and §14.4.1. So this is a genuine but minor gap, and Proposition 13.3.1.1 is not in doubt.

What uses the passage: Prop. 13.3.1.1 (slopes ≥ −3 in all degrees) is cited in the proof of Cor. 13.3.3.1 on p. 91 (the "<k−2" isomorphism in item 1). That corollary feeds Cor. 14.7.1 (p. 100) and Lemma 14.8.4 (p. 102, "with equality if k ≥ 3 by corollary 13.3.3.1"), and through them §14.8 and the main theorems. Since the gap can be filled, none of these stated results is affected. The degree-0 claim (slopes ≥ 0) uses a separate q-expansion argument and does not depend on either citation. Confidence is medium only because deciding whether an unstated routine extension counts as a gap is a judgement call. The facts about the hypotheses are certain.

review.reason: Confirmed as a gap, on both halves. (a) The printed argument on p. 89 passes from $\check H^i(C^{\bullet,++})$ to $H^i(\mathcal X_{\mathrm{Kli}}(p^n,\varepsilon),\mathcal F^{\kappa,w,++}\otimes(\omega^{++})^r)$ with `We now deduce from lemma 3.2.2 that the map … has kernel and co-kernel of bounded $p$-torsion', but Lemma 3.2.2 is stated on p. 13 for a sheaf $\mathcal F$ with $\mathcal F^+|_U$ trivial, which the Banach sheaf and its $++$-lattice are not; the refinement and the completed-direct-sum form of Bartenwerfer's bound have to be supplied, and the finite-group-invariants step costs a further bounded factor. (b) The construction of $p^3U$ on p. 88 needs the $++$ statement for $t_1$ at level $p^n$ and for $t_1^\star\mathcal F^{\kappa,w,++}$, not only for $\mathcal O^{++}$; that is E115 plus its completed-pullback version. The separate misprint is printed as reported: the chain `$R^i(t_1)_\star\mathcal O^{++}_{C_\varepsilon}=(t_1)_\star\mathcal O^{++}_{C_\varepsilon}=0$ for all $i>0$' asserts as written that $(t_1)_\star\mathcal O^{++}_{C_\varepsilon}=0$.

sourceIssues.printed:

- p. 89, §13.3.1, proof of Prop. 13.3.1.1: "embeds in the module of p-adic modular forms of weight (κ, r) tensored with ℂ (see definition 4.3 in [60])". The same page has "This is a perfect complex of ℂ_p vector spaces".
- p. 91, Prop. 13.4.1: "k ↦ dim_ℂ H^1_cusp(†, k, 2)^{=0} − dim_ℂ H^0_cusp(†, k, 2)^{=0}". The same subsection §13.4 has "Spa(Λ,Λ)×Spa(ℂ_p, O)" and "α^{-1} ∈ ℂ_p^×".
- p. 99, Cor. 14.6.2: "for all the roots a of P in ℂ, we have v(a) < 2r + k − 3".
- p. 100, §14.8: "We denote by 𝒳^{≥1}_{Kli}(p) the adic space over Spa(ℂ, O) attached to 𝔛^{≥1}_{Kli}(p)".
- p. 100, Lemma 14.8.1: "1. fRΓ(X_{Kli}(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D)) ⊗^L_{ℤ_p} ℂ ≃ fRΓ(𝒳_{Kli}(p), Ω^{(k,2)}(−D))". The proof also says "...is the adic space over Spa(ℂ, O)".
- p. 100, Rem. 14.8.1: "The ℂ-vector space H^i(...)".
Further occurrences:
- p. 101, proof of Lemma 14.8.2: "the analytic adic space over Spa(ℂ, O) attached to 𝔛*_{Kli}(p)".
- p. 101, footnote 25: "the ℂ-vector space".
- p. 102: "d_i(k) = dim_ℂ fH^i(...)" and "d_i^{†,'}(k) = dim_ℂ H^i_cusp(†,k,2)".
- p. 102, Prop. 14.9.1: "⊗_{ℤ_p} ℂ"; Cor. 14.9.1: "⊗ ℂ".

sourceIssues.correction: Throughout §§13.3.1–14.9, ℂ should be ℂ_p = Frac(O), where O is the ring of integers of ℂ_p fixed in §12.1 for all of Part III. So it should read "tensored with ℂ_p", "dim_{ℂ_p}", "roots a of P in ℂ_p" (HAL v3 has Q̄_p here), "Spa(ℂ_p, O)", "⊗^L_{ℤ_p} ℂ_p" and "ℂ_p-vector space". The statements are unchanged once ℂ is read as ℂ_p.
sourceIssues.reason:
The page images show a real inconsistency in notation; the text layer is not the cause. §12.1 (p. 73) makes Part III work over "O the ring of integers of ℂ_p", and §12.2.1, §12.9.2 and §13.4 write Spa(ℂ_p, O). The paper never defines ℂ to mean ℂ_p in Part III. Elsewhere ℂ means other things:
- the complex numbers in §5.1 (the Satake isomorphism into ℂ[X*(T)]^W, and GSp4(ℂ)) and in §15 ("Siegel threefold of level K over ℂ", "H^i(p,K_∞;…) = ℂ", and "We fix an isomorphism Q̄_p ≃ ℂ" on p. 108);
- on p. 48 (§7.4) a locally defined ℂ, "the completion of an algebraic closure of W(l)[1/p]".

Read as the complex numbers, "Spa(ℂ, O)" with O = O_{ℂ_p} is not a Huber pair. Even with §15's fixed isomorphism Q̄_p ≃ ℂ it fails, because Q̄_p is not complete and does not contain O. The GAGA-type identification in Lemma 14.8.1 and footnote 25 (the p-adic topology defined through ⊗̂_{ℤ_p} O) only make sense if ℂ = Frac(O) = ℂ_p. The mix is visible inside single passages: on p. 89 "ℂ_p vector spaces" and "tensored with ℂ" sit in the same proof, and §13.4 has "α^{-1} ∈ ℂ_p^×" followed immediately by dim_ℂ of the same ℂ_p-spaces. The correction to ℂ_p is right.

For Cor. 14.6.2, ℂ_p is also more precise than HAL v3's Q̄_p, since P has coefficients in O = O_{ℂ_p}. The author's change from Q̄_p to ℂ suggests ℂ was meant as shorthand for ℂ_p but was never declared.

Comparison with HAL v3 (6 Jan 2018):
- Prop. 13.4.1 already printed "dim_ℂ" (v3 printed p. 79).
- Cor. 14.6.2 printed "roots a of P in Q̄_p" (v3 printed p. 86).
- The degree-0 sentence of §13.3.1 has no "tensored with ℂ".
- v3's §14.8 is a different proof using ⊗ Q_p and [1/p], with no Spa(ℂ, O) and no Lemma 14.8.1.
- v3 has no §14.9.
So most of the ℂ occurrences were added in the 2019 revision.

Nothing depends on the choice beyond notation. The dimensions and Euler-characteristic arguments (Prop. 13.4.1 → Lemma 14.8.4 → Thm 14.8.1) come out the same with ℂ_p. Hence affects = nothing. For a formaliser, the only risk is confusing this ℂ with the complex numbers used in §§5 and 15.

sourceIssues.locator: §13.3.2, proof of Lemma 13.3.2.1, p. 89 (author version). HAL v3 has the same text on printed pp. 77–78.
sourceIssues.printed: There is an obvious map i : ℱℒ^+_{n,ε,w,w'} → ℱℒ^+, equivariant for the action of 𝒯_{w',n} on the left and 𝔾_m on the right (under the map 𝒯_{w',n} → 𝔾_m). Taking the −k invariants part of i^⋆ : 𝒪_{ℱℒ^+} → 𝒪_{ℱℒ^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'}} provides a map  Ω^{(k,0)} ↪ ℱ^{k,w}.
sourceIssues.correction: i : ℱℒ^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'} → ℱℒ^+
sourceIssues.reason: In this proof ℱℒ^+ → ℱℒ → 𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε) is the 𝔾_m-torsor over the Klingen-level flag variety. The very next sentence pulls back along i into 𝒪_{ℱℒ^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'}}, and ℱ^{k,w} is defined through ℱℒ^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'} (p. 79). With source ℱℒ^+_{n,ε,w,w'}, which lies over the full-level 𝒳(p^n,ε), i^⋆ would land in functions on ℱℒ^+_{n,ε,w,w'}, not on ℱℒ^+_{Kli,n,ε,w,w'}. So the source of i and the target of i^⋆ disagree, and 'Kli' was dropped. The full-level map does exist and is equivariant, so the sentence alone is not false; the slip is the inconsistency with the next line. Another fix would keep the full-level map and add a Klingen descent step, but the Kli correction matches how ℱ^{k,w} is defined.

sourceIssues.locator: §13.3.3, Proposition 13.3.3.1 (diagram, bottom horizontal arrow), p. 90; used in the proof of Corollary 13.3.3.1, pp. 90–91. HAL v3: Proposition 13.3.3.1, p. 78.
sourceIssues.printed: Proposition 13.3.3.1. — The following diagram is commutative: [top row] RΓ(𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε), 𝓕^{k,w^-} ⊗ ω^r) --U--> RΓ(𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε), 𝓕^{k,w^-} ⊗ ω^r); [both vertical arrows] d_1; [bottom row] RΓ(𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε), 𝓕^{-2-k,w^-} ⊗ ω^{k+r+1}) --p^{-k-1}U--> RΓ(𝒳_{Kli}(p^n,ε), 𝓕^{-2-k,w^-} ⊗ ω^{k+r+1}). Proof. See [3], prop. 7.2.3. (I checked the 300 dpi page image: the exponent is p^{-k-1}. HAL v3, printed p. 78 (PDF p. 79), prints the same diagram with w^+ in place of w^- and the same bottom label p^{-k-1}U.)
sourceIssues.correction: The bottom arrow should be labelled p^{k+1}U, where U is the §13.2.3 operator on 𝓕^{-2-k,w^-} ⊗ ω^{k+r+1}, normalised by p^{-(k+r+1)}. That is, d_1∘U = p^{k+1}·U∘d_1, or equivalently U∘d_1 = p^{-k-1}·d_1∘U. The printed factor p^{-k-1} is correct only with the two sides swapped. The fix is to change the sign of the exponent. Corollary 13.3.3.1 and the results built on it (Corollary 14.7.1, Lemma 14.8.4) are stated correctly and follow from the corrected diagram.
sourceIssues.reason:
I redid the computation.

(1) §13.2.3 (p. 87, checked on the image) defines U on 𝓕^{κ,w}⊗ω^{r'} for any κ and r' as (1/p^3)Tr ∘ (1/p^{r'})ξ*. Here ξ* is the transport of structure along (ξ*)^{-1}: ω_G → ω_{G_1} (Corollary 13.2.2.1: ξ*s(Fil,ρ) = s((ξ*)^{-1}Fil, (ξ*)^{-1}ρ)), tensored with the natural map on ω^{r'}. So the top row carries p^{-r} and the bottom row carries p^{-(k+r+1)}.

(2) d_1: 𝓕^{k}⊗ω^r → 𝓕^{-2-k}⊗ω^{k+r+1} is a canonical O_X-linear relative operator. It is (d/dY)^{k+1} ⊗ (det)^{k+1} in a flag coordinate Y. It is GL(ω)-equivariant by Bol's identity, (d/dz)^{k+1}((cz+d)^k f(gz)) = det(g)^{k+1}(cz+d)^{-2-k} f^{(k+1)}(gz). That identity is exactly what forces the twist ω^{+(k+1)} that the paper prints. So d_1 commutes with the unnormalised transport along any isomorphism of ω, including the rational one ξ*. It also commutes with t_i^* and with Tr.

Hence d_1∘U_top = p^{-r}·p^{k+r+1}·U_bottom∘d_1 = p^{k+1}U_bottom∘d_1.

Scalar check: for ξ* = c·Id, the top transport is c^{k+2r}p^{-r} and the bottom transport is c^{-2-k}c^{2(k+r+1)}p^{-(k+r+1)} = c^{k+2r}p^{-(k+r+1)}. Their ratio is p^{k+1}.

Coordinate check: from Lemmas 13.2.1.1 and 13.2.2.1, ξ* = diag(p,1) in the basis (HT(e_2), HT(e_4)). The flag coordinate goes Y ↦ pY and det ξ* = p. So (d/dY)^{k+1} picks up p^{k+1}, and the det normalisations cancel to 1 on both rows. Again the factor is p^{k+1}.

With the printed p^{-k-1}, the square would force (p^{k+1} - p^{-k-1})·U∘d_1 = 0, i.e. U∘d_1 = 0, so it is false as printed.

The paper's own Corollary 13.3.3.1 uses the corrected factor. Proposition 13.3.1.1 gives U slopes ≥ -3 in all degrees and ≥ 0 on H^0. So p^{k+1}U_bottom has slopes ≥ k-2 in all degrees and ≥ k+1 on H^0. Through the long exact sequence of Corollary 13.3.2.1, this gives exactly the thresholds <k-2 (isomorphisms in all degrees), <k+1 (H^0 isomorphism) and <k+1 (H^1 injective) in the corollary. With p^{-k-1}, the bound would only be slopes ≥ -k-4, and the corollary would not follow.

I classify this as a sign misprint in the exponent rather than a mathematical error: the downstream statements (Corollary 13.3.3.1, and through it Corollary 14.7.1 and Lemma 14.8.4) are correct and consistent with p^{k+1}. It still 'affects a stated result', because the displayed statement of Proposition 13.3.3.1 is false as printed. HAL v3 has the same p^{-k-1}. I tried to defend the paper and could not.

(1) Normalisations (checked on the images of pp. 86–88). By §13.2.3, U on 𝓕^{κ,w}⊗ω^{r'} is p^{-3}Tr ∘ p^{-r'}ξ^* ∘ res, where ω^{r'} = det^{r'} ω_G (§6: 'we sometimes write ω^r instead of Ω^{(0,r)}'). So the top row carries p^{-r} and the bottom row carries p^{-(k+r+1)}. By Corollary 13.2.2.1, ξ^*s(Fil,ρ) = s((ξ^*)^{-1}Fil, (ξ^*)^{-1}ρ). By Lemma 13.2.2.1, the flag HT(e_2)+αp^w HT(e_4) goes to HT(e_2)+αp^{w+1}HT(e_4). So in the basis (HT(e_2), HT(e_4)) we have ξ^* = diag(p,1), with det of valuation 1, as p. 88 uses ('ξ^*: t_2^*(ω^{++})^r → p^r t_1^*(ω^{++})^r').

(2) Computation. Write sections in a flag coordinate Y and a Gr-trivialisation t:
- top: t^{-k}P(Y)⊗E^r;
- bottom: t^{k+2}Q(Y)⊗E^{k+r+1}, with E the basis of det.

The canonical d_1 is P ↦ P^{(k+1)}. I checked by hand that this formula is invariant under diagonal changes of basis; Bol's identity covers the unipotent ones. After normalisation, transport sends P(Y) to P(pY) on the top row and Q(Y) to Q(pY) on the bottom row. The det factors p^r and p^{k+r+1} cancel exactly. Since (d/dY)^{k+1}[P(pY)] = p^{k+1}P^{(k+1)}(pY), and Tr and restriction commute with the O_X-linear d_1, we get d_1∘U_top = p^{k+1}·U_bot∘d_1. A monomial check in python agrees. So does a scalar check: for ξ^* = c·Id, both unnormalised transports are c^{k+2r}, and the normalisations differ by p^{k+1}. No normalisation in the paper produces p^{-k-1}.

(3) The printed square is false. It would force (p^{k+1} − p^{-k-1})·U∘d_1 = 0. But take a finite-slope class f that is not classical (Uf = αf with α ≠ 0 and d_1f ≠ 0). Then U(d_1f) = p^{-k-1}α·d_1f ≠ 0.

(4) The cited source does not rescue the statement; it explains where the slip came from. [3] is Andreatta–Iovita–Pilloni, Annals 2015; I read the homepage PDF. Its Prop. 7.2.3 (p. 35) prints Θ_αU_{p,i} = α(d_{g−i})^{⟨κ,α∨⟩+1}U_{p,i}Θ_α, with d_i = diag(p^{-1}1_{g−i}, 1_i) (p. 10). For g = 2 and α = t_1/t_2 this gives ΘU = p^{-(k+1)}UΘ, which is exactly Pilloni's p^{-k-1}. But [3] itself uses the other direction elsewhere:
- its §2.5 formula δ_iΘ_α = α(d_i)^{⟨κ,α∨⟩+1}Θ_αδ_i has δ on the left;
- its proof of Prop. 7.3.1 uses U_{p,g−i}Θ_α(f) = p^{k_{i+1}−k_i−1}Θ_αU_{p,g−i}(f).
Both mean ΘU = p^{k+1}UΘ, which agrees with the correction.

(5) Consequences. Proposition 13.3.3.1 is used only in the proof of Corollary 13.3.3.1. With the corrected factor, the bottom operator p^{k+1}U has slopes ≥ k−2 in every degree (Prop. 13.3.1.1 gives U slopes ≥ −3) and ≥ k+1 on H^0. The triangle of Corollary 13.3.2.1 then gives parts 1–3 with exactly the printed thresholds <k−2, <k+1 and <k+1. With the printed p^{-k-1}U, the bottom slopes are only ≥ −k−4 and nothing follows. Corollary 13.3.3.1 then feeds Corollary 14.7.1 (p. 100) and Lemma 14.8.4 (p. 102; 'equality if k ≥ 3', i.e. slope 0 < k−2), and both are right with p^{k+1}.

Classification. This is a sign misprint, not an error: the intended factor is fixed by the thresholds of Corollary 13.3.3.1, and the paper never uses the wrong sign. It is copied from the swapped formula in [3], Prop. 7.2.3. Still, the displayed Proposition 13.3.3.1 is false as printed, so affects = a stated result (the proposition itself). Nothing downstream is affected.

sourceIssues.printed: We let C(n, ϵ, w^−, k, r) = colim_{w′<w} C(n, ϵ, w, k, r).
sourceIssues.correction: C(n, ϵ, w^−, k, r) = colim_{w′<w} C(n, ϵ, w′, k, r), i.e. RΓ(X_Kli(p^n, ϵ), F^{k,w^−} ⊗ ω^r).
sourceIssues.reason: I rendered p. 90 at 110 and 300 dpi. The last argument of C inside the colimit is plainly an unprimed w, while the colimit index is w′<w. Two lines above, the paper defines F^{k,w^−} := colim_{w′<w} F^{k,w′}, with the prime in the right place. §12.8.1 (p. 79) defines C(n, ϵ, w, κ, r) := RΓ(X_Kli(p^n, ϵ), F^{κ,w} ⊗ ω^r), with transition maps for w1 ≥ w. So colim_{w′<w} C(n, ϵ, w′, k, r) is a directed colimit. On the quasi-compact space X_Kli(p^n, ϵ) it equals RΓ(F^{k,w^−} ⊗ ω^r). Corollary 13.3.2.1 then follows by applying RΓ to the exact sequence of Proposition 13.3.2.1. Read literally, the printed formula is the colimit of a constant diagram over a nonempty directed set, which is just C(n, ϵ, w, k, r). Corollary 13.3.2.1 would then become the fixed-w statement that the proof of Prop. 13.3.2.1 calls a 'minor error' in [3] ('the colimit is necessary because integration changes the radius of convergence'). So the printed line is not correct under the paper's own conventions. The meaning is unambiguous, so this is a misprint. The text layer shows the same thing ('colimw0 <w C(n, , w, k, r)'), so this is not an extraction artefact. HAL v3 (PDF p. 79, printed p. 78) has the identical line, and I checked it on the rendered image. The w^− version of C appears only in this definition and in Corollary 13.3.2.1. That corollary is used in the proof of Corollary 13.3.3.1, which is stated with F^{k,w}. With the obvious reading, nothing downstream changes, so affects = nothing.

sourceIssues.reason: Checked on the page image. Just above, C_cusp(A_l) is defined as the finite-slope part of C_cusp(n, ε, w, κ_{A_l}, 2), described as 'overconvergent cohomology of weight (κ_{A_l}, 2)'. So the second weight is 2, and no r is in play in §13.4. The paper's notation for overconvergent cuspidal cohomology is H^i_cusp(†, κ_A, r) = colim H^i(X_Kli(p^n, ε), F^{κ_A,w} ⊗ ω^r(−D)) (§12.8.1, p. 79). Prop. 13.4.1, a few lines below, correctly writes H^i_cusp(†, k, 2). The notation 'H^i_cusp(κ, r)' without † appears nowhere else in the paper. So both the missing † and the stray r are slips, and the intended meaning is clear.
